display.story_text:
Waldo Stadium turns Tuesday night into its annual Military Appreciation Game, and the Eastern Michigan vs Western Michigan spread asks a blunt question: can an Eagles offense that scored 7 points in its last outing stay within two touchdowns of the team sitting first in the MAC? Kickoff was moved up to 6:00 PM ET in Kalamazoo, and my pick is Western Michigan Broncos −14.5 with the Under 46.5.

Corwin Dahlquist has the athletic department's notes folded in his coat pocket. Three United States military veterans work on the Western Michigan football staff, from the strength room to the analytics office. "We stand for them first," Corwin says. "Then we push you around for four quarters. Politely. This is Kalamazoo."

Imogen Tremblay has a calendar instead. "Thirteen days off since Ford Field. You know what a little brother does with thirteen days? He gets mad."

Mad is not the same as productive. Eastern Michigan is 4-6, sixth in the MAC, scoring 19.9 points a game and allowing 26.6. Noah Kim took the most throws in every game through the Toledo loss on Oct. 17, and Western Michigan's own game notes say he hasn't played since. Brogan McCaughey has led the throwing in the two games after that: 197 yards in a 24-20 loss at Ohio, then 12 of 17 for 59 yards in the 35-7 loss to Central Michigan. I'm pricing McCaughey, and that price is steep against a defense allowing 18.7 a game.

Western Michigan is 7-3 and 5-1 in the conference. Jalen Buckley has 832 yards and 10 rushing touchdowns, and Broc Lowry has 12 touchdown throws against 3 interceptions. He went 15 for 15 at Akron in a 42-14 win. The Broncos have beaten Eastern three straight, 45-21, 26-18 and 31-21.

That run game is also the Under case. Six of Western Michigan's ten games finished under 46 combined points, because a team that keeps handing to Buckley keeps the clock moving. DraftKings opened Western Michigan Broncos −14.5 with a 47.5 total and has trimmed the total to 46.5 while the side holds.

The room is together on Western Michigan and split on the total. The Formula has it 31-16, takes Western Michigan Broncos −14.5 and goes Over 46.5. Next Man Up has 31-12 and likes both the Broncos and the Under 46.5. Letdown Watch sees 31-14 with Western Michigan and the Under. In The Trenches likes the Broncos at 31-19 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "Sixteen points for Eastern? McCaughey threw for 59 yards in a dome. The Formula is grading on a curve."

The Formula: "And you've got them at 12. One field goal apart, and you act like I left the porch light on for them."

My final is Western Michigan Broncos 31, Eastern Michigan Eagles 15. That margin clears the number by a point and a half, and 46 points stays half a point under. The night honors the veterans first. After that it belongs to whoever is carrying the ball for the Broncos.

Western Michigan Broncos 31, Eastern Michigan Eagles 15. Western Michigan Broncos cover the 14.5. Under 46.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Eastern Michigan Eagles vs Western Michigan Broncos prediction for Tuesday, Nov. 17: Waldo Stadium hosts its annual Military Appreciation Game, and the rivalry from the other side of the state gets a 6:00 PM ET kickoff in Kalamazoo. Corwin Dahlquist has a 7-3 Broncos team and a pocketful of thank-you notes, while Imogen Tremblay rolls in from Ypsilanti with a 4-6 Eagles team, thirteen days of rest and a chip on her shoulder roughly the size of Ann Arbor.

"Before anybody says a word about football," Corwin says, "three men on our staff served this country. Our analytics director spent more than three decades in the Army. Our head athletic trainer was deployed to Baghdad. Tuesday is theirs first."

"Agreed, and I'll clap the loudest," Imogen says. "Then I'm going to ruin your night."

Here's the funny part about this one. The Michigan MAC Trophy, the three-way prize between Western, Central and Eastern, is already staying in Kalamazoo. Central beat Eastern at Ford Field on Nov. 4, so the Broncos keep the hardware no matter what happens Tuesday.

"So we're playing for pride," Imogen says. "Pride is the only thing Eastern has ever needed. We run on it. It's cheaper than gas."

"You're playing for a bowl game," Corwin says gently. "You need to win out."

He's right, and she knows it. Eastern Michigan's season has a hinge in the middle. The Eagles opened MAC play 3-0, with a 38-14 win at UMass and a 25-23 escape at Akron, then dropped three straight to Toledo, Ohio and Central Michigan. Noah Kim, who took the most throws in every game through mid-October, hasn't played since the Toledo loss, according to Western Michigan's game notes. Brogan McCaughey has taken over, and it has been bumpy: 197 yards at Ohio in a four-point loss, then 59 yards on 12 completions against Central.

"The kid is learning in public," Imogen says. "That's the bravest thing you can do. I learned to parallel park in public."

Eastern still has a few names that make Corwin squint. Amareon Blue is listed at 5-foot-6 and leads the team with 447 rushing yards. Harold Mack has five touchdown grabs. Tight end Joshua Long has a team-high 44 catches, and Quincy Byas leads the Eagles in sacks.

"Byas is going to say hello to your quarterback," Imogen says.

"Broc Lowry has 12 touchdown throws and 3 interceptions," Corwin says. "He went 15 for 15 at Akron. He doesn't panic. He folds his laundry."

That's the Western Michigan personality in one sentence. The Broncos are 7-3, 5-1 in the conference and first in the MAC, and they win by pressing on people until they give up. Jalen Buckley has 832 yards and 10 touchdowns and needs 168 more to reach 1,000 for the third time in his career, which would put him in a club with three other Bronco backs in program history. Cole Cabana has broken an 82-yard touchdown run in each of the last two games, after running for 44 yards on 22 carries in his whole career before that.

"Eighty-two, then eighty-two again," Corwin says. "Same distance. I measured it twice. The second time I cried a little."

"You held the ball for 42 minutes against Akron," Imogen says. "Forty-two! My little brother can't hold anything for 42 minutes. He drops his phone in the soup."

The history is not on Eastern's side lately. Western Michigan leads the all-time series 37-22-2 and has won the last three, giving up 21 points or fewer in each. But Imogen has a date circled in her own heart: Oct. 22, 2022, the last time the Eagles beat the Broncos, and they did it right here in Kalamazoo.

"Waldo has been kind to green before," she says. "It can do it again."

Here's how Tuesday goes. Eastern comes out hot after almost two weeks of stewing, and Byas gets home once early to quiet the crowd for a series. Blue finds a crease or two. But Western Michigan does what it always does. Buckley carries and carries, Lowry hits Aveion Chenault on the one throw that matters, and the Broncos' defense, which allows 18.7 points a game, keeps McCaughey in third-and-long all night. Eastern gets a late score to make Imogen jump out of her seat, and the Broncos close it out with the clock.

Corwin stands for the final salute to the veterans and pours imaginary syrup over an imaginary full stack. Imogen opens a spreadsheet, finds the cell for Nov. 24 against Kent State, and colors it green in advance.

My call: Western Michigan Broncos 31, Eastern Michigan Eagles 15.

display.story_text:
Ohio has asked everybody at Peden Stadium to wear black on Tuesday night, which fits a Bobcats team still sore from blowing a 17-0 lead at Miami. My Ball State vs Ohio pick is Ohio Bobcats −11.5 plus the Over 49.5, because the MAC leader comes home to Athens looking to take that bruise out on somebody.

Penny Trautman is dressed for the theme. "Black shirt, black boots, and I tapped a brick on Court Street on the way in. We have won seventeen straight in this building. Ball State hasn't won at Peden in fifteen years."

Gus Ponder doesn't flinch. "We beat you 20-14 last year, Penny. You remember. You wore black that day too, emotionally."

That win in Muncie is real, and so is the gap between these teams now. Ohio is 7-3 and 5-1 in the conference, first in the MAC. Ball State is 3-7, giving up 34.1 points a game, and has allowed 45 or more three times. The Cardinals are also playing on a six-day turnaround after a 28-7 loss to Buffalo in the rain, where they drove inside the Buffalo 30 six times and came away empty every time.

Nick Poulos has taken the most throws in each of Ohio's last five games, with 8 touchdowns and 1 interception on the year. Riley Neer has 625 receiving yards, and Michael Molnar has 7 sacks and 94 tackles for a defense that should live in Keldric Luster's backfield. Luster has 1,618 yards, 10 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. My margin of 14 comes from that matchup: an Ohio front that gets home against a team that can't finish drives.

The Over is about Ball State's defense more than Ohio's offense. Eight of the Cardinals' ten games have gone past 49.5 combined points. TJ Horton has 9 rushing touchdowns and Donovan Hamilton caught 11 balls against Buffalo, so Ball State can chip in its share. DraftKings opened Ohio Bobcats −9.5 with a 50.5 total, and the side has climbed two points while the total slipped one.

Three of the cards line up on the same ticket. The Formula has Ohio 32-20 with Ohio Bobcats −11.5 and likes the Over 49.5. Next Man Up has 35-20 and likes both Ohio and the Over. Letdown Watch has 33-18, likes Ohio, and goes Over. In The Trenches has no score this week, sees the two fronts as even, and takes neither side nor total. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "Everybody wants a letdown after Oxford. I looked. There isn't one. Ohio comes home angry."

Next Man Up: "First time you've agreed with me all month, Letdown Watch. Bring a black shirt."

My final is Ohio Bobcats 33, Ball State Cardinals 19. That's a 14-point win, two and a half points clear of the number, and 52 points, two and a half past the total. Penny gets to tap her brick. Gus gets a long bus ride back to Indiana with a Garfield comic and his thoughts.

Ohio Bobcats 33, Ball State Cardinals 19. Ohio Bobcats cover the 11.5. Over 49.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Black is the dress code in Athens on Tuesday night, because Ohio has asked every fan at Frank Solich Field at Peden Stadium to wear it. Ball State Cardinals vs Ohio Bobcats kicks off at 7:00 PM ET, and Penny Trautman has her black boots laced while Gus Ponder shows up from Muncie in a red sweater and a grin, insisting black is just red that stayed up too late.

"Seventeen straight home wins," Penny says. "Longest run in the country. Nobody has walked out of this building happy since before some of these freshmen could ride a bike."

"Somebody has to be eighteen," Gus says. "I volunteer us. Ball State, always helping."

Penny laughs, but she's got a bruise she isn't hiding. Last Tuesday in Oxford, Ohio led Miami 17-0 midway through the second quarter and lost 34-17 in the Battle of the Bricks. The Bobcats didn't score again after building that lead.

"I've been walking the bricks on Court Street all week," she says. "Thinking. Brick by brick. You rebuild a street one stone at a time and you rebuild a season one half at a time."

"I walked to my mailbox," Gus says. "Also thinking."

Here's what Penny is thinking about. Ohio is 7-3, 5-1 in the conference, first in the MAC. Nick Poulos has thrown 8 touchdowns against 1 interception, and he ran 17 times at Miami because he refuses to go down quietly. Riley Neer has 47 catches for 625 yards and 6 touchdowns. On defense, Michael Molnar is everywhere: 94 tackles and 7 sacks, the kind of linebacker who makes the visiting quarterback check over his shoulder in the parking lot.

"Molnar is going to find Keldric Luster," Penny says. "He finds everybody. He found my car keys once."

"Keldric Luster has 1,618 yards and 10 touchdown throws," Gus says, puffing up. "And Donovan Hamilton caught 11 balls against Buffalo last week. Career high. You know who else peaked on a Wednesday?"

"Who?"

"Nobody. Garfield hates Mondays and loves lasagna, and he never once peaked on a Wednesday. Donovan did. That's growth."

The Buffalo game is where Gus has to get honest. Ball State hung with the Bulls for three quarters in the rain, tied 7-7 for most of the night, and the Cardinals drove inside the Buffalo 30 six times. Six. They came away with three missed field goals and three stopped fourth downs, and their only touchdown came on a blocked punt. Then Buffalo broke a 67-yard run late and pulled away 28-7.

"Six trips," Gus says quietly. "If we score on half of them, I'm doing this interview from a parade float."

And now the Cardinals turn around on six days' rest for their third straight midweek game. TJ Horton has 9 rushing touchdowns and ran for 92 yards on just 11 carries against Buffalo, and Sterling Smith leads the defense with 56 tackles. Gus has real football here. He also has a defense that has allowed 34.1 points a game.

"We beat you last year, though," he says. "Twenty to fourteen in Muncie. First MAC game for our coach. You were the champs."

"I remember," Penny says. "I wore black that day too."

History in this building is all Penny's. Ohio has won the last three meetings in Athens, and Ball State's last win at Peden came in 2011. The series is closer overall than she likes to admit, with Ball State ahead 16-13 coming into the 30th meeting, but the last decade has mostly been green.

Here's how Tuesday plays out. Ball State starts fast, the way it did against Buffalo, and Horton gets the Cardinals on the board early enough for Gus to stand on his chair. Then Molnar and the Ohio front settle in. Poulos hits Neer twice down the sideline, Duncan Brune grinds the middle, and the Bobcats spend the second half making Luster throw from his own end. Ball State scores late, Gus celebrates like it's a holiday, and the black-shirted crowd walks home up the hill with an eighteenth straight home win.

Penny taps a brick on the way out and grins. Gus pulls a Garfield comic out of his pocket, reads the Monday strip twice, and decides it's about him.

My call: Ohio Bobcats 33, Ball State Cardinals 19.

display.story_text:
Three of Miami's six wins this season came by three points or fewer, and that's the whole reason I'm taking the points in Kent on Tuesday night. Kent State Golden Flashes +9.5 is my Miami (OH) vs Kent State pick, paired with Over 45.5, on a Dix Stadium Senior Night when every fan gets a Gold Jacket koozie at the gate.

Ozzie Brannigan already has his koozie. He is holding it like a lost puppy. "Senior Night, a free koozie, and the RedHawks in town. Somebody's going to be crying into a gold jacket. Historically, it's us."

Cordelia Van Doren adjusts her pearls. "Historically, Ozzie, Miami owns this series by more than thirty games. I printed it. Laminated it, too."

I care more about the quarterback. Caleb Heavner took the most throws in five straight games, then left the Ohio game hurt in the second quarter, according to Miami's own notes, and freshman Drew Bellisari finished it with 99 throwing yards and a big scramble in a 34-17 comeback. Kent State is handing out Gold Jacket koozies at Dix Stadium for Senior Night, and Ozzie Brannigan has already decided his will be soaked with happy tears or sad ones by the fourth quarter. Miami (OH) RedHawks vs Kent State Golden Flashes kicks off at 7:00 PM ET Tuesday, and Cordelia Van Doren has driven up from Oxford with a bowl-eligible team, a cardigan in Miami red and a laminated history sheet she refuses to put away.

"A koozie," Ozzie says, turning it over in his hands. "They're giving us something to hold onto. That's how you know it's going to be a long night."

"It's a thoughtful gesture," Cordelia says. "Gold jackets for the Golden Flashes. Very on brand. I'll take two."

Senior Night in Kent has a soft spot in it no matter the season. The Golden Flashes are 3-7 and ninth in the MAC, and the seniors walking out of the tunnel have been through more than their share of long Saturdays. Ozzie knows every one of them by number, and he'll stand and clap for all of them.

"These guys showed up every week," he says. "Nobody showed up for them some weeks. They still showed up."

Cordelia doesn't argue. Then she pulls out the sheet.

"Seventy-second meeting," she says. "Miami leads it 53-18. We're 24-11 in this very stadium. And a win tonight gives Chuck Martin a winning record at Miami. He's 78-78. I've been waiting all season to say seventy-nine."

"I've been waiting all season for anything," Ozzie says.

Here's the thing Cordelia has to be careful about, and she knows it. Miami's quarterback room got shaken up last Tuesday. Caleb Heavner left the Ohio game hurt in the second quarter with the RedHawks down 17-0, and freshman Drew Bellisari came in and helped lead the biggest comeback Miami had pulled off in twelve years. He threw for 99 yards and scrambled for 64 more, including a fourth-and-9 run from the Ohio 32 down to the 1.

"Drew Bellisari," Cordelia says, like she's announcing a debutante. "Remember the name. I'll quiz you later."

"I don't know who's playing quarterback for you Tuesday," Ozzie says. "Neither do you."

"Neither of us does," she admits. "Which is exactly why D'Shawntae Jones matters. Two straight games over a hundred yards. A career-long 48-yard touchdown run against Ohio. And Roosevelt Andrews III has 6.5 sacks, so your quarterback should learn to throw fast."

Ozzie's quarterback has been learning to throw fast all year. Dru DeShields has 1,961 yards and 11 touchdown throws, and he runs the whole show because the Kent ground game hasn't been much help. At Bowling Green last week, DeShields threw for 332 yards and ran in two touchdowns, and Wayne Harris caught 8 balls for 143 yards and 2 scores. The Flashes still lost 33-28.

"Wayne Harris is the best thing about my week," Ozzie says. "817 yards. I'm not excited. I'm just saying it out loud so I can hear it."

"That's excitement, Ozzie."

"It's a cry for help."

The thing that gives Ozzie a sliver of hope is that Miami doesn't blow people out. The RedHawks beat UConn by three, UMass by one and Central Michigan by one. They also lost to Bowling Green by four and Buffalo by three. Close games are Miami's natural habitat, and close games can tip over.

"Twenty twenty-one," Ozzie whispers. "Forty-eight to forty-seven. The last time we beat you."

"Five years ago," Cordelia says. "I know. I keep a separate sheet for that one. It's in a drawer."

Here's how it goes. Kent comes out of the tunnel on a wave of senior emotion, and DeShields finds Harris deep early to send the Dix Stadium crowd into a frenzy. Miami steadies itself the way Chuck Martin teams always do. Jones grinds out the middle, Andrews gets home twice, and Miami pulls ahead in the third quarter. Kent keeps answering, DeShields keeps slinging, and the Flashes make it a game into the fourth before Miami runs the clock out and earns Martin his seventy-ninth win in Oxford colors.

Cordelia adds a gold sticker to her Cradle of Coaches chart and allows herself one small clap. Ozzie lifts his Gold Jacket koozie toward the seniors on the field, sighs, and says what he always says. "I expected this."

My call: Miami (OH) RedHawks 29, Kent State Golden Flashes 20.

Every one of Akron's ten games this season has finished with more than 46.5 points, and that one fact is half my card for Wednesday night in Amherst. So the Akron vs UMass pick is Massachusetts Minutemen −3 to go with Over 46.5, on Senior Night and Fan Appreciation night at McGuirk Alumni Stadium.

Abner Kettleworth wants to talk about the first meeting. "Our first win as an FBS program came against Akron. Four interceptions. I still have the ticket stub in a jar with my sourdough starter."

Hollister "Zip" Grubbs wants to talk about last year. "Forty-four to ten, Abner. We sent you home flatter than a blimp with a hole in it."

Both are true, and neither tells me much about this Wednesday. The present does. Akron is 1-9, 0-6 in the MAC and 12th in the conference, allowing 33.2 points a game. The Zips' only win came against Robert Morris in September. UMass is 5-5 and allows 22.3. On a neutral reading this is a mismatch, and three points is a small ask.

The catch is the UMass quarterback. William Watson III has completed 115 of 167 throws with 9 touchdowns and 2 interceptions, but the UMass game notes say he missed the Miami (OH) and Buffalo games and most of the Toledo game with lower body injuries. Logan Inagawa took the most throws at Toledo and went 10 for 27 in a 24-0 loss. I don't know who starts Wednesday, so I'm pricing Inagawa. Even at that price, UMass is the better team against a defense this soft, and Curtis Kimmons IV and T.Y. Harding give the Minutemen plays that don't need a quarterback to be perfect.

Akron changed quarterbacks too. Cibastian Broughton took over for the last two games and threw 2 touchdowns against Western Michigan, both to Marcel Williams. Jordan Gant has 791 rushing yards. That's enough to put points on the board, and that is the Over case. Akron games have landed at 48 or more combined points all year, every single time. DraftKings opened Massachusetts Minutemen −3.5 with a 47.5 total, and both have come down a little.

The room is almost unanimous. The Formula has UMass 29-21 and likes both Massachusetts Minutemen −3 and the Over 46.5. Next Man Up has 31-17, likes UMass, and goes Over. Letdown Watch has 30-18, likes UMass, and goes Over. In The Trenches projects UMass 34-20 and still likes Akron Zips +3, with no over/under call. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

The Formula: "In The Trenches has UMass by fourteen and takes Akron. That's like ordering a lobster roll and asking them to hold the lobster."

In The Trenches: "Better than the Cover Writer, who still thinks a 1-9 team can't hang around for three quarters."

display.fanatic_story:
The first time UMass ever won a football game as an FBS program, the visitors were from Akron. That was Nov. 10, 2012, a 22-14 night with four Minutemen interceptions, and Abner Kettleworth has carried it around for fourteen years like a smooth stone in his coat pocket, ready for the night Akron Zips vs Massachusetts Minutemen came back to McGuirk Alumni Stadium.

That night is Wednesday at 7:00 PM ET. It's also Senior Night and Fan Appreciation night in Amherst, and Hollister "Zip" Grubbs has driven in from Ohio with a 1-9 team and the unshakable belief that rubber always comes back to its shape.

"Fourteen years," Hollister says. "Abner, that's a long time to hold a grudge against a tire company's hometown."

"It's not a grudge," Abner says, very slowly, the way people in the Pioneer Valley say everything. "It's a keepsake. Grudges are heavy. Keepsakes are light. Isaiah Rodgers took one back for six that night. I like to think about it when the leaves fall."

"Well, think about last year too," Hollister says. "Forty-four to ten. In Akron."

Abner looks out over the hills for a moment. "I think about that one when the leaves are already on the ground."

This is the seventh meeting, and Akron leads the series 4-2. But this season doesn't look anything like last season. UMass is 5-5, with a defense that ranks third in the MAC in yards allowed and an offense that has had to find answers at quarterback. William Watson III leads the MAC in completion rate, hitting 115 of 167, but the UMass notes say he missed the Miami (OH) and Buffalo games and most of the Toledo game with lower body injuries. Abner doesn't pretend to know who takes the first snap Wednesday.

"Whoever it is," he says, "he has T.Y. Harding. Harding has scored on a catch, a run and a punt return this year. Only two players in the whole country can say that. The other one plays in Boca Raton and has never had a proper Amherst apple."

Akron's year has been a long one. The Zips beat Robert Morris 45-10 in September and haven't won since, and they're 0-6 in conference play. Hollister knows it. He just refuses to let it shrink him.

"Jordan Gant has 791 rushing yards," he says. "Donelius Johnson has 89 tackles. And Cibastian Broughton threw 2 touchdowns to Marcel Williams against Western Michigan last week. We've found something. It's small. A blimp starts small too, before you fill it up."

"A blimp starts as a large bag," Abner says.

"A large bag full of hope."

There's one thing about Akron Abner can't shake, and it has nothing to do with the record. Akron games light up the scoreboard. Every one of the Zips' ten games has seen at least 48 points combined. They give up plenty, and lately they've scored some too.

"So we'll need points," Abner says. "Derek Morris has made four field goals from fifty yards or more this season. Only seven kickers in the country can say that. We don't need touchdowns every trip. We need patience and a strong left leg."

"Is it his left leg?"

"I have no idea. It's a figure of speech in the Valley."

UMass also does the little things. The Minutemen lead the MAC with a plus-0.40 turnover margin, they've thrown only four interceptions all year, and Edward Phillipson is booming punts 45.6 yards a kick, best in the conference. Abner calls it "colonial football." Hollister calls it boring and then admits it works.

Here's how Wednesday goes. The seniors walk out with their families, Abner rings his little colonial bell, and the Minutemen start fast with Harding getting loose on an early touch. Akron answers with Gant and a Broughton strike to Williams, because these Zips can make a game of it for a half. Then the UMass defense settles in, Johnson piles up tackles on the other side trying to keep Akron close, and Morris drops a long one through the uprights in the third quarter to make the crowd roar. Kimmons grinds out the fourth quarter on the ground, and the Minutemen send their seniors off with a win.

Hollister bounces on his heels at the final whistle anyway. "Tread's still good," he says. Abner walks him to the parking lot, hands him a bag of Amherst apples for the drive, and plants a small tree in his own honor, just in case.

My call: Massachusetts Minutemen 31, Akron Zips 19.

Kendra Woolcott is wearing shorts. It is November in Western New York. "Hundreds of pounds of meat, Brynn. Roasts. Steaks. And Messiah Burch running through your defense like he's late for the drawing."

Brynn Haverkamp zips her parka all the way up. "Ope, you're going to freeze. We beat you 38-19 last year, and I brought a thermos."

That's the honest starting point. Buffalo is 7-3, 5-1 in the MAC and first in the conference, but its points for and against are almost even at 24.3 and 24.1 a game, and a lot of its wins were tight. Two of the last four came in overtime. Central Michigan is 5-5, has won two in a row, 35-7 and 28-7, and allows 22.1 a game. Two and a half points is a fair fight.

I side with Buffalo because of what it does when the offense gets going. The Bulls haven't lost a game this season when they score 21 or more, and they're 7-0 in those games. Burch is the reason they get there. He has 1,110 rushing yards, and he ran 31 times for 209 yards and 2 touchdowns at Ball State last week. Chance Morrow has 9 touchdown catches, and Jason Wright has 10 touchdown throws. Central Michigan has split quarterback duties between Jadyn Glasser and Angel Flores, with Flores also the team's leading rusher at 618 yards. That's a run-first offense, and Buffalo just ran for more than three hundred yards of its own at Ball State.

The Over is about history between these two. Central Michigan Chippewas vs Buffalo Bulls is the MACtion Meat Raffle game at Broadview Stadium, the Bulls' home finale with a 7:30 PM ET kickoff, and Brynn Haverkamp has come east from Mount Pleasant in a parka, wool socks and the calm of a woman who has survived a lot of deer camps.

"Ope," Brynn says. "Sorry. I just can't stop looking at your knees. It's November."

"My knees are fine. My knees are from Cheektowaga."

Let's be clear about the stakes, because there are real ones. Buffalo is 7-3 and 5-1 in the MAC, first in the conference, and the Bulls have won five in a row. One more would be six straight, their longest run since 2013. Central Michigan is 5-5 and just found its legs, beating Eastern Michigan 35-7 at Ford Field and Sacramento State 28-7 at home.

"We're rolling, Kendra," Brynn says. "Two straight, and the defense is mean again. Mayson Hitchens has 72 tackles and he's still hungry."

"Everybody's hungry tonight. That's the whole promotion."

The Bulls have a back who could win the raffle by himself. Messiah Burch has 1,110 rushing yards and leads the MAC at 111 a game. At Ball State last week he ran 31 times for 209 yards and two touchdowns, the most by a Buffalo back since Jaret Patterson's 409-yard day in 2020. Here's the wild part: Burch ran for 294 yards in the first 22 games of his career combined.

"Two hundred and nine," Kendra says. "He did that in the rain. You should see him in the snow. Actually, you might."

Chance Morrow is the other problem for Central. He has 54 catches, 693 yards and nine touchdowns, all of them in the end zone, which sounds obvious until you realize the Buffalo notes made a point of it. Tight end Clint Walker is one touchdown catch from tying the school record for a tight end in a season. And Oliver Hautanen has made 15 field goals, the most in the conference.

"We don't need touchdowns every time," Kendra says. "We need three points and a ribeye."

Brynn has an answer, and it's the ground game. Central Michigan's leading rusher is quarterback Angel Flores with 618 yards, and Nick Woodford ran 23 times for 119 against Sacramento State. Jadyn Glasser has taken most of the throws in the last three games and keeps it clean, with just 3 interceptions on the year. Langston Lewis is the deep threat.

"We move the chains, we keep your Burch on the bench, and your fans eat their raffle prizes cold," Brynn says. "Also, we won 38-19 last year. In Mount Pleasant. I made s'mores."

"In your building," Kendra says. "Over the last four meetings, both teams won both of their home games. This is our building now. It even has a new name."

It does. The old UB Stadium is Broadview Stadium now, and Kendra has been practicing the new name in the mirror. Central Michigan leads the all-time series 9-4, which Brynn mentions twice and then a third time for good measure.

Here's how Wednesday goes. Central comes out running, and Flores breaks one around the outside to give the Chippewas an early lead and Brynn a reason to rev her imaginary snowmobile. Buffalo answers the way it always does, with Burch between the tackles, carry after carry, until the Central defense starts to sag. Morrow catches a touchdown in the end zone, naturally, and Hautanen adds a long field goal. Central keeps it close into the fourth quarter, Glasser hits Lewis to make the last few minutes tense, and Burch runs out the clock on a night that ends with six in a row and a lot of Buffalo freezers a little fuller.

Kendra celebrates in shorts, arms up, steam rising. Brynn crawls into the little tent she set up by the parking lot, zips it shut, and tells everybody she's at deer camp until Saturday.

My call: Buffalo Bulls 24, Central Michigan Chippewas 20.

display.fanatic_story:
It's Owls against Owls on Thursday night at Lincoln Financial Field, and Temple has made it Fan Appreciation Night, which Teddy Fiorella has decided means the whole stadium should appreciate him personally. Rice Owls vs Temple Owls kicks off at 7:30 PM ET in South Philadelphia, and Odalys Chen-Moreau has flown up from Houston with a 1-9 team, a stack of note cards and a firm belief that the smarter Owl wins the night.

"Same mascot," Teddy says. "Different birds. Ours has a South Philly accent. Yours does homework."

"Ours finished its homework," Odalys says. "Yours is still looking for a pencil."

Two teams with rough seasons, sure. Temple is 2-8 and Rice is 1-9. But Teddy has never once in his life let a record keep him quiet, and Odalys has never met a bad season she couldn't break down into smaller, more manageable bad pieces.

"Fan Appreciation Night," Teddy says, throwing his arms wide like he's conducting an orchestra. "This is for the people who came to every game. In the cold. In September. In the rain on a Tuesday if they asked. We appreciate you. I appreciate you. I would run up the Art Museum steps for every single one of you."

"Would you, though?"

"In my heart I'm running them right now."

The Temple case is about having more ways to move the ball. Ajani Sheppard has thrown for 1,330 yards with 9 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions. Keveun Mason has 653 rushing yards, and Colin Chase leads the receivers at 395. And then there's Curly Ordonez, who has 100 tackles and 3 sacks and plays linebacker like he's late for a train on Broad Street.

"Curly is the best thing in this city that isn't on a roll," Teddy says.

Odalys counters with the close calls, and there are a lot of them. Rice lost to UTSA by two, to Florida Atlantic by two in a 51-49 track meet, to Western Michigan by seven, and to Tulane by three last week. These Owls have been right there.

"It's a small sample," she says. "But it's a consistent small sample. Statistically, we're due. Spiritually, we're overdue. Emotionally, I'd like a hug."

Rice's quarterback story changed halfway through the season. Jacurri Brown took the most throws for the first seven games and ran for 691 yards, more than anyone on the team. Then Gael Ochoa took over, and against Tulane he ran 17 times for 82 yards. Ochoa is a runner who throws when he has to. AJ Brown leads the Rice defense with 66 tackles from safety, and Chibby Nwajuaku gets after the quarterback.

"If the Marching Owl Band were here, they'd have a whole halftime bit about two kinds of owls," Odalys adds. "With instruments. Mostly instruments. Possibly a couch."

"There's no couch in a marching band."

"There is in ours. Don't ask questions you can't handle."

Here's what neither one wants to admit: the defenses in this game give up a lot of points. Temple allows 29.1 a game. Rice allows 32.6. Temple scored 48 at Toledo and lost in overtime, and put up 35 at Navy. Rice put up 49 at Florida Atlantic. When these offenses get rolling, the scoreboard operator earns his paycheck.

"So it's a shootout," Teddy says.

"It's a high-variance outcome," Odalys says. "Which is a shootout for people with library cards."

Here's how Thursday goes. Rice comes out with Ochoa running the ball outside, and the visiting Owls jump ahead early while Odalys flips through her note cards at top speed. Temple answers with Sheppard finding Chase down the sideline, and Mason starts grinding the middle. The teams trade scores into the third quarter, both defenses bending, neither breaking all the way. Then Ordonez makes the play of the night, a fourth-quarter stop in the backfield, and Sheppard leads one more drive to put Temple up by more than a score. Rice gets one back late, Odalys stands on her seat, and Temple runs out the clock in front of the fans it came to thank.

Teddy jogs up the Linc's steps two at a time, pretends they're the Art Museum's, and throws both fists in the air at the top. Odalys packs her note cards, mutters that the sample size is still too small to panic, and panics quietly all the way to the airport.

My call: Temple Owls 29, Rice Owls 24.

Twyla Hemmingsen is giving the forecast before anyone asks. "Clear skies over Aiden Flora with a strong chance of two hundred rushing yards. He ran for 216 against Cincinnati last week. Bring a jacket, Knox. The wind is coming from Ames."

Knox Brevard-Stiles has his arms up like he's at the top of the big drop. "Keep your hands inside the stadium, Twyla. This place bounces. It's the last home game for our seniors, and the Bounce House has a height requirement."

Here's the case for the Cyclones. Flora has 1,335 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns, and Iowa State has won two of its last three, scoring 51, 31 and 41. Jaylen Raynor has 13 touchdown throws against 6 interceptions. The Cyclones also beat UCF the last time these two met, 38-35 in 2024.

UCF is 5-5 and has had two different quarterback stretches. Keyone Jenkins took most of the throws from mid-September through the Baylor game, and Alonza Barnett III has led the last two, throwing for 257 yards against Arizona State. Josh Derry caught 7 balls for 137 in that game and has 708 yards on the year. That's a good receiver on a team that lost by 13 at home last week. The Knights do play well here, at 4-2 in this building, which is why I have them winning by a point and not losing.

So the score is UCF Knights 28, Iowa State Cyclones 27. One point. The Cyclones take the points and still have a point and a half to spare.

The Over comes from Iowa State's recent games. The last three finished 51-49, 42-31 and 41-13, all past this total, and the 2024 meeting landed on 73. UCF allows 26.0 points a game and Iowa State allows 27.3. DraftKings opened UCF Knights −1.5 with a 54.5 total, and the market has nudged the side a point toward UCF and taken a point off the total. I'll still take the Over.

Every handicapper with a side is on Iowa State. The Formula has it 27-27, likes Iowa State Cyclones +2.5 and goes Over 53.5. Next Man Up has UCF 29-27, takes Iowa State and the Over. Letdown Watch has Iowa State winning 29-24, likes the Cyclones and goes Under. In The Trenches has UCF 30-23, likes Iowa State anyway, and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Letdown Watch: "You all have UCF winning and you're still taking Iowa State. I'm the only one with the guts to say the Cyclones win outright."

The Formula: "And the only one taking the Under in a game where both teams score more than 28 a game, Letdown Watch. Guts are not the same as sense."

My final has the Knights by a point on Senior Knight, with 55 combined points, a point and a half over the total. Knox gets his win. Twyla gets her points and a forecast that verified.

display.fanatic_story:
Iowa State has been to Orlando one time in its football life, for the 2024 Pop-Tarts Bowl, and Twyla Hemmingsen still talks about that 42-41 win over Miami like it was a weather event she personally predicted. Iowa State Cyclones vs UCF Knights on Friday is the Cyclones' first visit to the Acrisure Bounce House, a 6:00 PM ET kickoff on UCF's Senior Knight, and Knox Brevard-Stiles is waiting at the gate to tell her this ride is a lot bumpier than a bowl game.

"Clear skies, light breeze, chance of Cyclones," Twyla says. "I checked the radar on the plane."

"Keep your hands and feet inside the stadium at all times," Knox says. "This is the last home game for our seniors. The building is going to shake. That's not a figure of speech. It's literally called the Bounce House."

Senior Knight is a big one for Knox, and for good reason. UCF is 5-5, and a win at home sends the seniors out on a high and gets the Knights to six. The Bounce House has been kind this year, with four wins in six home games, including a double-overtime thriller over BYU at homecoming.

"Thirty-nine to thirty-one in two overtimes," Knox says. "My heart did a loop-the-loop. I had to sit down on a bench by the lake for an hour."

"We had a thriller too," Twyla says. "Fifty-one to forty-nine over Oklahoma State on Halloween. I forecast every point. That's not true. I forecast about half the points. The rest were a surprise front."

Here's the thing about Iowa State right now: it's running people over. Aiden Flora has 1,335 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns, and last week against Cincinnati he carried 28 times for 216 yards and three scores in a 41-13 win. Jaylen Raynor has thrown 13 touchdowns and keeps the defense honest.

"Flora is a high-pressure system," Twyla says. "He builds slowly over the first quarter and then he's a storm warning."

"Josh Derry is a whole roller coaster by himself," Knox says. "Seven catches, 137 yards against Arizona State. 708 on the year. He's the first big drop. You think you're ready. You're not."

UCF's quarterback situation has had more than one loop of its own. Keyone Jenkins led the throwing from mid-September through Halloween week, including a 293-yard night in the BYU win, and Alonza Barnett III has taken over for the last two games. Barnett threw for 257 yards against Arizona State last week, but the Knights still lost 26-13. Duke Watson leads the ground game with 596 yards, and Tackett Curtis leads the defense with 67 tackles.

"We need that Kansas magic again," Knox says. "Thirty-three to thirty-two in Lawrence. One point. I screamed so loud on the drive home the GPS rerouted me."

"One-point games," Twyla says. "I don't love them. They're like hail. You hear them before you see them."

The last time these two met, in 2024, Iowa State won 38-35. Twyla mentions this every few minutes like a weather alert scrolling across the bottom of a screen.

"That was in Ames," Knox says. "Ames doesn't have a Bounce House."

"Ames has wind."

"Orlando has thrill rides. We win the vibes."

Both teams score plenty, and both give up plenty. Iowa State's last three games all turned into points festivals: 51-49, 42-31 and 41-13. UCF allows 26 points a game. Nobody in this one is going to win with a field goal and a prayer.

Here's how Friday goes. Senior Knight starts with the ceremony, and the Bounce House shakes on the opening kickoff, just as advertised. Iowa State answers right away with Flora, first a long run, then another, until the Knights start crowding the box. UCF punches back with Barnett to Derry over the top. It goes back and forth all night, a real rollercoaster for Knox and a shifting forecast for Twyla, and the fourth quarter starts with a one-score game. display.fanatic_story:
If you work on Duke's campus, leave early on Friday, because Duke University Road shuts down to the public as kickoff approaches and the university has warned of heavy traffic starting four hours before the game. Clemson Tigers vs Duke Blue Devils kicks off at 7:30 PM ET at Brooks Field at Wallace Wade Stadium, and Harrison Wexley-Moore IV plans to stroll past the gridlock with a pocket square while Dixie-Lynn Pruitt rolls up from the Upstate in an orange convertible that has opinions about Durham parking.

"Students in the Blue Zone have to move their cars by 4:30," Harrison says. "I read the memo. Twice. I annotated it."

"Of course you did," Dixie-Lynn says. "I brought a cooler and a folding chair and the patience of a woman who has sat through a lot of Death Valley traffic. Durham doesn't scare me."

Harrison straightens his tie. He has reason to feel good. Duke is 7-3, and the Blue Devils have been punishing people at home and away. They beat Boston College 47-2 and then went to Raleigh and beat NC State 41-3 the next week. The defense gives up 15.3 points a game, the kind of figure Harrison likes to say slowly so everybody can enjoy it.

"And last year," he says. "Forty-six to forty-five. In Clemson. On your grass."

Dixie-Lynn takes a long breath. "You were going to bring that up eventually."

"Eventually was ninety seconds ago."

There's no getting around it: that one stung in the Upstate, and Dixie-Lynn has been stewing on it for a full year. But her bigger worry is right now. Clemson is 6-4, and last week the Tigers lost 20-6 at home to Georgia Tech. Christopher Vizzina took most of the throws in that game after Tait Reynolds handled the job from mid-September through the win at Syracuse. Six points at home, in November, with the whole orange crowd watching.

"I put on more orange," Dixie-Lynn says. "For strength. It didn't help. So I'm wearing more tonight."

"How much more orange can a person wear?"

"Watch me."

Clemson still has a defense worth respecting. Will Heldt has 7 sacks off the end, and Corey Myrick leads the team with 77 tackles from safety. Gideon Davidson runs hard, with 528 yards and 5 touchdowns, and Bryant Wesco Jr. has 47 catches. The Tigers won at Florida State 36-24 on Halloween, and that version of Clemson could show up anywhere.

"That's my team," Dixie-Lynn says. "The one from Tallahassee. If she shows up in Durham, you're in trouble."

"She'll be stuck on Duke University Road," Harrison says. "It's closed."

The trouble for Clemson is Nate Sheppard. Duke's running back has 1,320 rushing yards and 19 touchdowns, and he's the face on the university's own traffic alert, celebrating a score against Boston College. Last week at Miami he ran for 131 yards and caught 12 balls, which is the kind of night that makes defensive coordinators stare at the ceiling. Walker Eget has thrown for 2,044 yards with 11 touchdowns and just 4 interceptions, and Kevin O'Connor leads the defense with 4.5 sacks.

"Sheppard isn't just a running back," Harrison says. "He's a logistics problem. Like the traffic. You can't route around him."

"Will Heldt is going to route right through your blockers, Harrison."

"Our blockers have perfect grades in footwork, Dixie-Lynn. Figuratively. Also possibly literally. I haven't checked."

Here's how Friday goes. The traffic eases once the game starts, just like the memo promised, and Clemson comes out swinging with Davidson running hard and Heldt making an early sack to send the orange section into a frenzy. Then Duke settles in. Sheppard breaks one in the second quarter, then another, and Eget keeps the chains moving without taking risks. The Blue Devils' defense does what it has done all year, swarming every Clemson throw, and the Tigers have to scratch out field goals. Clemson gets a late touchdown to give Dixie-Lynn something to wave her pompoms about, but Duke wins comfortably and walks out into a quiet, traffic-free night.

Harrison lists every Duke accomplishment of the evening in alphabetical order, starting with "awareness, situational." Dixie-Lynn adds one more orange scarf for the drive home and says the Upstate will remember this.

My call: Duke Blue Devils 28, Clemson Tigers 15.

Bradley is real trouble. He has 14 sacks, and Toledo's front has to account for him on every snap. But the rest of the matchup tilts hard toward the home team. Adjatay Dabbs has 736 receiving yards, CJ Miller has 827 on the ground, and Andrew Zock has 11.5 sacks of his own. The Rockets shut out UMass 24-0 last week.

Bowling Green is 3-7, scoring 19.3 and allowing 28.9. The Falcons also changed quarterbacks: Jay Kastantin took the most throws in the first nine games, and Austin Novosad led the 33-28 win over Kent State with 229 yards and 3 touchdowns. I'm pricing Novosad, a quarterback with one game of tape against a defense that just pitched a shutout.

display.fanatic_story:
Toledo's women's cross country team just became the first MAC school to win the NCAA Great Lakes Regional, the men won it too, and the volleyball team claimed its first MAC regular-season title, so the Rockets are hosting Bowling Green Falcons vs Toledo Rockets on Friday with a campus that has forgotten how to lose. Kickoff for the Battle of I-75, presented by Fremont Federal Credit Union, is 7:30 PM ET, and it is the last game of 2026 at the Glass Bowl.

Rocco Szczepanski has the Toledo flag zip-tied to his car antenna and the Klinger dress in a garment bag "for emergencies only." Darcy Fenwick drove up from Bowling Green in her old club goalie jersey, because she says football fans in her town learned how to yell at a hockey rink first.

"Every team on your campus is winning something," Darcy says. "It's exhausting. Do you people ever lose?"

"Twice this year," Rocco says. "We don't talk about it. We talk about four in a row and first place."

He's right about the run. Toledo is 8-2, 5-1 in the MAC, and tied for first with two weeks left in the race to Detroit. The Rockets beat Eastern Michigan, Western Michigan 45-38, Sacramento State 20-17, and then shut out UMass 24-0 last week. John Alan Richter has 2,501 throwing yards, 19 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions. Back in September he threw for 429 yards in a 49-48 overtime win over Temple, and Rocco still has the replay saved on his phone.

"You've shown me that clip eleven times," Darcy says.

"Twelve. You blinked during one."

Darcy has her own clips. Bowling Green won this game the last two years, 41-26 in Toledo and 28-23 at home, and by the Falcons' count the whole series sits at 43 wins apiece with 4 ties. Ninety meetings, dead even. That's the kind of thing a rink rat holds onto.

"Dead even," she says. "Forever. You can't win the rivalry, Rocco. Nobody can."

"I can win Friday."

That's the harder argument for Darcy. Bowling Green is 3-7 and has scored 19.3 points a game. Jay Kastantin took the snaps for most of the year, and then Austin Novosad stepped in against Kent State and threw for 229 yards and 3 touchdowns in a 33-28 win. Nakai Amachree ran for 110 yards and caught 3 balls for 87 more in that game. Darcy calls that one a power play goal, unexpected and gorgeous.

"Novosad's got some juice," she says. "And we've got Myles Bradley."

Bradley is the one player Rocco doesn't joke about. The Bowling Green end has 14 sacks, and Dorian Pringle has made 96 tackles behind him. If Bradley spends the night in Richter's backfield, this gets loud and strange fast.

"Bradley's a problem," Rocco says, and for once his voice is quiet. "Zock is a problem too, though. Ours. Toledo builds engines, Darcy. Miller is four hundred horsepower in shoulder pads."

Andrew Zock has 11.5 sacks for Toledo, and the Rockets have weapons all over the field. CJ Miller has 827 rushing yards. Adjatay Dabbs has 736 receiving yards and caught 7 balls for 144 against UMass. Julian Fox leads the defense with 81 tackles.

Here's how it goes. Bowling Green plays like it knows the series history, and Novosad hits an early deep ball to make it a game. Bradley gets home once, maybe twice, and the Falcons' section behind the bench goes nuts. Then Toledo takes over. Miller grinds down the clock, Richter finds Dabbs on two big gains, and the Rockets break it open late in the third quarter. Zock spends the fourth quarter making Novosad's life hard. The Falcons grab a late touchdown, but the Glass Bowl gets a happy goodbye for 2026.

Rocco waves the flag off his antenna in the parking lot. Darcy sends herself to the penalty box for two minutes of silence, which somehow lasts the whole drive home down I-75.

My call: Toledo Rockets 35, Bowling Green Falcons 16.

display.fanatic_story:
Somewhere around 7:50 on Friday night, fireworks will go up behind the Capitol dome in downtown Lansing, the state Christmas tree will already be glowing, and about ten minutes later Oregon Ducks vs Michigan State Spartans kicks off at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing. Silver Bells in the City and Senior Night on the same Friday. Shay Kowalczyk calls it the best doubleheader in mid-Michigan, and she plans to catch the Electric Light Parade at 6 and then sprint to her seat.

"You can't do both," Nix Wyatt-Aldana says. Nix flew in from Eugene with three jackets, all of them green and yellow in slightly different shades, and is already planning the outfit change between the parade and the game.

"Watch me, eh," Shay says. "I've got a cousin with a car and a parking spot near Grand River. Strike one on your doubt."

Nix is arriving with a lot of swagger about the Ducks, and that's fair. Oregon is 7-3, No. 16 in the country, and coming off its two best performances of the year. The Ducks went to Columbus and beat Ohio State 41-28, then came home and beat Michigan 31-7. Dylan Raiola threw for 341 yards and 4 touchdowns against the Wolverines, and Jeremiah McClellan caught 4 balls for 105 yards and a score.

"That game was a full collection," Nix says. "The uniforms were perfect, the route trees were perfect, the defense was perfect. Ten out of ten."

"Uh-huh. You want to talk about the UCLA game?"

Nix does not want to talk about the UCLA game. Oregon lost that one 17-15 at home, and the Ducks also scraped past Nebraska 17-14 and lost 21-10 at Illinois. When Oregon is off, it looks like a runway show where somebody tripped on the stairs, and Nix has a whole speech about it that nobody asked for.

Still, the Ducks bring plenty. Raiola has 1,695 throwing yards, 15 touchdowns and just 2 interceptions. Dakorien Moore has 702 receiving yards and 8 touchdowns, Dierre Hill Jr. leads the ground game with 572 yards, and Matayo Uiagalelei has 9.5 sacks. Devon Jackson leads Oregon with 63 tackles.

Michigan State is 3-7, and Shay will tell you every one of those losses has a story. The Spartans lost to Illinois 38-37 in overtime, to Northwestern 24-21, and to Washington 21-14 last week at home. She calls those three foul tips. You keep swinging, eh. Eventually one goes fair.

The Spartans also beat Michigan 15-6 in Ann Arbor earlier this month, which Shay has rewatched so many times her TV remote is shaped like her thumb.

"You beat Michigan by twenty-four," she tells Nix. "We beat 'em in their house. Different flavor. Ours tasted like a double scoop from the Dairy Store."

The quarterback picture is the big question for the Spartans. Alessio Milivojevic has handled most of the season with 1,559 throwing yards, 7 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Cam Fancher took the most snaps throwing against Washington and went 14 of 22 for 134 yards. Whoever is back there will need Chrishon McCray, who has 414 receiving yards, and Jaziun Patterson, who leads the team with 327 rushing yards. Dion Crawford has 58 tackles at linebacker, and Anelu Lafaele leads the team with 3.5 sacks.

"Fancher or Milivojevic, I don't care," Shay says. "Call the right pitch, keep the ball low, let the seniors go out fighting."

Here's how Friday plays out. Oregon scores on its opening drive, because of course it does, and Nix stands up to applaud the Ducks' cleats. But Michigan State's defense settles in and the senior class plays like it knows it's the last night in Spartan Stadium. Patterson punches in a short touchdown in the second quarter, the student section is still buzzing from the fireworks, and the Spartans are within a score at halftime. Raiola and Moore pull away in the third quarter, and Uiagalelei gets to the quarterback twice. Michigan State answers with a late score to keep the crowd standing, and the seniors walk off to a real ovation.

Nix rates the win a nine out of ten, docking a point for a muddy sleeve. Shay heads to the Dairy Store for a triple scoop and eats every bite in silence, which is how she grieves and also how she eats ice cream.

My call: Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan State Spartans 18.

The Wings of Blue parachute team is scheduled to drop into Falcon Stadium about twenty minutes before Friday's kickoff, weather permitting, and the cadets in the stands will spend Senior Night waiting to see how fast their option offense can bury a one-win visitor. My UTEP vs Air Force pick is Air Force Falcons −22.5 and the Over 45.5, kickoff 8:00 PM ET.

Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale has already given everyone call signs. "UTEP's quarterback is 'Scramble.' Our defense is 'Lid.' Their offense has been under the lid all season, Neto."

Neto Galindo, a Sun Bowl ironworker's kid, nods slowly. "Fair. We're 1-9. But Raymond Moore ran for 164 against Wyoming last week. That's real ore, Colonel."

It is. Moore is a quarterback who runs, with 686 rushing yards, and he has led UTEP in throws in four of its last five games. He is the expected starter here, and the Miners still have a hard time putting points up. UTEP is scoring 14.2 points a game and allowing 33.6. The Miners scored 7 points or fewer in four of their nine losses, and they allowed 30 or more six times.

Air Force is 8-2 and has won three straight, beating Army 24-21 and San José State 24-3. The Falcons are scoring 28.2 points a game and allowing 19.6, and they reached 24 points in eight of ten games. Evan Medders runs the option with 695 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, and he went for 146 yards on 13 carries last week. Blake Fletcher leads the defense with 92 tackles.

The quarterback room at the Academy rotates. Liam Szarka, Kemper Hodges, Medders and Howard Fisher IV have each led the team in attempts at least once. That matters less for an option team that threw three times last week.

Air Force Falcons 36, UTEP Miners 13 is a 23-point margin, half a point past 22.5, with 49 combined points, three and a half past 45.5. The side is tight. The total has more room: Air Force has scored 34 or more four times, and UTEP just has to reach the teens.

The cards agree on Air Force and the Over. Next Man Up has 38-14 with Air Force Falcons −22.5 and likes the Over 45.5. Letdown Watch has 36-12 with the Falcons and likes the Over. The Formula has 35-13 with UTEP Miners +22.5 and likes the Over too. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call this week. Follow The Money's side and total are both pending.

Next Man Up: "The Formula has Air Force by twenty-two and takes the Miners. Half a point of daylight."

The Formula: "Half a point is a whole point if you squint. I squint professionally."

Air Force covers by a hair, and the Over clears by more. The live falcons get their halftime flight, Marissa puts on her aviator shades, and Neto rolls up his sleeves for the trip home.

display.fanatic_story:
Three hours before kickoff on Friday, the Air Force Drum and Bugle Corps will march into Falcon Alley, and Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale will be standing at the front of the crowd in her aviator shades like she's inspecting the formation. UTEP Miners vs Air Force Falcons is Senior Night at Falcon Stadium, kickoff 6:00 PM in Colorado Springs and 8:00 PM ET, and the Academy is rolling out the full show: a Wings of Blue parachute jump about twenty minutes before the game, a military flyover, and live falcons with their cadet falconers at halftime.

Neto Galindo drove up from El Paso with a thermos of green chile stew and a jacket that he admits is built for a West Texas November, not a Colorado one.

"You people put a flyover AND skydivers on Senior Night?" he says. "Back home we get Paydirt Pete. I respect the budget, Colonel."

"Call sign for you is 'Thermos,'" Marissa says. "Welcome to the Academy."

The scoreboard part is harder for Neto. UTEP is 1-9, and the Miners have scored 14.2 points a game. They opened the year at Oklahoma and lost 51-0, and the only win came against Texas Southern, 51-10, back in September. The last two weeks have been close, though. The Miners lost 17-14 to Hawai'i and then 27-15 to Wyoming, and in that Wyoming game Raymond Moore III ran for 164 yards on 20 carries.

"Moore's the real thing," Neto says. "He runs like he's late for a shift. That's my highest grade. Pure ore."

Moore leads UTEP with 686 rushing yards and has taken over most of the throwing lately, too. EJ Colson Jr. has 687 throwing yards and 7 touchdowns for the year. Jaden Smith leads the receivers with 314 yards, and Jayden Wilson leads the defense with 65 tackles. Sterling Miles has 4 sacks off the end.

Marissa listens politely, then gets to her briefing. Air Force is 8-2. The Falcons beat Navy 14-9 in October, beat Army 24-21 at West Point this month, and then held San José State to a field goal in a 24-3 win last week. Evan Medders, a quarterback who mostly keeps the ball, has 695 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, and he ran for 146 yards on 13 carries against San José State.

"Medders is call sign 'Afterburner,'" Marissa says. "Fletcher is 'Radar.'"

Blake Fletcher leads Air Force with 92 tackles at linebacker. Liam Szarka leads the Falcons with 296 throwing yards, which tells you everything about how much this team likes to throw. Simon Kibbee, a tight end, leads in receiving with 166 yards. Max Mustell has 3 sacks from the secondary.

"Two hundred ninety-six yards in the air for a season?" Neto says. "We've had receivers do that by accident."

"We don't need the air," Marissa says. "We have the Wings of Blue for that."

There is one more thing Neto has working for him: the Falcons have stumbled before. They lost 38-32 at home to North Dakota State in September and fell 28-14 at Wyoming in October. Neto saw that Wyoming score and has been quoting it all week to anyone in earshot.

"Wyoming beat you by fourteen," he says. "Wyoming beat us by twelve. That makes us practically even, by my math."

"Your math needs a debrief," Marissa says.

Here's how it plays out. The Wings of Blue land on target, the flyover rattles the press box, and the seniors get a huge roar at kickoff. Moore breaks a long run on UTEP's first drive and Neto stands up and swings his imaginary pickaxe. Then the Air Force option starts its grind. Medders keeps it, pitches it, keeps it again, and the Falcons put together long drives that eat the clock and the Miners' energy. By halftime, when the cadet falconers bring out the birds, Air Force has a comfortable lead. Fletcher and the defense keep Moore boxed in during the second half, and UTEP grabs a late touchdown against the backups.

Marissa slides her aviator shades down and says "Mission accomplished." Neto zips his jacket, says "Back to the mine," and rolls up his sleeves for the long drive south.

My call: Air Force Falcons 36, UTEP Miners 13.

Wyoming is handing every fan an LED wristband on Friday night, giving away 1,000 glow-in-the-dark "Script Laradise" T-shirts, and handing out Cowboy Joe Club thundersticks to the first 1,000 fans, which means New Mexico Lobos vs Wyoming Cowboys at 7 p.m. in Laramie is going to look like a Balloon Fiesta dawn patrol that landed in a snowbank. That's how Paloma Begaye-Ortiz describes it, anyway, and she has flown in the real thing.

Colter Sprague, standing next to her in a Carhartt jacket with a wind gauge clipped to the zipper, has one word for the light show. "Pretty."

"Pretty? It's 'Light Up Laradise,' Colter. Your whole stadium is going to glow."

"Yep."

That's about as chatty as Colter gets, and Paloma has learned to fill in the rest. Wyoming has been on a tear. The Cowboys are 7-3, 6-1 in the Mountain West, sitting first in the conference and riding five straight wins. They are perfect at home, beating Northern Colorado, Hawai'i, Northern Illinois and Air Force at War Memorial. The Air Force game was a 28-14 statement in October, and Colter still smiles about it. That's two smiles in one month, which Paloma says is a personal record.

"Tell me about your quarterback," Paloma says.

Colter checks the wind gauge. "Depends."

It does. Tyler Hughes has run the offense most of the year and leads Wyoming in both throwing yards with 1,238 and rushing with 676. Then last week at UTEP, Landon Sims led the throws and went 19 of 25 for 289 yards in a 27-15 win. Kyle Frendt, the tight end, caught 4 balls for 113 yards in that game and leads the team in receiving. Ethan Stuhlsatz leads the defense with 79 tackles, and Esaia Bogar has 5.5 sacks.

"Two good quarterbacks," Colter says. Then, after a full ten seconds: "Good problem."

Paloma has her own stack of reasons. New Mexico is 8-2 and the defense has been brutal, giving up 11.9 points a game. The Lobos held UTEP to 7, Nevada to 3, and San José State and North Dakota State to 16 each. Scottre Humphrey has 736 rushing yards and 14 touchdowns, a back who runs like the wind's at his tail on every carry. Cade Keith leads the receivers with 384 yards, Darren Agu has 7.5 sacks, and Mercury Swaim leads the defense with 61 tackles.

"Our defense is green chile," Paloma says. "It sneaks up on you. One minute you're fine. Next minute you're crying and reaching for a sopapilla."

Then there's last week, which Paloma would rather not discuss. New Mexico lost 21-17 at home to UNLV, and Toa Fa'avae went 7 of 14 for 40 yards. She calls it "too much heat," sighs once, and moves on.

"And you've had our number lately?" she asks.

"Some," Colter says.

He's being modest. Wyoming won six of the last nine meetings, including a wild 49-45 shootout in 2024. New Mexico won back-to-back meetings in 2020 and 2021, but the Cowboys have taken the last three, and Colter knows it.

Here's how Friday goes. The wristbands light up on cue, the thundersticks never stop, and Wyoming feeds off the crowd early. Hughes or Sims, whoever starts, gets a touchdown drive going in the first quarter and Colter actually says "Yep" out loud. But New Mexico's defense settles in and starts taking the Cowboys' running lanes away. Humphrey finds space in the second quarter, scores twice before the night is through, and Agu gets home for a big sack on a third down. Wyoming kicks a field goal and adds a late touchdown, but the Lobos hold on in the cold and take the win home to Albuquerque.

Paloma pumps her fist and yells, "Red or green? BOTH!" Colter looks at his glowing wristband for a long moment, says "Nope," and walks to the truck.

My call: New Mexico Lobos 27, Wyoming Cowboys 17.

Florida says goodbye to its seniors at noon Saturday, and the Vanderbilt vs Florida spread asks a hard question about a Senior Day crowd: how many points does a farewell party add? DraftKings has Florida −13.5 with a 47.5 over/under for the last home game of Jon Sumrall's first season, and my pick is Vanderbilt Commodores +13.5 and Over 47.5.

The athletic department is telling people to arrive early for the pregame ceremony at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. That's the part of Senior Day nobody prices. Emotional starts cut both ways, and a home team playing for the families in the stands tends to score early, then exhale.

Dax Marchetti, who classifies every opponent by species, has the Commodores filed under "wounded." He's not wrong about the form. Vanderbilt has lost five of its last six, and last week Jared Curtis threw 40 times against Alabama for 223 yards and six points. The Commodores score 21.3 a game and allow 28.6.

Pippa Ashcroft has heard all of that and still wants the points. "Junior Sherrill has 63 catches for 847 yards. Curtis didn't throw a pick against Alabama. And your quarterback had to run for 102 yards to beat Kentucky."

She has a case. Aaron Philo is back as Florida's starter, but the Kentucky win was a 21-14 grind where he threw for 119 yards. Florida has scored 7 and 8 points in two of its last three games. A team that needed its quarterback as a runner to win by seven on the road is a big ask to win by two touchdowns, even at home.

DraftKings opened this at Florida −13.5 with a 48.5 total, and the side hasn't budged. The total came down a point.

My final is Florida Gators 31, Vanderbilt Commodores 20. Florida wins by 11, so Vanderbilt stays inside the 13.5. The 51 combined points clear the 47.5. Jadan Baugh has 905 rushing yards and 15 scores, so the Gators will get theirs. Vanderbilt's defense gives up 28.6 a game, and Florida allows 26.2, so Curtis and Sherrill should find two or three trips to the end zone.

The room splits on the side. The Formula has Florida 32-20 and takes Vanderbilt +13.5. Letdown Watch likes Vanderbilt +13.5 at 29-23. Next Man Up goes the other way with Florida −13.5 at 33-18, and In The Trenches likes Florida −13.5 at 30-18 with no over/under call. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch all like the Over 47.5. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Thirteen and a half is nothing for a team with Baugh. Letdown Watch thinks every Senior Day is a hangover."

Letdown Watch: "Florida scored 7 against Oklahoma two weeks ago. That's not a hangover. That's a pattern."

The Formula: "You two argue. I'll take the 32-20 and the points."

Senior Day gives Florida plenty of reasons to win. It doesn't promise a blowout, and Vanderbilt has enough Sherrill to keep this inside two scores.

Florida Gators 31, Vanderbilt Commodores 20. Vanderbilt Commodores cover the 13.5. Over 47.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Vanderbilt vs Florida closes the home schedule at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, and the Gators have dressed it up as Senior Day presented by Regions, with the pregame ceremony honoring the Florida seniors who are playing their last game in The Swamp. Florida insider Dax Marchetti says that makes noon a goodbye party with a reptile on the cake, while Vanderbilt insider Pippa Ashcroft says Jared Curtis, Junior Sherrill and the Commodores did not drive down from Nashville to hold anybody's tissues.

Dax: Pippa, the athletic department said arrive early. I have been here since sunrise. I brought a field guide and a handkerchief, and I'm only using one of them on purpose.

Pippa: You can use the handkerchief when Sherrill runs past your nickel. Sixty-three catches, Dax. Eight hundred forty-seven yards. That young man has a whole album of Saturdays.

That's the tension in Gainesville this week. One side is throwing a farewell, and the other side came to crash it. It's also the last home game of Jon Sumrall's first season in charge, so the seniors get the flowers, the coach gets one more chance to send them out winners, and Vanderbilt gets to play the role nobody invites on purpose.

Dax: Here is the thing you don't understand about this Florida team. It found itself in Lexington last week. Aaron Philo came back as the quarterback and ran for 102 yards and a score in a 21-14 win at Kentucky. When your quarterback is your leading rusher on the road, that's not a game plan. That's a species adapting.

Pippa: And Jadan Baugh?

Dax: Jadan Baugh has 905 rushing yards and 15 rushing scores. He is the apex predator of this ecosystem. He doesn't need to lead every Saturday to rule the swamp.

Pippa did her homework too, and she will tell you Vanderbilt's season has been more heartache than headline. The Commodores opened 3-0 with wins over Austin Peay, Delaware and NC State, then hit the SEC teeth: Auburn, Georgia, Ole Miss, Arkansas and Kentucky in a row. They broke through with a 25-23 win at Mississippi State, then lost 21-6 to Alabama last Saturday when Curtis threw 40 times and nobody could find the end zone.

Pippa: I wrote a song about the Alabama game. It's two verses long and the chorus is just "six points." But listen. Curtis went 25 of 40 for 223 yards and didn't throw an interception. Sherrill caught seven balls for 100. We moved it. We just parked it in the wrong lot.

Dax: Your defense gives up more than 28 points a game. My front is coming.

Pippa: Your front had better bring a lunch. Bryan Longwell has 73 tackles. Issa Ouattara has four sacks. Those two are not here for the senior photos.

Dax has his own defensive names to throw back. Jayden Woods leads the Gators with six sacks, and Myles Graham has 76 tackles, which means Curtis will spend much of the afternoon trying to find Sherrill before a linebacker finds him.

The two of them agree on exactly one point: this series has been lopsided. Florida's athletic department lists the all-time series at 44-11-2 for the Gators. Pippa answers that with a single date, Nov. 19, 2022, the 31-24 win in Nashville she has framed in her kitchen.

Pippa: Every lopsided series has a chapter where the little guy grabs the guitar. That's 2022. I'm just asking for a second verse.

Dax: You can have a verse. We're keeping the chorus.

What makes Senior Day dangerous is what it does to the home team's legs. The noise in the stadium comes early, and the emotion comes with it. If Florida starts slow because the seniors are still wiping their eyes from the ceremony, Vanderbilt can hang around the way it hung around at Starkville. If Florida starts fast, with Baugh going downhill and Philo taking off when the throwing lanes close, the Commodores will spend the second half trying to sing over the band.

Dax: The seniors get honored before kickoff, the crowd gets loud, and then the reptiles get loose. That's the order of operations.

Pippa: And while you're crying, we'll be throwing it to Sherrill. That's my order of operations.

Both of them want the same thing for the families in the stands, a clean, hard game and a sendoff worth remembering. Dax wants that sendoff in orange and blue. Pippa wants a road win to carry home to Nashville.

Dax: These seniors gave us everything they had. They get one more noon in the sun.

Pippa: Then let them enjoy it early, Dax. The fourth quarter belongs to whoever's still standing.

The ceremony will end, the families will find their seats and the seniors will run onto that grass for the last time. I think the Gators send them out with a win, and I think Vanderbilt makes them earn every yard of it.

My call: Florida Gators 31, Vanderbilt Commodores 20.

display.story_text:
Lawrence closes two seasons on Saturday. The Lawrence Farmers Market packs up its 50th year on New Hampshire Street at 11:30 a.m. Central, half an hour after Kansas kicks off its home finale against No. 10 BYU, and the BYU vs Kansas spread sits at BYU −5.5 with a 48.5 over/under on DraftKings. My pick is Kansas Jayhawks +5.5 and Over 48.5.

Saturday is also Senior Day at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, and this Kansas team has given its seniors plenty of near misses. The Jayhawks are 4-6, but the losses include 33-32 to UCF, 22-16 at TCU and 24-17 to Arizona State. That's a team that keeps finishing within a score, which is exactly what a 5.5-point underdog wants to be.

The line has already come our way. DraftKings opened BYU −7 with a 50.5 total, and both numbers have dropped. I'm still taking the points at 5.5.

Fitz Calloway, who converts every football stat into basketball points, brought last week's tape. "Isaiah Marshall went 15 of 18 and ran for 164 yards at West Virginia. Thirty points in the first half, 37-14 final." Kansas has now beaten BYU twice in a row, 38-27 in Lawrence and 17-13 in Provo.

Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi has the better team and knows it. "We're 8-2. We beat Notre Dame. Bear Bachmeier ran for three scores against Baylor." All true. BYU allows 18.5 points a game, and Bachmeier has 10 rushing touchdowns.

The trouble for the Cougars is the road. Their two losses came away from Provo, 39-31 in overtime at UCF and 28-20 at Utah, where Bachmeier threw four interceptions. Marshall gives Kansas a quarterback who can run as well as Bachmeier, with 692 rushing yards to Bachmeier's 449.

My final is BYU Cougars 27, Kansas Jayhawks 22. BYU wins, but Kansas stays inside the 5.5 by half a score. The 49 combined points clear 48.5 by the slimmest of hooks, and Kansas scores 30.2 a game with Marshall on his feet. Two running quarterbacks extend drives, and that keeps the scoreboard moving.

The room is split. The Formula likes BYU −5.5 at 29-22 and goes Over 48.5. Next Man Up also takes BYU −5.5 but goes Under at 27-21. Letdown Watch likes Kansas +5.5 at 26-24 and the Over. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call on this one. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Senior Day, home finale, a team that beat BYU two years running. Somebody tell The Formula where the game is."

The Formula: "It's in Lawrence. I checked. BYU still wins by seven."

Next Man Up: "And it'll be a low-scoring seven. I'm the only one here who watched Kansas hold West Virginia to 14."

The market folds its tents at 11:30, and the seniors get the rest of the afternoon. I trust Marshall to keep it inside a field goal and a hook.

BYU Cougars 27, Kansas Jayhawks 22. Kansas Jayhawks cover the 5.5. Over 48.5.

At 7:30 Saturday morning, three and a half hours before BYU vs Kansas kicks off, the Lawrence Farmers Market opens its tents on New Hampshire Street for the last time this year, closing out its 50th season on the same day the Jayhawks play their home finale. Kansas insider Fitz Calloway plans to buy apples downtown and walk them up the hill to David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, and BYU insider Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi says the No. 10 Cougars came to Lawrence to take something home that isn't produce.

Fitz: Fifty seasons of that market, Bryce. Fifty. That's longer than some basketball programs have been any good. You're standing in a town that knows how to finish a season.

Bryce: Oh my heck, Fitz, I love a farmers market. I'm buying honey for my wife and a pie for the flight home. Then we're beating you.

Kansas is calling Saturday Senior Day too, which means the Jayhawks get two goodbyes before lunch, one to the market and one to the seniors. The crowd that shows up at 11 a.m. Central will have muddy shoes and full grocery bags, and it'll be loud.

Fitz: You know what I saw last Saturday in Morgantown? Isaiah Marshall going 15 of 18 and running for 164 yards. Thirty points in the first half. We held West Virginia to 14. I converted that to basketball. It's a 37-14 win, which is roughly a forty-point blowout in hoops terms, and I refuse to show my math.

Bryce: Show your math. I'll show mine. Bear Bachmeier ran for three touchdowns against Baylor in a 28-7 win. He has ten rushing touchdowns this year to go with 14 through the air. The kid runs like he's late for a ward potluck.

That is the matchup everybody in Lawrence will be watching: two quarterbacks who would rather run through you than around you. Marshall leads Kansas in throwing and running with 692 rushing yards. Bachmeier leads BYU in both with 449 on the ground. Whoever gets the last word on a third-down scramble probably gets the last word on the afternoon.

Bryce: I'll be honest with you, Fitz, because that's how we do it in Provo. Bear had a rough night at Utah. Four interceptions. We lost 28-20. But he came back the next week and didn't throw one against Baylor. That's a kid who listens to his coaches.

Fitz: And Kansas has a guy who listens to nobody. Leroy Harris III has seven and a half sacks. He hears a snap count and just goes. I want him in Bachmeier's ear all day long.

Bryce: Cade Uluave is waiting on your Marshall. Sixty-one tackles. Bodie Schoonover has four sacks. We bring our own trouble.

The history is where Fitz gets a little smug. Kansas beat BYU 38-27 in Lawrence in 2023, then went to Provo the next November and won 17-13. Kansas athletics notes this is only BYU's second trip to Lawrence.

Fitz: Two meetings this decade, two wins. That's a perfect free-throw night.

Bryce: Respectfully, those were different Cougars. This group is 8-2 and has beaten Notre Dame. We don't scare easy, and we don't eat our pie before the game.

Fitz isn't hiding from the season, either. Kansas is 4-6, and the losses have stung: 33-32 to UCF, 22-16 at TCU, 24-17 to Arizona State. Three one-score losses, three what-ifs. The home crowd remembers every one of them, and Senior Day is the last chance for these seniors to send everybody to the parking lot happy.

Fitz: We play close with everybody. I'm tired of close. I want one more Saturday where the band plays the alma mater and nobody is checking the clock with a stomachache.

Bryce: You'll get the band. I can't promise you the stomach.

Then there's Legend Glasker, BYU's leading receiver with 706 yards. Nik McMillan is Kansas' with 541. Neither one has carried an offense by himself this year, which keeps sending the story back to the quarterbacks.

Bryce: Here's my dad joke for the market, Fitz. What do you call a Jayhawk at a farmers market? A little late in the season.

Fitz: That's terrible. I'm laughing because I'm polite, and because I'm going to win.

The tents come down at 11:30 on New Hampshire Street, half an hour after kickoff, and Lawrence will walk into winter after that. I think BYU leaves town with a win in its grocery bag, and I think Kansas makes the Cougars sweat right up to the final whistle.

My call: BYU Cougars 27, Kansas Jayhawks 22.
