display.fanatic_story:
Two days before Colorado vs Cincinnati, the Cincinnati Zoo flips the switch on its 44th annual PNC Festival of Lights, five million bulbs glowing across town from Historic Nippert Stadium. By Saturday at noon, the Bearcats want a different kind of glow, because Cincinnati is honoring 20 seniors before kickoff, and Colorado insider Moss Feldstein says the Buffaloes came east to turn the lights out on Senior Day.

Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy got to the zoo on opening night and headed straight for the Outpost Café, because the zoo serves Skyline Chili and he has never once ignored a sign.

Lionel: Moss, you have to understand what Thursday means around here. Fiona's Fairyland lights up, the hippo becomes a holiday icon again, and the whole city puts on a sweater. Then Saturday we send off 20 seniors at Nippert. This is our week. That's a five-way take, with extra onions.

Moss: Statistically, Lionel, five million lights is a lot of electricity for a team that's lost four of its last five. I'm not here to be rude. I'm here to be accurate.

He has a point, and Lionel knows it. Cincinnati started 4-0 and has spent the second half of the season limping. The Bearcats lost 34-7 at Arizona, 45-42 at West Virginia, 49-25 to Utah, 31-24 at Houston and 41-13 at Iowa State last Saturday. The one bright spot in that stretch was a 37-24 win over Texas Tech at home.

Lionel: At home, Moss. That's the whole story. We're 4-1 at Nippert this year. On the road we turn into four-way without the beans. At home we're the full bowl.

Moss: I'll grant you the bowl. But you gave up 41 to Iowa State, and we just put 42 on Houston.

That Friday night in Boulder was the best evening Colorado has had in a while. The Buffaloes beat Houston 42-32. Richard Young ran 21 times for 99 yards and two scores, Isaac Wilson threw for 217 yards, and Joseph Williams caught five balls for 80 yards and a touchdown. Williams has 63 catches for 933 yards on the season, which makes him the receiver Cincinnati's secondary will be talking about all week.

Moss: Joseph Williams is my whole hammock philosophy. Relaxed, then gone. Your safeties will look up and he'll already be in the end zone eating a granola bar.

Lionel: Jasper Beeler has 77 tackles. He doesn't let anybody eat in the end zone. House rules.

Cincinnati's answer on offense is two names. JC French IV has thrown 16 touchdowns and only three interceptions all season, which means he takes care of the ball like it's the last cheese coney in the pot. Cole Tabb has 977 rushing yards and ten scores, and he ran for 165 even in the loss at Ames.

Moss: Tabb is legit. I'll say it out loud. But French threw for 97 yards last week.

Lionel: And Tabb ran for 165 and caught eight more balls. When a running back is your whole offense in a 41-13 loss, you give him the ball 30 times at home with the seniors watching.

Colorado has a road problem, and Moss doesn't hide from it. The Buffaloes are 1-4 away from Boulder this year, with the only road win a 14-13 squeaker at Georgia Tech in the opener. They lost 41-7 at Northwestern, 23-13 at Baylor, 57-24 at Oklahoma State and 20-10 at Arizona State.

Moss: That's the thing about altitude, Lionel. When we come down to sea level, we get light-headed in the other direction.

Lionel: Cincinnati isn't sea level. We're river level. It's worse.

The last time these two met was 2024, in Boulder, and Colorado won 34-23. Moss brings it up the way people bring up a road trip where everything went right.

Lionel: Different building. Different month. Different chili.

The Senior Day ceremony is where Lionel gets soft for a minute, which he'd deny under oath. Twenty players, all of them walking out to a home crowd that has watched them through good and bad Novembers. The zoo will be lit up again that night, and Lionel wants the families to drive past it on the way home after a win.

Lionel: I want those seniors under the lights at the zoo Saturday night, holding a hot cocoa, not answering a single question about what went wrong.

Moss: And I want Joseph Williams past a thousand yards by the fourth quarter. Then I'll buy you a hot cocoa myself.

Lionel: Deal. Three-way. No beans.

The lights at the zoo run into January. The seniors only get one walk at Nippert, and Tabb gives them a winner to remember.

My call: Cincinnati Bearcats 30, Colorado Buffaloes 24.

Boston College closes its home schedule Saturday with the second Jay McGillis Memorial Senior Day, named for the Eagles' former strong safety who died of leukemia, and the Syracuse vs Boston College spread has Syracuse −3 with a 50.5 over/under on DraftKings. My pick is Boston College Eagles +3 and Over 50.5.

The memorial matters to how this game gets played. McGillis played for Tom Coughlin, and the Jay Fund Coughlin started in his honor still helps families fighting childhood cancer. Siobhan Dunleavy, who runs every argument like a trial, says the seniors know the story and will play like it. I don't price emotion, but I do price a home team that has won the last two meetings, 37-31 at Alumni Stadium and 34-12 at Syracuse.

Nico Calabrese brings Syracuse's case, and it's a good one. The Orange are 5-5, one win from a bowl, and have won three of four. Steve Angeli threw for 272 yards in last week's 34-31 win at NC State, Calvin Russell III caught 17 passes, and Umari Hatcher has 1,045 receiving yards.

Here is why I still want the points. Syracuse's wins in that stretch came by one point in overtime at North Carolina, three over SMU and three at NC State. This team plays close games, and a field goal is exactly what the line gives Boston College. DraftKings opened Syracuse −3.5 with a 50.5 total, and the side has slipped half a point toward the Eagles.

Boston College has been rough lately. Mason McKenzie went 8 of 21 for 51 yards in a 41-7 loss at Notre Dame, and the Eagles have dropped three straight. But McKenzie is also the team's leading rusher with 686 yards, and he ran the offense when Boston College scored 49 at Georgia Tech. Anthony Palano has 87 tackles, and Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks.

My final is Boston College Eagles 26, Syracuse Orange 25. The Eagles win outright, so they clear the 3 with room to spare. The 51 points clear 50.5 by half a point. Syracuse scores 29.8 a game and Boston College allows 28.4, so the Orange should get theirs through Hatcher. The Eagles find enough at home with McKenzie running.

The room splits two and two on the side. Letdown Watch likes Boston College +3 at 27-25, and In The Trenches likes Boston College +3 at 28-22 with no over/under call. The Formula takes Syracuse −3 at 27-24, and Next Man Up takes Syracuse −3 at 28-23. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch all go Over 50.5. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

In The Trenches: "Boston College won this matchup the last two years. The Formula is still grading Syracuse on a curve."

The Formula: "Seventeen catches for one receiver, In The Trenches. Count them."

Letdown Watch: "Count Boston College's seniors instead. They're the ones playing for a name."

One point decides it on the Heights, and the Eagles finish their home season with a win that means more to them than any scoreboard could show.

Boston College Eagles 26, Syracuse Orange 25. Boston College Eagles cover the 3. Over 50.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Jay McGillis was Boston College's strong safety in 1991, and on Saturday his name sits on the Syracuse vs Boston College game at Alumni Stadium, the second Jay McGillis Memorial Senior Day. Boston College insider Siobhan Dunleavy says that makes the home finale bigger than a record, while Syracuse insider Nico Calabrese says Steve Angeli and an Orange team one win from bowl eligibility are coming to Chestnut Hill with every reason in the world to spoil it.

The story behind the name is why this one lands differently on the Heights. McGillis played for Tom Coughlin, was diagnosed with leukemia during that 1991 season and died in the summer of 1992 after chemotherapy and a bone marrow transplant from his older brother. Coughlin started the Jay Fund in 1996 to help families facing childhood cancer, and a memorial scholarship in McGillis' name still goes to a senior defensive back every year.

Siobhan: Nico, I'll keep the courtroom closed for one minute. Saturday our seniors get honored under the name of a teammate who never got his own senior day. Our guys know that story. They'll play like it.

Nico: I respect that completely, Siobhan. Nobody from Syracuse is going to say a word against it. We'll just try to ruin your afternoon the old-fashioned way, with a receiver named Umari and a few of his friends.

Then the courtroom reopens, because these two have been arguing about this rivalry since long before this week.

Siobhan: Exhibit A. The Eagles have won the last two meetings, 37-31 here in 2024 and 34-12 at your place last November.

Nico: Objection. Different year, different Orange. Exhibit B. Steve Angeli threw for 272 yards at NC State last Saturday, we won 34-31, and Calvin Russell III caught 17 balls. Seventeen, Siobhan. That's not a box score. That's a blizzard. Two feet of snow, minimum.

Seventeen catches for 137 yards in one game is the kind of thing an opposing defensive coordinator stares at on a Sunday night. And Russell isn't even Syracuse's main target. That's Umari Hatcher, who has 66 catches for 1,045 yards and eight touchdowns. When a defense chases one of them, the other wanders open.

Siobhan: Anthony Palano has 87 tackles. He has been in on more plays than some of our fans. I'll put him on whoever's catching it and let the jury decide.

Nico: Keyshawn Johnson has eight sacks for us. Your quarterback had a rough day at South Bend.

That's the hard part for Boston College. Mason McKenzie is the Eagles' leading thrower and leading rusher, with 686 yards on the ground, but last week at Notre Dame he went 8 of 21 for 51 yards in a 41-7 loss. The week before, Florida State won 31-24 at Alumni Stadium. The week before that, Duke won 47-2. Boston College has dropped three straight and has been searching for its offense since the leaves turned.

Siobhan: Overruled. Mason ran our offense at Georgia Tech and we scored 49. When he gets outside the pocket, he becomes a running back with a better haircut.

Nico: That's fair. I've seen it, and I didn't enjoy it.

Syracuse comes in with the momentum. The Orange have won three of their last four, including a 31-30 overtime win at North Carolina and last week's 34-31 win at NC State. Angeli has been the steady hand since he got the job back in late October, and Tylik Hill gives the Orange 591 rushing yards to keep defenses honest.

Nico: We're 5-5, Siobhan. One more win and we're going bowling. I would drive to Chestnut Hill in a whiteout for that.

Siobhan: Bring a shovel. And bring a coat for your secondary, because Demetrius Ballard has four and a half sacks and he plays like the wind off the reservoir.

Even the closing arguments sound a little different this week. Both of them come back, without being asked, to the man whose name is on the game.

Siobhan: Whatever happens, I want our seniors to walk off that field knowing they honored Jay McGillis with how hard they played.

Nico: That I can promise you. They'll have to play hard, because we will.

The verdict is a one-point game on the Heights, with the home side honoring its seniors and the man in whose name they play by holding on at the end.

My call: Boston College Eagles 26, Syracuse Orange 25.

My pick is Boston College Eagles +3 and Over 50.5.

The memorial matters to how this game gets played. McGillis played for Tom Coughlin, and the Jay Fund Coughlin started in his honor still helps families fighting childhood cancer. Siobhan Dunleavy, who runs every argument like a trial, says the seniors know the story and will play like it. I don't price emotion, but I do price a home team that has won the last two meetings, 37-31 at Alumni Stadium and 34-12 at Syracuse.

Nico Calabrese brings Syracuse's case, and it's a good one. The Orange are 5-5, one win from a bowl, and have won three of four. Steve Angeli threw for 272 yards in last week's 34-31 win at NC State, Calvin Russell III caught 17 passes, and Umari Hatcher has 1,045 receiving yards.

Here is why I still want the points. Syracuse's wins in that stretch came by one point in overtime at North Carolina, three over SMU and three at NC State. This team plays close games, and a field goal is exactly what the line gives Boston College. DraftKings opened Syracuse −3.5 with a 50.5 total, and the side has slipped half a point toward the Eagles.

Boston College has been rough lately. Mason McKenzie went 8 of 21 for 51 yards in a 41-7 loss at Notre Dame, and the Eagles have dropped three straight. But McKenzie is also the team's leading rusher with 686 yards, and he ran the offense when Boston College scored 49 at Georgia Tech. Anthony Palano has 87 tackles, and Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks.

My final is Boston College Eagles 26, Syracuse Orange 25. The Eagles win outright, so they clear the 3 with room to spare. The 51 points clear 50.5 by half a point. Syracuse scores 29.8 a game and Boston College allows 28.4, so the Orange should get theirs through Hatcher. The Eagles find enough at home with McKenzie running.

The room splits two and two on the side. Letdown Watch likes Boston College +3 at 27-25, and In The Trenches likes Boston College +3 at 28-22 with no over/under call. The Formula takes Syracuse −3 at 27-24, and Next Man Up takes Syracuse −3 at 28-23. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch all go Over 50.5. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

In The Trenches: "Boston College won this matchup the last two years. The Formula is still grading Syracuse on a curve."

The Formula: "Seventeen catches for one receiver, In The Trenches. Count them."

Letdown Watch: "Count Boston College's seniors instead. They're the ones playing for a name."

One point decides it on the Heights, and the Eagles finish their home season with a win that means more to them than any scoreboard could show.

Boston College Eagles 26, Syracuse Orange 25. Boston College Eagles cover the 3. Over 50.5.

Twenty-one points is a lot to lay on the road against a team that has beaten you five straight times, and that is the Wake Forest vs Georgia Tech spread this week, Wake −21 at DraftKings, with the over/under at 56.5. My pick is Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets +21 and Under 56.5.

Saturday is Georgia Tech's home finale, Senior Day and the annual Michael Isenhour Toy Drive game, with fans bringing new, unwrapped toys to the gates at Bobby Dodd Stadium. Wendell Quist, who treats everything as a physics problem, is bringing a toy truck. He's also bringing a team that just won 20-6 at Clemson.

That win matters for this handicap. Justice Haynes ran for 116 yards and a score in Death Valley, and Georgia Tech won by holding the ball and keeping the clock moving. That's exactly how a big home underdog survives a team like Wake. Haynes has 751 rushing yards this season. Long drives shorten the game, and a short game protects a three-touchdown cushion.

Eloise Brightman-Rowe has the stronger team and every reason to say so. "Seven straight wins. We beat SMU 49-7 in Dallas. Gio Lopez has 19 touchdown throws and one interception." Wake scores 43.9 points a game and allows 15.0. Carlos Hernandez has 1,039 receiving yards.

None of that is in dispute. Wake is the better team, and my final has the Deacons by 18. But Georgia Tech has won five straight in this series, and Wake's last trip to Bobby Dodd was in 2017. The Deacons are playing for an ACC title-game spot, so expect them to grind it out instead of running up the score late.

My final is Wake Forest Demon Deacons 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 18. Wake wins by 18, so Georgia Tech stays inside the 21. The 54 combined points stay under 56.5. A Georgia Tech team running Haynes keeps Lopez on the bench longer than Wake would like, and that keeps the total down.

DraftKings opened Wake −20.5 with a 56.5 total. The side has crept half a point toward Wake, and the total hasn't moved.

Three handicappers are with me on the side. The Formula likes Georgia Tech +21 at 36-19. Next Man Up also takes Georgia Tech +21 at 39-18, and In The Trenches likes Georgia Tech +21 at 31-20 with no over/under call. Letdown Watch is alone on Wake −21 at 38-16. On the total, The Formula takes the Under, Letdown Watch likes the Under 56.5, and Next Man Up goes Over. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Thirty-eight to sixteen. Wake isn't losing focus with a title game in sight."

The Formula: "That's not a letdown pick, that's a fan club."

In The Trenches: "Haynes ran for 116 at Clemson. You want me to lay 21 into that? I like toys, not charity."

The bins fill up at the gates either way. On the field, Wake wins comfortably, but the Jackets stay inside three touchdowns.

Wake Forest Demon Deacons 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 18. Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets cover the 21. Under 56.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Wendell Quist is bringing a toy to Bobby Dodd Stadium on Saturday, new and unwrapped, because Wake Forest vs Georgia Tech is the Yellow Jackets' annual Michael Isenhour Toy Drive game and the home finale on The Flats. Wake Forest insider Eloise Brightman-Rowe is bringing a toy too, and a 9-1 team with Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez that would very much like to leave Atlanta with an ACC Championship Game ticket in its pocket.

Some background for anybody who hasn't been on North Avenue in November. The drive was started in 2001 by Michael Isenhour, a Georgia Tech basketball player who wanted to help families after the September 11 attacks. He died in 2002, and the student-athletes renamed the drive for him. Fans bring new, unwrapped toys, and in past years Tech student-athletes have stood at the gates with the donation bins. It's also Senior Day and First Responders Appreciation Day, so the Jackets have a full house of reasons to play hard.

Wendell: Eloise, I've done the physics on this. A toy in a bin has potential energy. A kid opening it at the holidays is kinetic. That's the best conversion rate on campus, and I go to Georgia Tech.

Eloise: Wendell, that's the most generous thing an engineer has ever said to me. I'm still going to roll the Quad when we win.

Wake has given her plenty to roll. The Demon Deacons have won seven in a row and just took apart SMU 49-7 in Dallas. They score 43.9 points a game and give up 15.0. Lopez has thrown 19 touchdowns and one interception all season, which is the kind of number that makes a debate coach weep with joy.

Eloise: One interception, Wendell. One. Gio treats the football like a first-edition library book. And Carlos Hernandez has 1,039 receiving yards. Your secondary is going to need a study group.

Wendell: Our secondary has Tae Harris, and Tae Harris has 63 tackles. Graph paper doesn't lie, Eloise. Neither does a safety who arrives on time.

Georgia Tech's season has been a grind, and Wendell isn't pretending otherwise. The Jackets are 3-7 and spent late October and early November getting pushed around, losing 49-27 to Boston College, 34-11 at Pittsburgh and 44-17 to Louisville. But last Saturday something clicked at Clemson. Georgia Tech won 20-6 in Death Valley, Justice Haynes ran for 116 yards and a score, and the defense held Clemson to six points.

Wendell: That's not luck, that's mechanics. We controlled the ball, we tackled in space and we made a road crowd go quiet. Physics says a body at rest stays at rest. A body coming off a win at Clemson stays moving.

Eloise: Physics also says a 9-1 team is heavier than a 3-7 team.

The history gives Wendell a little more to stand on. Georgia Tech has won the last five meetings in the series, according to the Jackets, including 30-29 at Wake last year. Tech leads the all-time series 24-8, and this is Wake's first trip to Bobby Dodd since 2017.

Eloise: I've read the brief, Wendell. History is not a defensive coordinator. History doesn't get Gio on the ground.

Wendell: No, but Taje McCoy might. Three sacks. And Alberto Mendoza has thrown for 2,081 yards for us. He has completed 190 of 279 throws, and he keeps getting up.

Here is where both of them get serious. Wake has plenty at stake Saturday. The Jackets know they can spoil the Deacons' title-game hopes, and nothing motivates a home team in November like the chance to be the reason somebody else's season gets complicated.

Eloise: Our guys know that, which is why I'm not taking this lightly. Lopez and Hernandez are going to come out throwing early, and Ty Clark III is going to run behind them when your defense backs up.

Wendell: And we're going to run Haynes into the teeth of it and make the clock our best friend. Nobody beats Wake in a track meet. You beat Wake by making them wait.

That's the whole puzzle. If Georgia Tech can keep Lopez on the sideline with long Haynes drives, the Flats stay loud deep into the afternoon. If Wake scores early, the toys in the bins will be the happiest part of the day for the home crowd.

Eloise: Bring a big toy, Wendell. You'll want something to hug on the drive home.

Wendell: I'm bringing a toy truck. Engineered for all terrain, like my patience.

The bins at the gates will fill up for the Atlanta kids either way. On the field, Wake is too good to stop and Georgia Tech is too proud to fold.

My call: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 18.

Every handicapper with a side on this card agrees on it, and that almost never happens in a series this even. The Northwestern vs Minnesota spread is Northwestern −3 at DraftKings with the total at 42.5, and my pick is Northwestern Wildcats −3 and Over 42.5 for Senior Day at Huntington Bank Stadium.

Minnesota's game-day timeline has the Senior Day ceremony on the field at 10:30 a.m. Central and the ROW chant two minutes before kickoff, with the whole stadium pulling imaginary oars. Tor Engebretsen will row harder than anybody. The question for this pick is whether the Gophers can row with a Northwestern team that has already reached six wins.

Both teams have lost three straight, so form doesn't separate them. Quality of losses does. Northwestern's three came against Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State, and it was within nine at the Horseshoe last week. Minnesota lost 42-14 at Penn State and 34-20 at home to UCLA. Drake Lindsey has thrown 326 passes for 1,982 yards, and the Gophers score 23.6 points a game.

Ezra Lindqvist has the Wildcats' numbers and footnotes them. "Northwestern scores 29.8 and allows 20.2. Nicco Marchiol threw for 225 at Ohio State. Braydon Brus has 81 tackles." Griffin Wilde has 843 receiving yards and Caleb Komolafe 697 rushing, and Aidan Chiles threw 13 touchdowns against one interception before Marchiol took most of the throws the last two games.

DraftKings opened Northwestern −3 with a 43.5 total. The side hasn't moved. The total has dropped a point, which makes the Over cheaper.

My final is Northwestern Wildcats 27, Minnesota Golden Gophers 21. Northwestern wins by six and clears the 3. The 48 combined points clear 42.5 comfortably. These two have played some high-scoring games lately, 38-35 last year and 37-34 in 2023, and both offenses have a receiver who can break a game open in Wilde and Javon Tracy.

The room lines up on Northwestern −3 across the board. The Formula likes it at 29-20, Next Man Up likes it at 27-19, Letdown Watch likes it at 28-18, and In The Trenches likes it too, with no over/under call. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch all like the Over 42.5. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Four of us on the same side. Somebody check The Formula for a fever."

The Formula: "I'm fine. You're the one who had Minnesota scoring 19 on Senior Day."

Letdown Watch: "Eighteen, actually. Minnesota has lost three straight. The emotion fades by halftime."

The oars go up right before kickoff. Northwestern pulls away in the second half because it has more answers on offense.

Northwestern Wildcats 27, Minnesota Golden Gophers 21. Northwestern Wildcats cover the 3. Over 42.5.

display.fanatic_story:
At 10:58 a.m. Central on Saturday, two minutes before Northwestern vs Minnesota kicks off, everybody in Huntington Bank Stadium is supposed to grab an imaginary oar and row. Minnesota insider Tor Engebretsen has been practicing his stroke in the garage all week, and Northwestern insider Ezra Lindqvist says Nicco Marchiol and a bowl-eligible Wildcats team plan to leave the Gophers rowing upstream on Senior Day.

The schedule for the day reads like a Gopher fan's prayer book. Tailgate lots open at 7. The team arrives for the Ski-U-March near Gate C at 8:30. The Spirit Rally at Tribal Nations Plaza starts at 9:40. Then comes the Senior Day ceremony on the field at 10:30, the Pride of Minnesota Marching Band at 10:40 and the ROW chant right before the kick.

Tor: Ezra, I want you to understand the ROW chant. It isn't a cheer. It's a philosophy. You keep pulling no matter what the river does. We've had a rough river lately.

Ezra: Footnote one: rough river is generous. Footnote two: I'll row with you, Tor, but only to be polite.

The river has been rough for both sides, and that's what makes this one interesting. Minnesota has lost three straight: 23-16 in overtime at Indiana, 34-20 to UCLA and 42-14 at Penn State. At 5-5, the Gophers need one more win to get to a bowl game. Northwestern already has its six wins, but it's lost three in a row too, to Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State.

Tor: Here's how I rate teams. I ask how they'd handle January. A January team doesn't panic. We're a January team. Cold enough for ya? Good.

Ezra: Northwestern is a lakefront team. We handle wind off Lake Michigan that would knock a Gopher back into its hole. Footnote: affectionately.

The quarterbacks are where the conversation gets real. Drake Lindsey has thrown 326 times for Minnesota and has 1,982 yards. He threw two touchdowns at Penn State, and Darius Taylor caught four balls for 85 yards. Lindsey has been the steady name in a season that hasn't always been steady around him.

Northwestern's quarterback room is a two-chapter story. Aidan Chiles threw for 1,898 yards, 13 touchdowns and only one interception in the first eight games. The last two weeks, Marchiol has thrown the most passes for the Wildcats, and he went 18 of 31 for 225 yards and a touchdown at Ohio State in a 28-19 loss.

Ezra: Marchiol threw at the Horseshoe without blinking. Luke Dehnicke caught five for 88 and a score. Footnote: I was right about Dehnicke in August, and I have the notebook to prove it.

Tor: We'll see how Dehnicke likes Maverick Baranowski. Eighty tackles. That kid hits like an ice-out on Lake Minnetonka. Then there's TJ Bush Jr. up front with six sacks.

Ezra: Braydon Brus has 81 tackles and four sacks for us, Tor. He leads our team in both. I'd call that a full-service linebacker.

Then there's Griffin Wilde, Northwestern's top receiver with 843 yards. Caleb Komolafe has 697 rushing yards for the Wildcats. Minnesota counters with Javon Tracy, who has 55 catches, and TJ Thomas on the ground.

The series is as even as a canoe with two people who know what they're doing. In the last eight meetings, going back to 2016, Northwestern and Minnesota have each won four. Last year's game was 38-35 to the Wildcats. In 2023, Northwestern won 37-34. Ezra brings those up with a straight face.

Tor: Two close losses. That's what a river does. It pushes you sideways. Then you row.

Ezra: Or you get out and walk. Footnote: we walked to a bowl already.

That's the difference, and Tor knows it. Northwestern can relax a little. Minnesota can't. The Senior Day ceremony at 10:30 will be emotional, and then the seniors have a ballgame to win to keep their season going into December.

Tor: I'm going to cry at 10:30, I'm going to row at 10:58, and I'm going to yell for three hours after that. That's a full Saturday on the East Bank.

Ezra: I'll bring you tissues. Purple ones.

The oars come up at 10:58, the Gophers will pull hard, and the Wildcats will pull a little harder at the end.

My call: Northwestern Wildcats 27, Minnesota Golden Gophers 21.

display.story_text:
Lincoln sold out its final home game early, and the Ohio State vs Nebraska spread has drifted toward the Huskers ever since DraftKings opened it. The number now is Ohio State −3, total 41.5. I'm taking Ohio State Buckeyes −3 and Over 41.5, my pick for Senior Day at Memorial Stadium.

That line move is the story of this handicap. DraftKings opened Ohio State −5.5 with a 47.5 total. The spread has dropped two and a half points and the total six. The market has marked down Ohio State's offense since Luke Fahey took over the throwing three weeks ago, and it has marked up a Nebraska defense allowing 14.9 points a game. I think the market went too far.

Darla Rasmussen will tell you the sellout and the seniors are worth a field goal. "Bowl eligible. Shut out Rutgers 31-0. Three of our four losses in that skid were one-score games." All true. Nebraska is better than its 6-4 suggests.

But here is Buck Holloway's case, and I agree with it. Fahey went 21 of 32 for 201 yards and three touchdowns against Northwestern, and he's throwing to Jeremiah Smith, who has 80 catches for 1,317 yards and 15 touchdowns. Bo Jackson ran for 114 last week. Ohio State scores 34.9 a game and allows 18.4, and it has won all seven meetings in this stretch since 2016.

Nebraska's offense is the concern. The Huskers scored 17, 14, 10 and 13 in their four straight losses before Rutgers. Anthony Colandrea has 18 touchdown throws, but against good defenses this team has struggled to find the end zone.

My final is Ohio State Buckeyes 27, Nebraska Cornhuskers 21. Ohio State wins by six and clears the 3. The 48 combined points clear 41.5 comfortably. A six-point drop in the total is an overreaction for a game with Smith on the field and a Nebraska offense that just scored 31 on the road.

The room agrees on the side. The Formula likes Ohio State −3 at 28-22. Letdown Watch likes Ohio State −3 at 26-21. Next Man Up takes Ohio State −3 at 25-21. All three like the Over 41.5. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Twenty-five points. I'm the cautious one, and I still have Ohio State covering."

Letdown Watch: "Cautious is how The Formula got a 28-22. Sold-out crowd, Senior Day, and you three still trust a new quarterback on the road."

The Formula: "I trust Jeremiah Smith. The quarterback just has to find him."

Memorial Stadium will be red and loud for the seniors. Smith is the difference, and Ohio State pulls away late.

Ohio State Buckeyes 27, Nebraska Cornhuskers 21. Ohio State Buckeyes cover the 3. Over 41.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Ohio State vs Nebraska is the last home game of the year at Memorial Stadium, Senior Day in Lincoln at 11 a.m. Central, and the Huskers announced it sold out more than a week ahead of time. Nebraska insider Darla Rasmussen says a full house and a team that just found itself at Rutgers make this the best chance Lincoln has had at the Buckeyes in years, while Ohio State insider Buck Holloway says Jeremiah Smith and Luke Fahey didn't come to Nebraska to be anybody's farewell gift.

Darla: Buck, I have one rule this week. You don't get to talk about our history until you've stood in that stadium when it's full. Every seat sold, every seat red, and the seniors running out of the tunnel for the last time.

Buck: Darla, I respect a sellout. We have plenty in Columbus. But I've stood in a full stadium before, and I've watched the home team walk out of it quietly. That's a Columbus problem for you, not for me.

The quiet part is the history, and Buck has it memorized. Ohio State won all seven meetings in this stretch going back to 2016, and some of them weren't close: 62-3 in 2016, 56-14 in 2017, 48-7 in 2019. The most recent one, in 2024, was a 21-17 game that Nebraska fans still replay in their heads.

Darla: Twenty-one to seventeen. In your building. We were right there, Buck. Right there.

Buck: Right there is a nice place to visit.

This year, though, Nebraska has a better case than usual. The Huskers are 6-4 and bowl eligible after a 31-0 win at Rutgers last Saturday. Anthony Colandrea threw two touchdowns and went 15 of 22, Jamal Rule ran 22 times for 103 yards, and the defense didn't let Rutgers score at all. That ended a four-game skid in which the Huskers lost to Indiana by three, Oregon by three, Washington by seven and Illinois by 11.

Darla: Three of those four were one-score games. We aren't a bad team, Buck. We're a close team that needed somebody to finish. Colandrea has 18 touchdown throws. Our defense gives up 14.9 points a game. Go Big Red.

Buck: Your defense is legit, and I'll say that on the record. But your offense has scored 17 or fewer in four of its last six. We give up 18.4 a game ourselves.

Ohio State's season has turned, too. The Buckeyes started 6-1, then lost at USC and to Oregon at home, and Julian Sayin hasn't been the one throwing it the last three weeks. Fahey has, and last Saturday he looked comfortable, going 21 of 32 for 201 yards and three touchdowns in a 28-19 win over Northwestern.

Buck: Fahey's growing up in front of us. And when your quarterback has Jeremiah Smith, you don't have to be perfect. You have to be pointed in the right direction. Eleven catches, 117 yards last week. Fifteen touchdown catches on the year. That young man is the best receiver I've ever watched in scarlet, and I've watched a lot of them.

Darla: We've got Kwazi Gilmer and his 603 yards, and Jahsear Whittington with five and a half sacks. Whittington's going to say hello to Fahey early and often.

Buck: Kenyatta Jackson Jr. has five sacks for us. Earl Little Jr. is everywhere. And Bo Jackson ran for 114 last week. We can hand it to him all afternoon if we have to.

The Senior Day ceremony is where Darla goes quiet for a second. She has watched these seniors through the hard years, and she wants them to walk off the field with something to point to, a home win over a name brand before the trip to Iowa City on Black Friday.

Darla: This isn't about revenge. It's about a group of kids who stuck around when it was hard. Give them one Saturday like this.

Buck: I hear you, Darla, and I mean it when I say congratulations on the bowl. But Ohio State doesn't hand out Saturdays. You have to take them.

There's real tension in that. Nebraska's crowd will be loud from the first snap, and the Huskers' defense can keep it close. Ohio State has more ways to score and the best player on the field in Smith. If the Buckeyes protect Fahey and keep it simple, the Huskers' farewell gets complicated in the fourth quarter.

Darla: Fill every seat, then make it loud. That's the plan.

Buck: The plan in Columbus is Jeremiah Smith on third down.

The seniors get their roar, and Memorial Stadium gives them everything it has. Smith gives Ohio State just a little bit more.

My call: Ohio State Buckeyes 27, Nebraska Cornhuskers 21.

West Lafayette's sports weekend starts Friday at 7 p.m. at Mackey Arena, where Purdue basketball hosts Oakland, and it ends Saturday at noon next door at Ross-Ade Stadium. For the football half, the Wisconsin vs Purdue spread is Wisconsin −5.5 and the over/under is 44.5 on DraftKings, and I'm on Wisconsin Badgers −5.5 and Over 44.5.

This is a pick where I'm against most of the room, so let me lay it out. Purdue has lost four straight and is 3-7. Wisconsin is 6-4 and bowl eligible. The Badgers allow 17.1 points a game, and Purdue allows 31.9. Wisconsin has won all eight meetings since 2016, including 52-6 in 2024.

Barnaby Wolcott-Reese, who draws every play on graph paper, has a fair counterargument. "Ryan Browne has 2,418 passing yards. Fame Ijeboi has 10 rushing scores. We lost to Wake Forest by two in overtime and to Maryland by five." Purdue scores 27.2 a game, and Asaad Waseem has 802 receiving yards.

Lars "Brat" Ellefson knows his team's weakness too. Wisconsin's offense has been streaky. Colton Joseph led the Badgers in throws for most of the year, and Ryan Hopkins has thrown the most passes the last two weeks, with three touchdowns against Rutgers and 77 yards at Maryland. But Wisconsin doesn't need a big throwing day here. Cooper Catalano has 99 tackles and Sebastian Cheeks has seven sacks, and they face a Purdue team that has scored seven and 17 in two of its last three games.

DraftKings opened Wisconsin −6 with a 44.5 total. The side ticked down half a point and the total hasn't moved.

My final is Wisconsin Badgers 27, Purdue Boilermakers 21. Wisconsin wins by six and clears the 5.5. The 48 combined points clear 44.5. Purdue's defense gives up enough for Wisconsin's running game to find the end zone three times, and Browne gets Purdue to 21 at home.

Here's where the room stands. Letdown Watch is with me on Wisconsin −5.5 at 27-19. The Formula takes Purdue +5.5 at 27-23 and likes the Over. Next Man Up takes Purdue +5.5 at 24-21, and In The Trenches likes Purdue +5.5 at 30-19, with no over/under call. The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch are all on the Over 44.5. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

In The Trenches: "Thirty to nineteen, and I'm on Purdue. Don't ask me to explain it to Letdown Watch. It can't count past eight straight."

Letdown Watch: "Eight straight wins in the series. Four straight Purdue losses. I counted fine."

The Formula: "It's a five-and-a-half-point line between a bowl team and a team with nothing to play for but pride. I'll take the points and the pride."

Pride matters, but Wisconsin's defense matters more. The Badgers grind out a bowl team's road win after Purdue's big basketball night.

Wisconsin Badgers 27, Purdue Boilermakers 21. Wisconsin Badgers cover the 5.5. Over 44.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Purdue fans get a doubleheader this weekend: Purdue basketball hosts Oakland at Mackey Arena on Friday night, and 17 hours after tipoff Wisconsin vs Purdue kicks off next door at Ross-Ade Stadium in the home finale. Purdue insider Barnaby Wolcott-Reese plans to do both on about five hours of sleep, and Wisconsin insider Lars "Brat" Ellefson says the Badgers came to West Lafayette to make sure Saturday is the quieter of the two nights.

Barnaby: Lars, this is a basketball school that happens to have a football stadium across the parking lot. Friday we fill Mackey. Saturday we walk over and finish the football season at home. I've drawn the walk on graph paper, shortcut through the grass included.

Lars: Barnaby, I've got a polka for every step. Wisconsin travels well. We'll bring the band in our heads and the cheese in our coats.

Here's what makes this matchup tricky to talk about. Neither team has been at its best lately. Purdue has lost four straight, to Washington, Penn State, Maryland and Iowa, and it's 3-7. Wisconsin is 6-4 and already bowl eligible, but it lost 24-21 at Maryland last Saturday and has spent the season with an offense that comes and goes.

Barnaby: Our losing run has a lot of near misses in it. We lost to Wake Forest in overtime by two. We lost to Maryland by five. Ryan Browne has thrown for 2,418 yards. Fame Ijeboi has 684 rushing yards and ten scores. We move the ball. We just need the last ten yards to cooperate.

Lars: You move it, sure. Then you give up 31.9 a game. Our defense allows 17.1. You can't engineer your way around that, Barnaby, no matter how many pencils you've got in that pocket protector.

Wisconsin's defense is the reason Lars sleeps at night. Cooper Catalano has 99 tackles, and Sebastian Cheeks has seven sacks. Iowa shut out the Badgers 30-0 and UCLA held them to seven, but Wisconsin's defense has also carried it through wins at Penn State and over USC.

Lars: Catalano doesn't tackle you. He files a claim on you. Ninety-nine tackles, Barnaby. That's a dairy herd's worth of stops.

Barnaby: And Asaad Waseem has 802 receiving yards for us. He catches it, and then your secondary goes to find him. Jojo Hayden has 77 tackles on our side, and he hits like a cooling tower falling over.

The quarterback picture on Wisconsin's side has shifted. Colton Joseph led the Badgers in throws most of the season, with 1,368 yards and 11 touchdowns. The last two weeks, Ryan Hopkins has thrown the most passes, throwing three touchdowns in a 31-10 win over Rutgers and then struggling at Maryland, where he went 11 of 22 for 77 yards.

Lars: Hopkins was great against Rutgers. Maryland was a hiccup. Darrion Dupree ran for two scores in that game. We'll run it more Saturday. It's November. In November, Wisconsin hands it off and dares you to stop us.

Barnaby: You'll hand it off into Ross-Ade with a crowd that just came off a basketball high. I'll ring my train bell every time Ijeboi gets loose.

Lars: Your train bell is going to be very lonely.

There's history here, and it isn't kind to Barnaby. Wisconsin has won all eight meetings since 2016, including a 52-6 game in 2024 and a 47-44 thriller in 2018. Purdue fans remember that last one. They'd rather not.

Barnaby: Eight is a lot. I know. But we beat Minnesota 41-13 this year. We beat Illinois on the road. This team can play. It just needs somebody to tell it the season isn't over until the last whistle at home.

Lars: I'll tell them myself. Then I'll beat them.

The football weekend ends at Ross-Ade, and Barnaby wants the band, the train and the seniors to get one more happy afternoon in West Lafayette. Lars wants a bowl team to look like one on the road.

Barnaby: Boiler up. I'm engineering a comeback.

Lars: Engineer whatever you want. We'll be running the same play twelve times.

Two nights in a row of noise on the Purdue side of campus, and the Badgers grind out the second one.

My call: Wisconsin Badgers 27, Purdue Boilermakers 21.

display.story_text:
A rested Army team at home against a road team that has won three straight by a combined 12 points is the whole East Carolina vs Army handicap. DraftKings has Army −6 and a 44.5 total. Army Black Knights −6 and Over 44.5 are my pick for the Black Knights' final home game at Michie Stadium.

Saturday is a full house of causes at West Point: Senior Day for the academy's senior class, Military Appreciation Day, Youth Football Day and Scout Day, with scouts spending the day with cadets from the academy's Scoutmaster's Council. Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke calls it the best classroom on the Hudson. For this handicap, what matters is that Army had last Saturday off after a 24-21 loss to Air Force, and it has had two weeks to get ready for East Carolina.

Bart Quidley has the Pirates' case. "Three straight wins. Temple 17-9, South Florida 20-17, Charlotte 17-16." That's real, and it's also the problem. East Carolina scores 22.9 points a game, and those three wins came by eight, three and one. The Pirates have split their quarterback work between Emory Williams and Mitch Griffis, and Williams threw two interceptions at Charlotte.

Army's offense is Cale Hellums, with 908 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns. The Black Knights score 32.2 a game and have topped 30 at home twice this year. When Army gets a lead, it runs the ball and keeps it.

DraftKings opened Army −4.5 with a 42.5 total, and both numbers have climbed. The total moved two points and the side moved a point and a half. I'm still on both.

My final is Army Black Knights 28, East Carolina Pirates 21. Army wins by seven and clears the 6. The 49 combined points clear 44.5. TJ Engleman Jr. has 695 rushing yards for East Carolina, and Army allows 25.3 a game, so the Pirates get their 21. Hellums gets Army to 28.

The room tilts toward Army, with one dissent. Next Man Up likes Army −6 at 29-17, and Letdown Watch takes Army −6 at 28-21. The Formula takes East Carolina +6 at 27-24. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call. On the total, The Formula and Letdown Watch both like the Over 44.5, and Next Man Up goes Over too. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

The Formula: "Three straight one-score wins for East Carolina. Some of you call that luck. I call it a team that keeps it close."

Next Man Up: "I call it a team that scored 17 in two of them. Army runs for more than that by halftime."

Letdown Watch: "Twenty-eight to twenty-one. Same as the Cover Writer. Somebody note that I'm finally agreeing with somebody."

Scouts are coming to West Point on Saturday, and the ones who show up for East Carolina vs Army get to spend the day with cadets from the academy's Scoutmaster's Council and leave with an Army Football Scout Day patch. Army insider Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke says Michie Stadium's final home game of the year, with Youth Football Day, Military Appreciation Day and the Class of 2027 Senior Day all on one ticket, is the best classroom on the Hudson, while East Carolina insider Bart Quidley says the Pirates are sailing up from Greenville to teach a lesson of their own.

Rourke: Quidley, I want you to picture it. Kids in their scout uniforms, cadets showing them how this place works, youth football players in the stands, and the seniors who'll be commissioned in the spring walking out for their last home game. That's not a promotion. That's a mission statement.

Bart: Captain, I'm moved. I really am. I'll be wearing my tricorn hat, so the scouts will have something to talk about at the next meeting, too.

There's a football game in the middle of all that, and it's a good one. East Carolina comes in at 6-4 and riding three straight wins. None of them was pretty. The Pirates beat Temple 17-9, South Florida 20-17 and Charlotte 17-16 last Saturday, when Ashton Gray ran 24 times for 88 yards and two scores.

Bart: Ugly wins are still wins, Captain. You don't hang the scoreboard in a museum. You hang the flag. Three in a row, hoist the colors.

Rourke: And Army is coming off a week of rest. We lost to Air Force 24-21 on Nov. 7. That one stung. We had a bye last Saturday, and a rested Army team is an organized Army team.

Army's offense starts and ends with Cale Hellums, and anybody who's watched this team knows it. Hellums has 908 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns. He's thrown just 86 times all year. The Black Knights run, run again, then run somewhere else.

Bart: Eighteen rushing scores is a lot, Captain. I respect a quarterback who runs like he's late for formation. But Crews Law has 64 tackles for us, and our defense gives up 22.6 a game.

Rourke: Elijah Walton has 60 for us. Victor Afolabi has three sacks, and we don't even throw it enough to know what a sack feels like from the other side.

East Carolina's side of the ball is a little harder to pin down. The Pirates have gone back and forth between two quarterbacks, Emory Williams and Mitch Griffis, for most of the season. Williams has thrown for 1,034 yards and nine touchdowns. TJ Engleman Jr. leads the Pirates with 695 rushing yards, and Ray Ray Joseph Jr. is the top receiver.

Bart: Two quarterbacks means two plans, Captain. You'll be ready for one of them.

Rourke: We'll be ready for whichever one is holding the ball when our linebackers arrive.

The history here is short and split. Army won 45-28 at Michie in 2024. East Carolina won 28-6 in Greenville last September. Each side won at home, and the scouts in the stands won't care about either one.

Bart: That 28-6 game was a fine night in Greenville. I'll tell the scouts about it. It has a moral.

Rourke: The moral is to win at home. We intend to.

The weather will be November on the Hudson, and Army will run it until somebody makes it stop. For East Carolina, the plan is to make the game long enough to matter in the fourth quarter. The Pirates have won three close games in a row. They know how to stay in one.

Rourke: Our seniors walk out on Saturday knowing they've still got a December game left on the calendar against the team that matters most. But first, they finish at Michie. Copy that, and beat Navy.

Bart: Even when you're playing us, Captain?

Rourke: Especially then. It's a habit.

The scouts go home with their patches, the young football players go home with stories, and the seniors go out the way cadets do: on schedule and in order.

My call: Army Black Knights 28, East Carolina Pirates 21.

The Naval Academy Masqueraders close "Poe's Dark Carnival of Tales" in Mahan Hall on Saturday night, and the scariest story in Annapolis that afternoon may be a 67.5 total. The Memphis vs Navy spread is Memphis −3.5 at DraftKings, and my pick is Memphis Tigers −3.5 and Under 67.5.

The Tigers score 39.0 points a game, Marcus Stokes has 28 touchdown throws, and they just won 52-41 at South Florida. But Navy is the opponent, and Navy plays with the clock.

Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather explains it in nautical terms. "Jackson Gutierrez ran 30 times for 180 yards and five touchdowns against Temple. We hand it to him until you stop him." Gutierrez has 1,159 rushing yards and 18 rushing scores. Navy builds long drives, and long drives mean fewer possessions for Stokes. Navy also had last week off, so the Mids get two weeks to prepare.

That's why I'm Under. Memphis will get its points, but not as many as usual, because it won't have the ball enough. Navy allows 30.4 a game, and I expect Memphis in the low 30s.

Otis Delaney-Crum hears all that and points to the side. "Four straight wins. Jaylin Carter has 1,038 rushing yards. Jemyri Davis caught five balls for 161 at South Florida." Memphis is 8-2. Navy is 3-6 and lost to Florida Atlantic, UAB, Air Force, UTSA, North Texas and Notre Dame. Navy did win the last two meetings, 56-44 and 28-17, but this Memphis team is better than either of those.

display.fanatic_story:
Saturday night in Mahan Hall, the Naval Academy Masqueraders close their run of "Poe's Dark Carnival of Tales," a steampunk carnival where the audience shouts for the most terrifying Edgar Allan Poe story of the night. Eight hours earlier, Memphis vs Navy kicks off at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, and Navy insider Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather says Jackson Gutierrez is the scariest tale in Annapolis, while Memphis insider Otis Delaney-Crum says Marcus Stokes and an 8-2 Tigers team came up the Chesapeake to write their own ending.

Annabel: Otis, our midshipmen put on Poe in costume, then they go to class Monday and learn to navigate a destroyer. That's the Academy. We do the dramatic and the practical in the same week. Steady as she goes.

Otis: Commander, I'm from Memphis. We invented dramatic. I'll come to the show Saturday night, but I'm bringing a guitar and a better ending.

The two have a lot to argue about. Memphis is 8-2 and has won four straight, the last of them a 52-41 shootout at South Florida on a Thursday night, Nov. 12. Stokes threw for 313 yards and three touchdowns, Jaylin Carter ran for 109 and two scores, and Jemyri Davis caught five balls for 161 yards. The Tigers score 39.0 points a game. Stokes has 28 touchdown throws and six interceptions.

Otis: That's not an offense, Commander. That's a horn section. Stokes is the trumpet, Carter is the bass, and Davis is the solo nobody saw coming. That drive had a backbeat, and so did the next one, and so did the next one.

Annabel: A horn section sounds great on Beale Street. Here, we play a different instrument. It's called the clock.

Navy's instrument is Gutierrez, and he plays it loud. The quarterback has 1,159 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns. In Navy's last game, a 42-35 win over Temple on Nov. 7, he ran 30 times for 180 yards and five scores. Navy had last weekend off, so the Mids have had two weeks to get ready for Memphis.

Annabel: Five touchdowns, Otis. One afternoon. We hand it to him, we hand it to him again, and while your offense sits on the bench and watches, our offense sails on.

Otis: Your defense gives up 30.4 a game, Commander. Our offense won't sit on the bench long. Mike Montgomery has 86 tackles for us, and Elijah Kinsler has seven and a half sacks, and your quarterback is going to get very familiar with both of them.

Annabel: Coleman Cauley has 67 for us, and MarcAnthony Parker has four sacks. And Jordan Collins, our tight end, caught two balls for 112 yards against Temple. When we throw, we throw deep.

That's the Navy game plan in one sentence: run until the defense creeps up, then throw it over everybody's head. Collins has only eight catches all season, and they've gone for 324 yards.

The history is a funny one. Memphis has won six of the last ten meetings, but Navy has won the last two, 56-44 in Annapolis in 2024 and 28-17 in Memphis last November. Annabel has both dates written in the margin of her nautical charts.

Otis: Those were different Tigers. This group has been in a groove since October. We lost at Tulane and we answered with four wins.

Annabel: We've been in rough water all season, Otis. We're 3-6. I won't pretend otherwise. But rough water is where Navy trains. Our Mids don't lose their footing in front of the Brigade.

The game will be a test of patience. Memphis wants to score fast and often. Navy wants to make every possession last long enough for the stadium to sing twice.

Otis: Commander, by halftime, I'll have ranked your fight song on my soul scale and given it a seven.

Annabel: By halftime, you'll still be waiting for the ball.

The Masqueraders will ask their audience Saturday night to choose the most frightening Poe tale. Down at the stadium, Memphis will find its most frightening Navy story in Gutierrez, and the Tigers will survive it.

My call: Memphis Tigers 33, Navy Midshipmen 29.

DraftKings opened North Texas −13.5 at Tulane, and the number has nearly been cut in half since. The Mean Green are now North Texas Mean Green −6.5, the total sits at 57.5, and I'm still taking the road team. My pick is North Texas Mean Green −6.5 and Over 57.5.

The drop started with last Saturday in San Antonio. UTSA beat North Texas 35-16, and Tayven Jackson went 10 of 20 for 125 yards with an interception. That's one bad afternoon from a quarterback with 3,005 yards, 23 touchdowns and six interceptions this season. Before UTSA, the Mean Green scored 45, 50, 49, 48 and 52 in five straight games. They score 41.8 a game, and Jahiem White has 1,218 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns.

Grady Mayhew-Ochoa keeps time on it. "One missed beat. We've got Justin Stevenson with 937 receiving yards and Jahiem White in the backfield. Mean Green, baby."

Tulane is 5-5 and plays for bowl eligibility on Senior Day, and Twan Ducros-Labat says that matters. "We've beaten North Texas three straight times. 35-28, 45-37, 34-21. The Wave know this team." He's right about the series. He also has to explain 21.0 points a game, a 60-10 home loss to Tulsa on Nov. 7, and a 20-17 escape at Rice. Trace Johnson has 1,008 passing yards, three touchdowns and seven interceptions. That's not an offense built to chase 35.

That's the side. North Texas wins by nine, and Tulane's offense can't keep pace for four quarters.

The total works the same way. My final is North Texas Mean Green 35, Tulane Green Wave 26, which is 61 points. North Texas allows 31.3 a game, so Tulane can get into the 20s. Most of the scoring comes from the Mean Green, and 35 is about what they do on a normal day.

The room agrees on everything except the trenches. The Formula is North Texas −6.5 and Over 57.5 at 33-25. Next Man Up likes North Texas −6.5 and likes the Over at 36-27. Letdown Watch likes North Texas −6.5 and likes the Over at 35-25. In The Trenches calls the trenches even, so it has no side and no over/under call. Letdown Watch: "North Texas lost a road game last week. That's the letdown. This is the bounce back."

Next Man Up: "Tulane has scored 38 once all year, and it took overtime."

In The Trenches: "Nobody up front moves anybody. I'm watching."

display.fanatic_story:
The first 2,000 fans through the gates at Yulman Stadium on Saturday will get a doubloon, a commemorative coin from the Louisiana America 250 Commission, and Tulane insider Twan Ducros-Labat already knows where his is going. "In my trumpet case, next to the mouthpiece," he says. "For luck. We need it."

That's an honest Uptown admission. Tulane is 5-5. The Green Wave beat Rice 20-17 last Saturday, two weeks after Tulsa came into Yulman on Homecoming and won 60-10. One more win makes this team bowl eligible, and the chance comes on Senior Day, when Will Hall walks his seniors and their families onto the field before kickoff. The first 2,500 fans get a Tulane scarf, too, which is a lot of optimism for an 11 a.m. kickoff in New Orleans.

North Texas insider Grady Mayhew-Ochoa is bringing his drumsticks. Denton has one of the most famous college jazz programs in the country, and Grady has been waiting all season to play a New Orleans room.

"Twan, I've got the whole set list written," he says. "We open with Tayven Jackson. We close with Jahiem White. And somewhere in the middle, your defense gets lost in the solo. Mean Green, baby."

Grady has the material. North Texas is 7-3 and scores 41.8 points a game. Jackson has thrown for 3,005 yards with 23 touchdowns and six interceptions. White has run for 1,218 yards and 16 touchdowns. Justin Stevenson has 58 catches for 937 yards. In five straight games this fall, the Mean Green put up 45 at Tulsa, 50 on Charlotte, 49 at Navy, 48 on Florida Atlantic and 52 on Rice.

Then came last Saturday in San Antonio. UTSA won 35-16, and Jackson finished 10 of 20 for 125 yards with an interception. Grady doesn't hide from it.

"Everybody misses a beat," he says. "You don't quit the gig. You count it off again."

Twan isn't buying the drummer's calm. He rates every opponent by its gumbo, and he's been tasting this one all week.

"North Texas gumbo smells great from the street," he says. "Big roux, lots of spice. Then you get it to the table and the bottom of the bowl gives up 31.3 points a game. That's a nice-looking pot with no okra in it. I give it a six."

He has a point. North Texas has allowed 35 or more six times, including 49 at Texas State and 41 to Florida Atlantic. Tulane's problem is finding enough offense to take advantage. The Green Wave score 21.0 a game, and Trace Johnson has thrown for 1,008 yards with three touchdowns and seven interceptions since taking over the job. Johnnie Daniels leads the team with 542 rushing yards, and Destyn Hill has 41 catches for 489 yards.

"We don't win pretty this year," Twan says. "We win at Charlotte in overtime. We win by three at Rice. We beat Memphis 31-17 on a Friday night under the lights. This team plays ugly jazz, Grady. It still swings."

The Tulane defense has carried most of that. Dickson Agu has 96 tackles, and Ed Smith IV has four sacks. The Wave held Duke, South Alabama, Southern Miss, Army and Rice to 24 or fewer.

Then there's the history, and Twan brings it up before Grady can stop him. Tulane has won the last three meetings, 35-28 in 2023, 45-37 in 2024, and 34-21 last December, when the Green Wave went on to win the American Conference and reach the College Football Playoff.

"Three for three, baby," Twan says. "You came to our house in December and left without a trophy. Now you're back for an encore?"

"That was a different band," Grady says. "Different Tulane, too. We've got the best offense on the field Saturday by a lot."

North Texas has its own defensive names. Zakye Barker has 83 tackles, and Davion Rhodes has six and a half sacks. Johnson has been intercepted seven times, and Barker would happily make it eight.

Here's how I see the set playing out. Tulane will feed on Senior Day emotion early, and the doubloons will be flashing in the student section. Hall's team will make North Texas work for the first quarter. But the Mean Green have scored at least 44 seven times this season, and Tulane hasn't scored more than 38 all year. At some point, the Green Wave need to match touchdowns, and they don't have the horns to do it.

Twan will play the alma mater on the trumpet after the game anyway. Grady will tap along on the rail. Both of them will agree on one thing: whoever wrote this set list put North Texas at the end.

"Roll Wave!" Twan says, because he always does.

"Mean Green, baby," Grady says back.

My call: North Texas Mean Green 35, Tulane Green Wave 26.

DraftKings opened North Texas −13.5 at Tulane, and the number has nearly been cut in half since. The Mean Green are now North Texas Mean Green −6.5, the total sits at 57.5, and I'm still taking the road team. My pick is North Texas Mean Green −6.5 and Over 57.5.

The drop started with last Saturday in San Antonio. UTSA beat North Texas 35-16, and Tayven Jackson went 10 of 20 for 125 yards with an interception. That's one bad afternoon from a quarterback with 3,005 yards, 23 touchdowns and six interceptions this season. Before UTSA, the Mean Green scored 45, 50, 49, 48 and 52 in five straight games. They score 41.8 a game, and Jahiem White has 1,218 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns.

Grady Mayhew-Ochoa keeps time on it. "One missed beat. We've got Justin Stevenson with 937 receiving yards and Jahiem White in the backfield. Mean Green, baby."

Tulane is 5-5 and plays for bowl eligibility on Senior Day, and Twan Ducros-Labat says that matters. "We've beaten North Texas three straight times. 35-28, 45-37, 34-21. The Wave know this team." He's right about the series. He also has to explain 21.0 points a game, a 60-10 home loss to Tulsa on Nov. 7, and a 20-17 escape at Rice. Trace Johnson has 1,008 passing yards, three touchdowns and seven interceptions. That's not an offense built to chase 35.

That's the side. North Texas wins by nine, and Tulane's offense can't keep pace for four quarters.

The total works the same way. My final is North Texas Mean Green 35, Tulane Green Wave 26, which is 61 points. North Texas allows 31.3 a game, so Tulane can get into the 20s. Most of the scoring comes from the Mean Green, and 35 is about what they do on a normal day.

Next Man Up: "Tulane has scored 38 once all year, and it took overtime."

That's North Carolina. Seven of the Tar Heels' ten games have been decided by eight points or fewer, and they've won at Pitt 21-17 and at Duke 24-20. They've also lost 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime, 38-35 to Miami and 16-14 to Louisville. Billy Edwards Jr. has 2,247 passing yards, 18 touchdowns and six interceptions. Ainsley Pemberton puts it her way: "We've played Clemson, Notre Dame and Miami. Virginia played Norfolk State."

Prescott Ashby-Lowell isn't conceding a thing. "We just beat California 36-7. Beau Pribula has 15 touchdown passes and three interceptions. It's Senior Day on the Grounds." Fair. Virginia also lost 51-7 at Wake Forest and 38-7 at Florida State, and it scored 13 at SMU and 16 against Duke. When Virginia's offense stalls, it really stalls.

display.fanatic_story:
North Carolina and Virginia meet for the 131st time on Saturday, and Virginia's own release says that ties this for the second-most played rivalry between FBS opponents. They call it the South's Oldest Rivalry. This year, it might as well be called the South's Most Even Rivalry, because both teams arrive at Scott Stadium at 5-5, and the winner gets the sixth win that makes a team bowl eligible.

Virginia insider Prescott Ashby-Lowell adjusts his bow tie and points out that Mr. Jefferson would appreciate the symmetry. "Two schools, ten games each, five wins each," he says. "The Grounds will settle it. They usually do."

He says "the Grounds" on purpose. Prescott has never said the other word in his life and will not start for a visiting team.

North Carolina insider Ainsley Pemberton has a different read on the symmetry. "We're 5-5 against a schedule with Clemson, Notre Dame and Miami on it," she says. "Virginia went 5-5 by beating Norfolk State and Delaware. And yes, we beat Duke in Durham. I mention that every chance I get. It's the best thing that happened in October."

That's the second season of Bill Belichick in Chapel Hill, and it's been a season of close calls. The Tar Heels lost to Syracuse 31-30 in overtime and to Miami 38-35. Last Saturday, they lost to Louisville 16-14 at home. They also won at Pitt 21-17 and at Duke 24-20. Seven of their ten games were decided by eight points or fewer.

Billy Edwards Jr. has been steady through all of it. He's thrown for 2,247 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jordan Shipp leads the team with 57 catches for 703 yards. On defense, linebacker Derek McDonald has 100 tackles, and Xavier Lewis has seven sacks.

"Derek McDonald hits like a Duke fan's feelings after we leave Durham," Ainsley says. "Hard and often."

Virginia's season has come in waves. The Cavaliers started 3-1, then lost four of five, including a 51-7 loss at Wake Forest on Oct. 31. Then came last Saturday, when Virginia beat California 36-7 at home to snap a three-game skid. Beau Pribula has been efficient all year, with 1,727 passing yards, 15 touchdowns and only three interceptions. Da'Shawn Martin has seven touchdown catches, and Jekail Middlebrook leads the team with 540 rushing yards. Matthew Fobbs-White has five and a half sacks.

"Pribula makes good decisions," Prescott says. "Jefferson believed an educated citizenry was the foundation of the republic. Beau believes in throwing it to the open man. Same principle."

The history is a coin flip. Virginia has won six of the last ten meetings, but those games swing wildly. North Carolina won 59-39 in 2021 and 41-14 here two years ago. Virginia won 44-41 in 2020 and 17-16 in Chapel Hill last October. Prescott remembers the one-point game the best.

"Seventeen to sixteen," he says. "A gentleman's margin."

"A lucky margin," Ainsley says. "We'll take this one by a field goal and drive home before the traffic."

Saturday is also Virginia's home finale and Senior Day, and Prescott wants the Cavaliers' upperclassmen to leave the Grounds with something to remember. A bowl trip would do it. So would beating North Carolina in the 131st meeting.

Here's the matchup. North Carolina allows 22.1 points a game. Virginia allows 21.5. North Carolina scores 25.8. Virginia scores 26.9. Those numbers are close enough to be a Jefferson riddle. The difference may be up front. Lewis and Fobbs-White could each decide a series, and Pribula and Edwards have both been careful with the ball, so a single turnover could be the whole game.

Ainsley has her worries. Edwards went 10 of 14 for 120 yards in the Louisville loss, and the Tar Heels managed only 14 points. "We need the Miami Billy, not the Louisville Billy," she says. "Miami Billy threw four touchdowns."

Prescott has his own worry, and it's Wake Forest. "When this team loses, it doesn't lose politely," he says. "We gave up 51 in Winston-Salem. We gave up 38 in Tallahassee. I'd prefer not to discuss either."

I think this is a one-score game into the fourth quarter, with both offenses doing just enough. Virginia has the home crowd, the seniors and the better rhythm after the Cal win. North Carolina has the tougher résumé and a quarterback who's played in a lot of tight finishes this fall.

Ainsley will probably spend the last five minutes roasting Duke for comfort. Prescott will straighten his bow tie and hum the Good Old Song. One of them will go home with a bowl game. The other will have to wait a year to even things out.

My call: Virginia Cavaliers 23, North Carolina Tar Heels 22.

display.story_text:
West Virginia scores 34.9 a game and allows 34.8, and the over/under on Houston at West Virginia is 70.5. I think that number is a little too high, and I think Houston −7.5 is too many points. My pick is West Virginia Mountaineers +7.5 and Under 70.5.

DraftKings opened Houston −7 and 71.5. The side has barely moved, and the total has dropped a point. I'd have taken the points at either number.

Start with Houston, because the Cougars are the better team. They're 7-3 and ranked No. 14, and Conner Weigman has 2,552 passing yards, 25 touchdowns and three interceptions. Amare Thomas has 764 receiving yards and nine touchdowns. Yo Pacheco says the ship is ready: "We beat Oklahoma State, Kansas State and Cincinnati. Boulder was one bad launch."

But that bad launch is part of a pattern. Houston lost 42-32 at Colorado, 21-13 at Utah and 28-26 at Texas Tech, and all three came on the road. The Cougars' 31-24 home win over Cincinnati and 35-32 home win over Oklahoma State weren't blowouts either. A seven-point road number is plenty for a team that has lost three of its five road games.

Jolene Buckhannon has the West Virginia case, and it starts with Cam Cook. "1,084 yards. Eight touchdowns. He keeps their quarterback on the bench." Cook gives West Virginia a way to shorten the game, and Michael Hawkins Jr. has only three interceptions. It's Senior Day in Morgantown, and the Mountaineers are 5-5 with a bowl trip on the line. They lost 37-14 to Kansas last week, but they've beaten Cincinnati and TCU this year.

My final is Houston Cougars 34, West Virginia Mountaineers 28. Houston wins by six, and West Virginia covers the 7.5. The 62 combined points stay under 70.5, because Cook's runs keep the clock moving and Houston's defense, allowing 23.4 a game, holds West Virginia under its usual output.

The room splits right down the middle on the side. The Formula is West Virginia +7.5 at 33-26 and likes the Under 70.5. Next Man Up is Houston −7.5 at 40-31 and Under 70.5. Letdown Watch is West Virginia +7.5 at 33-27 and likes the Under 70.5. In The Trenches likes Houston −7.5 at 29-26 and has no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Houston just lost in Boulder. Now it's an early kick in Morgantown. Bad combination."

In The Trenches: "Houston wins up front. West Virginia wins the scoreboard math."

The Formula: "Houston by seven is fine. Houston by seven and a half is a hook too far."

Gold and Blue Gratitude day ends with a close loss, and the points get West Virginia home.

display.fanatic_story:
West Virginia is calling Saturday "Gold and Blue Gratitude," a thank-you to Mountaineer fans for sticking with the team all season, and the school says more than 1,000 ticket holders will get a fan experience or a giveaway at Milan Puskar Stadium. It's also Senior Day and the last home game of the year. Jolene Buckhannon has her own way of saying thanks. She's bringing a cooler of pepperoni rolls to the tailgate, and she's keeping count.

"One roll for every Mountaineer touchdown," she says. "I've eaten a lot of pepperoni rolls this year. Load up, I don't miss."

She isn't exaggerating. West Virginia scores 34.9 points a game. It also allows 34.8, which is how a team with that much offense ends up 5-5. The Mountaineers scored 48 at Texas Tech and lost. They scored 42 at Iowa State and lost. They scored 45 against Cincinnati and won by three, on a day Michael Hawkins Jr. threw for 464 yards.

Houston insider Yo Pacheco has heard the stories. He's flying in with a No. 14 ranking and, as he puts it, "a fully fueled launch vehicle."

"Houston, we have a quarterback," Yo says. "Conner Weigman has 25 touchdown passes and three interceptions. That's not a passer. That's mission control."

The numbers back Yo up. Houston is 7-3. Weigman has thrown for 2,552 yards, and Amare Thomas has 53 catches for 764 yards and nine touchdowns. Makhi Hughes leads the backfield with 712 rushing yards. The Cougars score 35.1 and allow 23.4, and they've beaten Oklahoma State, Kansas State, UCF and Cincinnati.

But Yo's rocket has had some trouble on reentry. Houston lost 42-32 at Colorado last Friday night. It lost 21-13 at Utah in October and 28-26 at Texas Tech in September. All three losses came on the road.

"We had a small anomaly in Boulder," Yo says. "A very small one. Ten points. The crew has reviewed the data and corrected course."

Jolene laughed at "anomaly" for a full minute.

West Virginia's own trip to the launch pad didn't go well last week. Kansas came into Morgantown and won 37-14. Hawkins was 19 of 34 for 227 yards, and the Mountaineers never found their usual rhythm. Rich Rodriguez's team now needs one more win for a bowl trip, with Houston at home and a Friday night trip to Utah left.

"Kansas was a bad day," Jolene says. "I ate two rolls. Two. I haven't eaten that few since September."

Her case for Saturday is Cam Cook. The running back has 1,084 yards and eight touchdowns, and he's the reason West Virginia can stay on the field long enough to keep Weigman on the sideline. DJ Epps is the big-play threat, with 615 yards on only 28 catches. Isaiah Patterson leads the defense with 65 tackles and three sacks.

"Cam Cook runs like he's late for a shift at the mine," Jolene says. "He gets where he's going."

Yo has a rebuttal for that, too. "Kentrell Webb has 59 tackles for us, and Ashton Porter's got three sacks. And remember, we've played Texas Tech too. We lost by two in Lubbock. You lost by five. In orbital mechanics, that's called a rounding error."

The teams have met twice in recent years, and they've split. The Cougars won 41-39 in 2023, and West Virginia won 45-35 last November. Both games were the kind of shootouts Jolene likes.

"Two shootouts," she says. "If you're keeping score at home, that's a lot of pepperoni rolls."

Here's where I land. Houston is the better team, with the better quarterback and the better defense. Weigman has three interceptions all year, and a West Virginia defense allowing 34.8 a game isn't likely to force many more. But the Mountaineers will have a lot of emotion on Senior Day, and Cook can make this a long afternoon of handoffs. I think West Virginia keeps it close into the fourth quarter before Houston pulls away.

Yo will probably call it a successful splashdown. Jolene will count her rolls, find four of them gone, and say it could have been worse.

"Gold and Blue Gratitude," she says. "I'm grateful we're still in it in November."

My call: Houston Cougars 34, West Virginia Mountaineers 28.

display.fanatic_story:
Liberty is calling Saturday Employee Appreciation Day, which means the people who keep Williams Stadium running, from the ticket windows to the concession stands, get their turn to be thanked. Liberty insider Gideon Fairweather wants to add one more group to the list. "The bus drivers," he says. "Nobody ever thanks the bus drivers."

Gideon rates every team bus that pulls into Lynchburg, and he's been waiting for this one. Western Kentucky has made a long trip this fall. The Hilltoppers have played at Nevada, Georgia, Indiana, New Mexico State, Sam Houston and Middle Tennessee.

"That bus has earned a nine," Gideon says. "The team inside it, I'll pray for. I pray for both teams every Saturday. This week, I'll pray a little longer for the visitors."

Western Kentucky insider Tops Whitsitt hears that and drapes his red towel over his shoulder. Tops cuts hair in Bowling Green, and he's been listening to customers argue about this season since August.

"Pray all you want, Gideon," Tops says. "We just beat Jacksonville State 34-24. We beat Sam Houston on the road and gave up three points. We're sweeping up."

That's the Western Kentucky story in a nutshell. The Hilltoppers are 4-6 and they've had a rough fall, but there have been good afternoons mixed in with the bad ones. They lost 70-20 at Georgia and 38-0 at Indiana in September. They also beat Missouri State 34-13 and won 16-3 at Sam Houston in October. Last week, they beat Jacksonville State by ten.

Brock Glenn has done a little of everything. He's thrown for 1,121 yards and eight touchdowns and run for 604 yards and eight more. Rodney Tisdale Jr. has played quarterback too, going 14 of 16 against Jacksonville State. Jonathan Stafford Jr. leads the receivers with 56 catches. Jaylen Lewis has 70 tackles.

"Two quarterbacks, one haircut," Tops says. "Fresh cut on both sides, nice and even."

Liberty doesn't need two of anything. The Flames are 9-1, and their only loss came on opening day at James Madison, 20-13. They've won nine straight since then, and they've allowed 14.5 points a game. That's a defense that held Sam Houston to three, Kennesaw State to six and FIU to ten.

Deshawn Purdie runs the offense, and he's barely made a mistake. He's thrown for 1,769 yards with 12 touchdowns and one interception. Kam Davis has 792 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Makai Jackson has 752 receiving yards on 40 catches. Brenton Williams has six sacks from the secondary, and Derrell Farrar leads the team with 56 tackles.

"Purdie has thrown one interception all season," Gideon says. "One. I've had more flat tires on the way to church."

Last Saturday wasn't easy. Middle Tennessee came to Lynchburg and stayed close, and Liberty won 28-23 on a day Purdie threw for only 64 yards. Kam Davis carried the load with 126 rushing yards. Gideon calls that kind of win a test of faith.

"You win the hard ones and you say thank you," he says. "Then you go home and watch the tape."

The history is all Liberty. The Flames are 5-0 against Western Kentucky, going back to a 23-14 win in 1996. The three most recent meetings went 30-24, 42-29 and 38-21, and Liberty won all three. Tops has an answer for that, too.

"Five haircuts in a row, and Liberty's never once tipped the barber," he says. "We'll get the tip this time."

Senior Day is part of Saturday, too, and Liberty's seniors walk out with a chance at a tenth win. After this one, the Flames finish at Missouri State and then hope to play for the Conference USA title on Dec. 4.

Here's how I see it. Western Kentucky's defense allows 32.4 a game, and the Hilltoppers have given up 49, 70 and 51 in their worst afternoons. Liberty doesn't need many points to win with its defense, but Davis and Purdie should find plenty. Western Kentucky's two-quarterback approach may keep things interesting for a quarter. After that, Liberty's defense takes over.

Gideon will stand for the halftime show when the marching band plays toward the west side. Tops will sweep the floor of his shop on Monday and tell everyone about the road trip. One of them will be very happy.

"Good game, Tops," Gideon will say. "I'll pray for your bus on the way home."

My call: Liberty Flames 36, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 16.
