Tulsa just scored 60 at Tulane and 38 against Florida Atlantic, and now it gets a 1-9 Charlotte team on Senior Day. That's why I'll lay the big number in Tulsa vs Charlotte. My pick is Tulsa Golden Hurricane −22.5 and Over 52.5.

DraftKings opened Tulsa −20.5, and the side has moved two points toward the Golden Hurricane. The total hasn't moved off 52.5. I agree with the side move, and I think the total is a little low.

Start with Tulsa's offense. Baylor Hayes has 1,990 passing yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions, and he's thrown for 338 and 309 yards in the last two games. Oran Singleton Jr. has 775 receiving yards, and Damari Alston has eight rushing touchdowns. Tulsa scores 33.6 a game. Wiley Pettibone calls it a gusher: "Sixty in New Orleans. Thirty-eight on Homecoming. The well's flowing."

Charlotte has to stop that, and it hasn't stopped much. The 49ers allow 36.2 a game. They gave up 59 to Memphis, 50 to North Texas, 41 to Ole Miss and 34 to Louisiana. Priya Halloran knows the risk: "We've been close lately. One point to East Carolina. Overtime with Tulane. But the defense is a bad loan." Charlotte scores 19.3 a game, and Conner Harrell has 1,167 passing yards with seven touchdowns.

The close losses are real, but Tulsa is a big step up. The Golden Hurricane allow 22.6 a game, Kyran Duhon has seven and a half sacks, and Chris Thompson Jr. has 93 tackles. Their only losses came to Arkansas, Navy, Army and North Texas, and two of those were by a field goal or less.

My final is Tulsa Golden Hurricane 38, Charlotte 49ers 15. Tulsa wins by 23 and covers the 22.5. The 53 combined points go Over 52.5. It's close, but Tulsa does most of the work on the scoreboard, and Charlotte should find a couple of scores against a team that's playing for its seniors.

The room is split on the side. The Formula takes Charlotte +22.5 at 37-17 and is Over 52.5. Next Man Up likes Tulsa −22.5 at 40-14 and is Over 52.5. Letdown Watch takes Tulsa −22.5 at 38-15 and is Over 52.5. In The Trenches calls the trenches even, so it has no side and no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

The Formula: "Twenty points is my margin. Charlotte keeps it under the number."

Next Man Up: "Twenty-six points. Tulsa's offense has scored that many all by itself lately."

Letdown Watch: "Senior Day after two big wins. Tulsa won't relax."

Band Day at Chapman brings the noise, and Tulsa brings the points.

display.fanatic_story:
Somewhere around Tulsa this week, a high school trombone player is practicing the Tulsa fight song. Saturday is Band Day at H.A. Chapman Stadium, when local student musicians join the Sound of the Golden Hurricane, and it's also Tulsa's Senior Day Celebration and the last home game of the year. Tulsa insider Wiley Pettibone calls it a full derrick. "Seniors, a band twice its normal size and a team that's finally pumping," he says. "That's a gusher of an afternoon."

Charlotte insider Priya Halloran has a different job. She looks at football the way a loan officer looks at an application, and she's been reviewing Charlotte's file all week.

"Credit history: poor," she says. "One win in ten. But the recent payments have been close. We lost by one to East Carolina last Saturday. We lost to Tulane in overtime. I'd call that a borrower who's trying."

Priya isn't wrong. Charlotte is 1-9, but two of its last three games have been one-score losses, 38-31 in overtime to Tulane and 17-16 to East Carolina, with a 23-12 loss at UAB in between. The 49ers' only win came at Temple, 38-31, the week Conner Harrell threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Harrell has 1,167 passing yards with seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Jaden Barnes has 59 catches, and Henry Rutledge leads the team with 520 rushing yards. Gavin Willis has 86 tackles, and Collin Gill has four sacks.

"Gavin Willis is my collateral," Priya says. "Every time someone runs at him, the bank gets something back."

Wiley spent the week watching Tulsa tape, and he liked what came up out of the ground. The Golden Hurricane are 6-4 and have won two straight in a big way. They went to New Orleans and beat Tulane 60-10. Then they came home for Homecoming and beat Florida Atlantic 38-21. Baylor Hayes threw for 338 yards and four touchdowns at Tulane and 309 more against FAU.

"Two gushers in a row," Wiley says. "I haven't seen oil come up like that since my granddaddy's lease."

Hayes has thrown for 1,990 yards with 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. Oran Singleton Jr. leads the receivers with 63 catches for 775 yards and seven touchdowns. Damari Alston has 573 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. On defense, Kyran Duhon has seven and a half sacks, and Chris Thompson Jr. has 93 tackles.

Priya looks at Tulsa's file with professional respect. "Strong income. Steady cash flow. Some old bad debt, though. You lost to Army, North Texas and Navy. That's three close ones."

Wiley doesn't flinch. "We lost to North Texas in overtime by one. We lost to Army by three. Those are dry wells, I'll grant you. But we drilled two new ones since and struck both times."

Tulsa has also beaten Oklahoma State, 24-10, in the season opener. That's the kind of win that makes a Tulsa fan forget about the dry wells.

There is one thing in Charlotte's file that Priya likes to point at. The last time these teams met, in 2023, Charlotte won 33-26.

"Last meeting, we won," she says. "I'd call that a clean repayment history."

"One game, three years ago," Wiley says. "That's not a history. That's a sample."

The difference on Saturday is in the numbers Priya can't explain away. Charlotte allows 36.2 points a game and scores 19.3. Tulsa scores 33.6 and allows 22.6. Charlotte gave up 59 to Memphis, 50 to North Texas and 41 to Ole Miss. Tulsa's offense has been running at full pressure for two weeks.

Priya's best hope is that her 49ers keep playing the close games they've played lately. Charlotte's defense held UAB and East Carolina to 23 and 17. If Charlotte can keep Tulsa's drives long and slow, the afternoon gets interesting.

I don't think that happens. Tulsa's seniors will want a big send-off, Hayes has been sharp, and the Band Day crowd will be loud. Charlotte will get a couple of scores and may hang around for a half. Then Tulsa's offense hits another gusher.

Wiley will tip his hat to the high school band on the way out. Priya will close the file and mark it "under review." She's never fully given up on a borrower.

"Next year," she says. "Next year, the terms improve."

My call: Tulsa Golden Hurricane 38, Charlotte 49ers 15.

Jacksonville State has won seven of its last nine, and it's home against a Missouri State team that allows 29.1 points a game. The Missouri State vs Jacksonville State spread is Jacksonville State −10.5, the total is 52.5, and I'm laying it. My pick is Jacksonville State Gamecocks −10.5 and Under 52.5.

DraftKings opened Jax State −10.5 and 53.5. The side hasn't moved, and the total has come down a point. That's the market agreeing with both halves of this pick.

The case for the Gamecocks starts with Caden Creel. He has 2,151 passing yards, 17 touchdowns and 817 rushing yards. Jax State allows only 20.7 a game, and it's beaten Sam Houston 47-14 and Eastern Kentucky 49-7 at AmFirst Stadium. Burl Ashcraft-Neeley, in his red apron, puts it simply. "At home, we cook. Missouri State hasn't seen our smoker yet."

The concern is that Jax State plays a lot of close games. It beat Georgia Southern by four, Kennesaw State by one and FIU by three, and it lost 34-24 at Western Kentucky last week. That's why this isn't a bigger number.

Clementine Bilyeu has the Missouri State case. "Isaiah Myers has 1,030 receiving yards. Jared Lloyd has 117 tackles. We just won in overtime." The Bears are 4-6 and beat New Mexico State 27-21 in overtime last Saturday. But Missouri State has scored 24 or fewer in seven of its ten games, and Henry Belin IV has nine touchdown passes and six interceptions. The Bears lost 50-0 at Texas A&M, 34-13 at Western Kentucky and 34-24 at SMU on the road.

Here's my comparison. Both teams played at Western Kentucky. Jax State lost by ten, and Missouri State lost by 21. Both beat Sam Houston. Jax State won by 33, and Missouri State won by 21.

My final is Jacksonville State Gamecocks 32, Missouri State Bears 20. Jax State wins by 12 and covers the 10.5. The 52 combined points stay under 52.5, because Missouri State's offense doesn't do enough against this defense.

Jacksonville State has a name for Saturday's game against Missouri State: Southerners Reunion. Alumni of the Marching Southerners, Jax State's marching band, come home to AmFirst Stadium, and Jax State insider Burl Ashcraft-Neeley is planning to feed as many of them as his smoker can handle.

"Old band folks are hungry folks," Burl says, tying on his red apron. "I've got four briskets going and a pan of beans the size of a tuba. Reunion means feeding people."

It's also a first. Jax State's own schedule release calls this the first meeting between these programs, and it's Senior Day in Jacksonville. Missouri State insider Clementine Bilyeu is driving down from the Ozarks with a canoe paddle in the back seat, because she brings it everywhere.

"New water," Clementine says. "I've never paddled this creek before. You read the current, you watch for rocks and you don't panic."

Here's the current she's reading. Jacksonville State is 7-3. The Gamecocks lost 34-24 at Western Kentucky last Saturday, which stung, but they'd won seven of eight before that. Caden Creel does almost everything for them. He's thrown for 2,151 yards with 17 touchdowns and run for 817 more. Deondre Johnson has 592 receiving yards on just 28 catches. On defense, safety Caleb Nix leads the team with 65 tackles, and Tae Floyd has three and a half sacks. The Gamecocks allow 20.7 points a game.

"Creel's like good bark on a brisket," Burl says. "It takes time to build, and once it's there, it's the best part of the whole thing."

Burl's team has a habit of making things close, though. Jax State beat Georgia Southern 31-27, Kennesaw State 27-26 and FIU 27-24. It lost at Ohio 29-27 in overtime. When the Gamecocks win big, it's usually at home, like the 47-14 Homecoming win over Sam Houston on Nov. 7 and the 49-7 win over Eastern Kentucky.

"We cook low and slow most weeks," Burl says. "Some weeks we just turn up the heat."

Clementine's Bears are 4-6, and they've had some rough water. They lost 50-0 at Texas A&M and 61-38 at Delaware. But they've won two of their last three, including last Saturday's 27-21 overtime win over New Mexico State. They also beat Sam Houston 24-3 and Kennesaw State 24-21.

Henry Belin IV has taken most of the snaps since mid-October. He's thrown for 1,489 yards with nine touchdowns and six interceptions. His top target is the reason Clementine drives so far. Isaiah Myers has 51 catches for 1,030 yards and eight touchdowns.

"Isaiah Myers is a spring-fed creek," Clementine says. "It doesn't matter how dry the summer gets. He keeps running."

Missouri State's defense starts with Jared Lloyd. The linebacker has 117 tackles, more than anyone on either roster. Tim Brantley Jr. has four sacks. The Bears allow 29.1 a game, and Burl keeps pointing at that figure with his tongs.

"Twenty-nine a game," he says. "You can't give that up to Creel. He'll carve you like a brisket on the cutting board."

The two programs do share some opponents, which helps. Both beat Sam Houston, Jax State by 33 and Missouri State by 21. Both played Western Kentucky on the road and lost, Jax State by ten and Missouri State by 21. Both beat Kennesaw State, each by a field goal or less. Missouri State lost a close one at FIU, 23-20. Jax State beat FIU at home, 27-24.

"Same rivers," Clementine says. "Different boats."

Here's how I see it. Jacksonville State is the better team, and it's playing at home on Senior Day with a reunion crowd in the stands. Creel should find room to run, and Missouri State will struggle to stop him on early downs. But Myers is the kind of receiver who can keep his team in it for a while, and Lloyd will be in on a lot of tackles. I expect Jax State to pull away in the second half, after Clementine's Bears make it uncomfortable early.

Burl will hand out plates long after the final whistle. Clementine will take one, because she's polite and because it's brisket.

"It's good bark," she'll say.

"Told you," Burl will say. "Come back next year and I'll make it better."

My call: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 32, Missouri State Bears 20.

display.fanatic_story:
Lem Coxwell has a campfire story about Middle Tennessee, and it starts in 1956. "Pull up a stump," he says. "The first time these two teams met, it was the first of December, and Sam Houston won 27-13. Then nobody saw each other for 35 years."

That's true, and it's on Sam Houston's own game page. The series between the Bearkats and the Blue Raiders is tied 2-2. Sam Houston won in 1956 and won 23-20 in 2023. Middle Tennessee won 20-19 in 1991 and 31-17 last November. Saturday's game at Bowers Stadium breaks the tie.

It's also Fan Appreciation Day and Senior Day in Huntsville, and Lem, Sam Houston's insider, says the fans have earned the thank-you more than usual this year.

"We're 1-9," he says, poking the fire. "Our folks kept coming. That's appreciation in both directions."

Middle Tennessee insider Opal Stonebriar is bringing a casserole dish to the visitors' section, because that's what she does. She hums "Blessed Assurance" when she's nervous, and she's been humming it since last Saturday.

"We lost 28-23 at Liberty," Opal says. "Liberty is 9-1, and we lost by five. I'm proud of those boys, and I'm nervous about this week, because a team that plays that hard on the road sometimes forgets to show up the next Saturday."

Opal's Blue Raiders are 5-5, and a sixth win would make them bowl eligible. They've been up and down. They lost 55-0 at Kansas in October, and they lost 44-28 at home to Kennesaw State. They've also beaten Delaware 33-30, won at FIU 26-23 and put up 51 on Western Kentucky on Nov. 7.

Roman Gagliano is the steady one. He's thrown for 2,101 yards with 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions. Antonio Martin leads the team with 750 rushing yards, and Cam'ron Lacy has 64 catches for 676 yards. Korey Smith is the tackling machine, with 96 stops.

"Roman takes care of the ball like it's my grandmother's china," Opal says. "Nobody touches the good dishes."

Lem's Bearkats have had a hard fall. They opened with a 24-21 loss at Troy and a 23-17 loss to Tulsa, two games that could have gone either way. They beat Nicholls 59-0. Then they lost seven straight, and they scored three points in three of those games.

"The fire's been low," Lem says. "But it's not out. You blow on the coals and it comes back."

Sam Houston's quarterback is the one doing the blowing. He's thrown for 1,850 yards with 14 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he threw for more than 300 yards in each of the first three games. Chris Reed leads the receivers with 485 yards and five touchdowns. Josh Alexander-Felton has five sacks, and linebacker Dean Ford has 56 tackles.

"Our quarterback had it going in September," Lem says. "That's the one I'm hoping shows up for Senior Day."

The trouble for Sam Houston is points. The Bearkats score 16.5 a game. But Middle Tennessee gives up 30.7, and that's the opening Lem is counting on. Middle Tennessee has allowed at least 20 points in nine of its ten games, and 42 or more three times.

Opal won't argue the point about her defense. "We make it exciting," she says. "My pastor says excitement builds faith. Our defense has built a lot of faith this year."

The game, I think, comes down to whether Sam Houston can score enough to stay in it. The Bearkats played Tulsa and Troy within a touchdown early in the season, and Middle Tennessee's defense has given up points to almost everyone. Gagliano should move the ball, and Middle Tennessee should win. But a 1-9 home team on Senior Day, with the old series tied, has every reason to fight for four quarters.

Lem will tell the 1956 story one more time at halftime, to anyone who stops by his fire. Opal will offer him a plate of casserole, and he'll take it.

"Good game," Lem will say. "That's three for you, two for us. We'll even it up next time."

"Bless you, Lem," Opal will say. "Bring a bigger stump."

My call: Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 27, Sam Houston Bearkats 24.

Start with the seven points. Illinois is 6-4 and had won four straight before a 22-14 loss at UCLA on a Friday night. The Illini beat Oregon 21-10 and Nebraska 24-13 at home. Katin Houser has 2,131 passing yards and 18 touchdowns, and Collin Dixon has 72 catches for 946 yards and 13 touchdowns. Margery Vandermolen ran it through her slide rule: "One bad night in Pasadena. Three interceptions. It won't repeat."

Iowa is the better team. It's 8-2, ranked No. 15, and coming off wins of 30-0, 24-10 and 28-7. But the Hawkeyes' offense is modest. Hank Brown has 1,504 passing yards, ten touchdowns and four interceptions, and Iowa scored 16 against Iowa State, 20 at Michigan and 10 at Minnesota. Orrin Kalvelage says that's how Iowa likes it: "We win with defense and punting." That style keeps games close, and seven points is a lot to give against a home team that scores 27.0 a game.

Now the Over. My final is Iowa Hawkeyes 25, Illinois Fighting Illini 19, and those 44 combined points clear 42.5 by a point and a half. Illinois gets two touchdowns from Houser and Dixon, and Iowa's offense has scored 24 or more in each of its last three. It's tight, but the number has come down far enough.

The room likes the points. The Formula likes Illinois +7 and likes the Over 42.5 at 25-21. Next Man Up likes Illinois +7 and likes the Under 42.5 at 22-18. Next Man Up: "Forty points total. Iowa doesn't play Overs."

The Formula: "Dixon scores. Iowa scores. That's enough for 46."

Letdown Watch: "Illinois just lost in Pasadena. Senior Day won't fix that."

Bret Bielema played at Iowa, and he knows this kind of game better than anyone. His team keeps it within a touchdown.

display.fanatic_story:
Bret Bielema walked on at Iowa, earned a scholarship and ended up a co-captain up front on the Hawkeyes' defense. On Saturday, he'll stand on the Illinois sideline at Gies Memorial Stadium for Senior Day and try to beat the program that made him. Illinois insider Margery Vandermolen has done the math on that with her slide rule, and she likes the answer.

"A coach who knows the opponent from the inside," she says. "That's not a disadvantage. That's a calculation. Oskee-wow-wow!"

Iowa insider Orrin Kalvelage has a simpler response. "He knows us," Orrin says. "He also knows what we do to people in November."

That's a fair warning. Iowa is 8-2 and ranked No. 15, and the Hawkeyes have won three straight, 30-0 over Wisconsin, 24-10 at Northwestern and 28-7 over Purdue. The defense allows 11.7 points a game, and it has three shutouts this season. Linebacker Cam Buffington has 90 tackles, and Joseph Anderson has four sacks.

"Our defense doesn't give up points," Orrin says. "It gives up hope."

Orrin's best-loved part of any game, though, isn't the defense. It's the punt. He keeps a notebook of every Iowa punt that's downed inside the 10, and he'll tell you about each one in detail. He's also the first one on his feet at the end of the first quarter at home, when Kinnick turns to wave at the children's hospital. He'll miss that on Saturday, and he says so.

"You can't take the Wave on the road," he says. "But you can take the punter."

Iowa's offense is steady rather than flashy. Hank Brown has thrown for 1,504 yards with ten touchdowns and four interceptions. Kamari Moulton leads the backfield with 541 rushing yards, and Tony Diaz has 549 receiving yards. The Hawkeyes beat Michigan 20-19 on the road and Iowa State 16-13 at home. Their two losses were to Ohio State and at Minnesota, 13-10.

Margery's Illini are 6-4, and they're coming off a hard week. They had won four straight, including a 21-10 win over Oregon and a 24-13 win over Nebraska. Then they went to the Rose Bowl on Friday night, Nov. 13, and lost 22-14 to UCLA. Katin Houser threw three interceptions that night.

"One bad night in Pasadena," Margery says. "Statistically insignificant. Katin Houser has 18 touchdown passes. Collin Dixon has 13 touchdown catches. Those numbers have a very small margin of error."

She's right about Dixon. The receiver has 72 catches for 946 yards and 13 touchdowns, and he's the biggest threat on the field Saturday. Houser has thrown for 2,131 yards. Aidan Laughery leads Illinois with 664 rushing yards, and defensive back Matthew Bailey has 74 tackles.

The trouble is the history. Iowa has won seven of the last eight meetings. Illinois' only win in that stretch came in 2022, 9-6, and the most recent meeting, in 2023, went to Iowa 15-13. Iowa games against Illinois tend to look like a slide-rule problem, low numbers carefully worked out.

"Nine to six," Margery says. "Beautiful game. Elegant. I wouldn't change a thing."

"You wouldn't," Orrin says. "You won it."

So the question for Saturday is whether Dixon can find enough space against an Iowa defense that hasn't given up more than 31 points all season, and only did that once. Iowa's offense won't run away from anyone. It doesn't have to. If the Hawkeyes punt well, play defense and don't turn the ball over, they win a lot of low-scoring games.

I think Illinois makes it close. Houser and Dixon will get their touchdowns. Bielema will have his team ready for an opponent he knows better than anyone in Champaign. And the Senior Day crowd will be loud, with the Illini needing a bounce back after Pasadena. But Iowa's defense has been the best group in this game all season, and the Hawkeyes are good at winning the kind of game they want to play.

Margery will slide her rule back and forth after the final whistle and come up with a reason it was closer than it looked. Orrin will open his notebook and add another punt.

"Oskee-wow-wow," Margery will say, a little quieter.

"Downed at the 6," Orrin will say. "Beautiful."

My call: Iowa Hawkeyes 25, Illinois Fighting Illini 19.

My USF vs FAU pick is South Florida Bulls −1.5 with the Under 65.5, and my final is South Florida Bulls 33, Florida Atlantic Owls 29, kickoff 2:30 PM ET at Flagler Credit Union Stadium, where the Owls close their home schedule in red.

Kaia Brightwater has been waiting all week to say it. "We are unbeaten in Paradise. Five home games, five wins. Caden Veltkamp has 3,086 yards and 29 touchdowns, Easton Messer has 1,033 receiving yards, and you want me to worry about a team that just gave up 52 to Memphis?"

The market moved toward Tampa. DraftKings opened Florida Atlantic −1.5 with the total at 69.5, as shown in ESPN pickcenter, and it now sits at South Florida −1.5 and 65.5. That is a three-point swing across the zero, and I agree with it. USF allows 18.8 points a game, the best defense on this field by a lot. FAU allows 35.3. When Veltkamp has to throw 58 times, as he did in the 21-38 loss at Tulsa, the Owls stop being a home-run team and start being a long-afternoon team.

Kromenhoek is the quarterback to price. He has taken the most throws in each of the last three USF games, and he threw for 271 and three scores against Memphis without an interception. D.J. Crowther gives the Bulls 689 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, which matters against a defense that bleeds points.

display.fanatic_story:
Boca Raton puts falling snow on Mizner Park Saturday night, and before that the South Florida Bulls vs Florida Atlantic Owls game turns Flagler Credit Union Stadium red for the last home date of the year. Kaia Brightwater wants the Owls to go out of Paradise unbeaten; Reina Valdés-Kowalski drove across the state to ruin the whole holiday mood.

"Red Out, Senior Day, Owls Giving Back Day," Kaia says, counting on her fingers like she is reading a surf report. "Then we walk downtown, the mayor lights a 40-foot tree at 7:30, and fifty thousand lights come on in the palm trees. That is the schedule. You are not on it."

"I am the first item on it," Reina says. "Two-thirty kickoff. I will be done by sunset and still make the snow."

Here is what makes this one fun. Both teams walk in at 6-4, both already bowl-eligible, and they do football in completely different languages. Florida Atlantic, under Zach Kittley, plays like the ocean is chasing it. Caden Veltkamp has 3,086 throwing yards and 29 touchdowns with just 6 interceptions. Easton Messer has 86 catches for 1,033 yards and 13 scores, and he is the guy Kaia names before she names her own family. The Owls score 38.3 points a game. They hung 60 on UTSA and 66 on Texas Southern, and they survived Rice 51-49 in a game Kaia still describes with her hands.

"Five home games, five wins," she says. "Navy, FIU, Texas Southern, Rice, UTSA. Nobody leaves Paradise happy."

Reina lets her finish, because Reina has a defense and Kaia does not. South Florida gives up 18.8 points a game. Florida Atlantic gives up 35.3. That difference is the whole argument from the Tampa side, and Reina makes it in one breath.

"You gave up 38 at Tulsa last week and your quarterback had to throw 58 times. Fifty-eight, Kaia. That is not an offense. That is a cry for help."

"That was a road game in the cold," Kaia says, which is a very Boca thing to say about Oklahoma in November.

The Bulls changed shape this fall. Michael Van Buren Jr. started the year as the man with the ball, and he still leads the team with 1,273 throwing yards. But Luke Kromenhoek has thrown the most in each of the last three games, and against Memphis he did a little of everything: 271 yards and three touchdowns through the air, then 30 carries for 146 yards and another score on the ground. Mudia Reuben caught two of those touchdowns. South Florida still lost 52-41, and Reina has not forgiven the Memphis secondary or the weather or whoever scheduled it.

"Kromenhoek runs like he is late for a boat show," she says. "And D.J. Crowther has 689 yards and seven touchdowns, and he is going to find out how many of your tacklers came to the game in sandals."

Kaia answers with the one name that keeps her up at night. C.J. Hicks has five sacks for the Bulls, and Veltkamp has to hold the ball long enough for Messer to break free. If Hicks gets home early, Paradise gets very quiet. If Veltkamp gets time, FAU can score from anywhere on the field, and Kaia will be on her feet for every snap until the fourth quarter ends.

The history does not help her much. Florida Atlantic crushed South Florida 56-14 in 2023, a game Kaia keeps a photo of. Then the Bulls won 44-21 in 2024 and 48-13 last October. This is only the eighth meeting ever, and the Owls are still chasing their third win in the series.

"Third win comes Saturday," Kaia says. "In red. On Senior Day. In front of the seniors who lost to you last year. That is a story."

"That is a wish," Reina says. "I came for the tree."

Here is how it goes. Veltkamp and Messer get their points, because they always do, and the student section turns the red up to full volume after an early touchdown. But the Bulls keep handing the ball to Crowther and Kromenhoek and keep the Owls offense standing on the sideline in the sun. Hicks gets one big sack in the third quarter. FAU answers late and Paradise roars, but South Florida runs out the last few minutes on the ground, and Reina gets to Mizner Park just in time to watch the snow fall on Kaia.

"It is fake snow," Kaia says.

"It is a real win," Reina says.

My call: South Florida Bulls 33, Florida Atlantic Owls 29.

The fiddles come out at the Jones House on Thursday night, and by Saturday Boone is ready to send its seniors off at Kidd Brewer Stadium. My UL Monroe vs App State pick is UL Monroe Warhawks +14 with the Over 50.5, and my final is App State Mountaineers 32, UL Monroe Warhawks 19, kickoff 2:30 PM ET on Senior Day.

Zeb Coldiron tells it slow, the way the old-time players tune up. "We've won five of the six meetings with Monroe since 2016. Jaquari Lewis ran for 137 at Marshall last week. Malachi Singleton has 2,287 throwing yards. Caleb Sandstrom has seven sacks. It's Senior Day, Darnell. Nobody in Boone is losing this one."

Darnell Vidrine has heard that before, usually around three in the morning on his own radio show. "Both of our wins came on the road, Zeb. We went to Troy and won 21-14. We went to Jonesboro and won 19-17. Noah Flemmings has 89 tackles. We like your mountain better than our couch."

Here is the case for the points. Two touchdowns is a lot to ask from an App State team that scores 25.7 a game and has scored 3 points twice this year, against Old Dominion and at Georgia Southern. The Mountaineers are 3-2 at home and lost the last one 39-23 to Georgia State. Singleton has 11 touchdowns and 7 interceptions, and the 20-16 win at Marshall came with 131 throwing yards. That is not an offense that buries people.

The market nudged a half point the other way. DraftKings opened App State −13.5 and now deals −14. I'll take the extra half. UL Monroe has lost by 28 to Florida Atlantic and by 21 to Louisiana, so the blowout risk is real. But my 32-19 has App State winning by 13, and that's still one short of the number.

The Over is the matchup that keeps this honest. UL Monroe allows 35.5 points a game, and App State should get its 30-plus. The Warhawks have scored 20 or more in six games, and Bryson Roland ran for 111 against Louisiana. My 51 clears the 50.5 by half a point, the same DraftKings number that opened the week.

The room mostly sides with the visitors. The Formula has App State 33, UL Monroe 19, takes UL Monroe +14 and goes Over 50.5. Letdown Watch lands on the exact same 32-19 I have, with UL Monroe +14 and the Over. In The Trenches has App State 31, UL Monroe 21, likes UL Monroe +14, and has no total pick. Next Man Up is the holdout at App State 33, UL Monroe 17, laying the 14 and taking the Under. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Next Man Up wants a three-score Senior Day from a team that scored three against Old Dominion. Bold."

Next Man Up: "Bold is copying the Cover Writer's homework and calling it a read, Letdown Watch."

The banjo stops around closing time Thursday. The seniors get their walk Saturday. The question is whether App State can turn a farewell into a rout.

display.fanatic_story:
Thursday night at the Jones House in downtown Boone, somebody will tune a fiddle, somebody will pull a banjo out of its case, and the old-time jam will run until the last call for tunes. Two days later the UL Monroe Warhawks vs App State Mountaineers game turns Kidd Brewer Stadium into a Senior Day farewell, and Zeb Coldiron and Darnell Vidrine have very different ideas about who gets to play the closing song.

Zeb is in no hurry. Zeb is never in a hurry. He talks about this App State season the way he talks about a long hike: steady going, a couple of hard climbs, then a view.

"We started 3-0," he says. "Maine, a road win at East Carolina, Charlotte. Then the climb got steep. Lost at NC State. Lost to Old Dominion at home, 10-3, on Homecoming. That one still stings. Then we won at Coastal, beat James Madison in overtime, and I had to sit down on a rock for a while."

"You lost to Georgia State at home two weeks ago," Darnell says. "Thirty-nine points. On Heroes Day."

"I'm getting there," Zeb says. "That's the part of the trail with the mud. But we went to Huntington last week and beat Marshall 20-16, and Jaquari Lewis ran for 137 yards. The view is coming back."

Darnell hosts the overnight sports show back home, and he is the most hopeful man who has ever answered the phone at three in the morning. His Warhawks are 2-8. He knows it. He also knows exactly where the two wins came from, and he will tell you before you ask.

"Troy," he says. "On the road. Twenty-one to fourteen. Then Arkansas State, on the road, nineteen to seventeen. Zeb, we like other people's stadiums. We are the best guests in the Sun Belt."

There is something to it. UL Monroe has been rough at home, including that 42-21 loss to Louisiana last week in the in-state game Darnell will not discuss before sunrise. But on the road the Warhawks have been scrappy, and the reason is a defense led by Noah Flemmings, who has 89 tackles, and Kevontay Wells, who has four sacks. Aidan Armenta has thrown for 1,483 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Austin Carlisle runs the ball as a second quarterback with 465 yards. Bryson Roland gave the Louisiana defense 111 rushing yards to think about.

Zeb answers with the people Boone will be cheering for when the seniors walk out. Malachi Singleton has thrown for 2,287 yards, with 11 touchdowns. Sam Pickett III has 679 receiving yards and caught five balls for 89 at Marshall. Lewis has eight rushing touchdowns. And on defense the Mountaineers have Caleb Sandstrom, with seven sacks, and Colton Phares, with 81 tackles.

"Sandstrom against your quarterback is the whole afternoon," Zeb says. "He's going to be in that backfield more than your center."

"Armenta has been hit before," Darnell says. "He gets up. Monroe people get up. That's what we do."

The history is mostly Zeb's. App State has won five of the six meetings since 2016, including a 59-28 game in 2021 and a 52-7 game in 2019. But Darnell has his one, and he wears it like a church pin: the 2017 game, when UL Monroe went into Boone and won 52-45. The last meeting, in 2023, went to App State by a single point, 41-40.

"One point," Darnell says. "One more snap and that's a whole different conversation."

"It was one point," Zeb says, "and I say this as a man who hikes: the top of the hill counts the same no matter how hard you breathed getting there."

Senior Day changes the air in Boone. The stadium sits up in the mountains, the crowd knows every name being read, and the players who stayed through all of it get one more walk on that field before App State heads to South Alabama for the regular-season finale. Zeb gets a little quiet when he thinks about it. Darnell, to his credit, takes his hat off when the seniors are announced, because he is a gentleman even at 2-8.

Here is how it plays. App State runs Lewis early and often, and the home crowd gets loud when Singleton finds Pickett deep in the first half. Sandstrom gets a sack that makes the student section bounce. But UL Monroe does not fold the way people expect. Roland keeps finding cutback lanes, Carlisle steals a few first downs with his legs, and Flemmings makes tackle after tackle to keep the Warhawks within shouting distance. The Mountaineers pull away in the fourth quarter and the seniors get their win, while Darnell drives home talking into a recorder about how close it was.

Thursday's jam ends with a last tune. Saturday's ends with a happy mountain.

My call: App State Mountaineers 32, UL Monroe Warhawks 19.

Downtown Lafayette spends the weekend at the movies, with the Southern Screen Festival running through Sunday, and Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium gets the closing reel on Saturday. For Coastal Carolina vs Louisiana I'm laying it with the home team, Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns −10.5, and riding the Under 51.5 to a projected Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 31, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 19 when the seniors take the field at 3:00 PM ET.

Mimi Fontenot reads the script like she wrote it. "Five home games, five wins. Lunch Winfield has run for 604 yards and 10 touchdowns. We beat South Alabama 28-26 and Troy 33-6 in this building. Goldie, this is the part of the movie where the hero walks off into the sunset."

Goldie Seabrook is unbothered. "Deuce Bailey went 21 of 24 last week. Marcellius Pulliam has 104 tackles. We won at Marshall and we won at Georgia State. And we beat you twice in the four meetings since 2016, Mimi. Sequels are a thing."

Here is why I lay the 10.5. Louisiana's offense is built around Winfield's legs, and Coastal's issue is that it gives up yards in bunches when it falls behind. The Chanticleers are 4-6 and lost three games by a touchdown or less, but they also scored 8 against Old Dominion and threw three interceptions doing it. Bailey has 9 interceptions on the year. Louisiana's defense allows 21.7 a game and has Jake St. Andre with 83 tackles to clean up anything Bailey leaves on the field.

The market agrees and then some. DraftKings opened Louisiana −7.5 and now deals −10.5, a full field goal of movement in the Cajuns' direction. I don't love chasing a number, but my 31-19 has Louisiana winning by 12, and that's clear of the 10.5.

The Under is the cleaner call. Four of Louisiana's five home games stayed under 51.5 points, and only the 28-26 South Alabama game went past it. The Cajuns like to run, and a team that runs holds the ball. Winfield threw only 13 times in the 42-21 win at UL Monroe, and Steven Blanco carried 15 times for 113 yards. Coastal's best defensive player, Ibrahim Diawara, has six sacks and will make Winfield earn every throw. My 50 lands under the 51.5.

The room is almost unanimous on the Under and mostly with Louisiana. Next Man Up has Louisiana 30, Coastal Carolina 18, lays the 10.5 and likes the Under. display.fanatic_story:
Lafayette has movie people in town all weekend, with the Southern Screen Festival filling downtown with screenings, panels and late-night music from Thursday through Sunday. On Saturday afternoon the Coastal Carolina Chanticleers vs Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns game takes over Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium for Senior Day, and Mimi Fontenot has already decided the home team gets the happy ending while Goldie Seabrook keeps insisting on a twist.

"Southern Screen says come dance a two-step and eat well," Mimi says. "That is not a festival slogan. That is how we play football. We run, we hit, we dance, we eat. In that order."

Goldie, who writes poems about blocking schemes and means every verse she has ever made, just smiles. She came from the coast, where the turf is teal and the wind off the water teaches you to keep your feet.

"Your festival has films with plot twists," Goldie says. "So do we. Coastal Carolina is the twist."

The Cajuns have made this a very good fall. Louisiana is 7-3 and has not lost at home: Lamar, UAB, Arkansas State, Troy, South Alabama, five for five. The heart of it is Lunch Winfield, the quarterback who runs like the ball owes him money. He has 604 rushing yards and 10 rushing touchdowns, plus 1,664 throwing yards. Last week at UL Monroe he barely had to throw at all, because Steven Blanco carried 15 times for 113 yards in a 42-21 win.

"Lunch is the main course," Mimi says. "Blanco is the second plate. And Jake St. Andre has 83 tackles, which means your quarterback is going to meet him a lot."

That quarterback is Deuce Bailey, and Goldie lights up when she talks about him. Bailey has thrown for 2,386 yards and 20 touchdowns, and last week against Arkansas State he completed 21 of 24 in a 28-21 win. Colton Hinton is the deep target, with 452 yards. Marcellius Pulliam has 104 tackles at linebacker and Ibrahim Diawara has six sacks off the end.

"Diawara is the wave you don't see coming," Goldie says. "Lunch likes to run around. Diawara likes to catch people who run around."

"Diawara has never met Lunch," Mimi says. "Lunch has a way of making strangers fall down."

The honest part for Goldie is the record. Coastal is 4-6, and the losses have hurt in different ways. West Virginia, Georgia Southern and App State all won by a touchdown or less. Old Dominion beat them 21-8, and Bailey threw three interceptions in that one. But Coastal has also won on the road at Marshall and at Georgia State, and Goldie quotes those like scripture.

The history between these two is a real back-and-forth. Coastal won 30-28 in 2018 and 30-27 in 2020, the year both programs were roaring. Louisiana won 48-7 in 2019 and 34-24 in 2024. Two apiece since 2016.

"Two apiece," Goldie says. "Saturday is the tiebreaker. Every good festival has a closing-night surprise."

"Every good festival has a closing-night party," Mimi says. "It's going to be in our end zone."

Senior Day in Lafayette is its own kind of movie. The Cajuns close the home schedule, the families walk out with the seniors, and Cajun Field gets loud and a little teary at the same time. Mimi says she will not cry. Mimi cried at a trailer once.

Here's how it plays out. Louisiana runs early, Winfield keeping it outside the pocket and Blanco pounding inside, and the crowd counts every first down. Coastal stays close in the first half because Bailey is accurate and Hinton gets behind the secondary once for a big gain. Diawara gets one sack that brings the teal section to its feet. But Louisiana controls the second half the old-fashioned way, chewing clock and making Coastal's defense stay on the field until legs get heavy. St. Andre makes a fourth-down stop late, and that's the closing credits.

"See," Mimi says, "no twist."

"The twist is that I'm staying for the film after," Goldie says, and she means it.

My call: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 31, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 19.

The Delaware vs New Mexico State prediction here takes the points: New Mexico State Aggies +3.5 and the Under 53.5, with Delaware Blue Hens 27, New Mexico State Aggies 24 as the final for the 3:00 PM ET kickoff.

Hen Lofland comes armed with the box scores, as a First State historian should. "Nick Minicucci went 27 of 30 against FIU last week. He has 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya answers with a bag of roasted chile in one hand. "History says you're 1-4 on the road, Hen. Vanderbilt, Virginia, Middle Tennessee, Kennesaw State, all losses. James Jones has 1,090 rushing yards and ran for 150 at Missouri State. Come down to the valley and see how far your throws carry."

That road number is my starting point. Delaware's one road win came at Western Kentucky; the other four trips ended in losses, and three of them were by single digits. A road favorite flying across the country to a Senior Day crowd is not a team I want to lay points with. New Mexico State is 3-7 and has lost three straight, but Jones is the best runner on the field and the Aggies can shorten a game by handing him the ball 25 times.

The market drifted toward the home side. DraftKings opened Delaware −4.5 and now sits at −3.5, with the total unmoved at 53.5. My 27-24 has Delaware winning by three, which keeps New Mexico State inside the hook.

But the Blue Hens scored 3 at Virginia and 14 against Liberty. My 51 stays under 53.5.

The room is with New Mexico State across the board. The Formula and Letdown Watch both have Delaware 27, New Mexico State 24, both take New Mexico State +3.5, and both go Under 53.5. display.fanatic_story:
Las Cruces does its holiday shopping by the mouthful this weekend. HomeGrown, the twelfth annual New Mexico food show and gift market, fills the Farm and Ranch Heritage Museum on Saturday morning with salsas, pecans and chile, and by early afternoon the Delaware Blue Hens vs New Mexico State Aggies game kicks off at Aggie Memorial Stadium on Senior Day, with Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya and Hen Lofland ready to argue about everything from defense to dessert.

Esperanza has the morning planned down to the minute. She will be at the museum gate at nine, among the first hundred cars so she gets the free shopping bag, and she will fill it with jars from J.P.M.'s Salsa of Las Cruces and pecans from Worthington Pecan Farm before she ever thinks about parking at the stadium.

"You eat with us before you lose to us," she tells Hen. "That is valley hospitality."

Hen Lofland, who can recite the date Delaware ratified the Constitution faster than most people can say hello, accepts the snack and none of the premise. "We came to New Mexico for a road win, Esperanza. The salsa is a bonus."

The Blue Hens have earned some swagger. Delaware is 5-5 in its new life in the top level of college football, and Nick Minicucci has become a quarterback people circle on their calendar. He has thrown for 2,115 yards with 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions, and last week against FIU he completed 27 of his 30 throws in a 24-16 win. Sean Wilson has 54 catches for 717 yards. When Minicucci gets going, he gets going in a hurry: 414 yards at Western Kentucky, 408 at Kennesaw State, five touchdowns against Missouri State.

"Delaware was the first state," Hen says. "Minicucci intends to be first down the field."

Esperanza has a rebuttal, and his name is James Jones. The New Mexico State running back has 1,090 rushing yards on 179 carries, and he ran 25 times for 150 yards last week at Missouri State in an overtime loss that still makes her put her fork down. The Aggies are 3-7 and they have lost three in a row. But they beat Western Kentucky 34-13 in this stadium, and they won at Sam Houston, and Esperanza believes Jones can carry a team the way her grandmother carried a tray of tamales: steadily, and without dropping anything.

"Twenty-five carries," she says. "Thirty if he wants. Your defense will need a nap by the third quarter."

Delaware does have people who tackle. Blake Matthews leads the Blue Hens with five sacks, and Gavin Moul has 72 tackles at linebacker. New Mexico State answers with Gabe Peterson, who has five and a half sacks, and Tory Gethers, who has 75 tackles. The quarterback question on the Aggies' side is a little cloudier. Trey Hedden has thrown the most in each of the last two games, and he has 9 touchdowns against 10 interceptions this season, so Esperanza wants the ball in Jones's hands and Hedden throwing only when he has to.

There's also the travel. Delaware has been a tough out at home and a different team on the road, 1-4 away from Newark, with losses at Vanderbilt, Virginia, Middle Tennessee and Kennesaw State. The Kennesaw game was a 42-40 heartbreaker. The Middle Tennessee game was 33-30. Hen calls those games "close," which is the historian's word for "painful."

"You've never played in this valley," Esperanza says. "The light is different. The air is different. The chile is definitely different."

"I'll adjust," Hen says. "Delaware adjusts. We've been adjusting since 1787."

Senior Day gives the home crowd a reason to stay loud, and the conference has also marked Saturday for mental health awareness, which matters to Esperanza more than she lets on. She wants every player on that field, in crimson or in blue, to walk off knowing people care how they are doing, not just how they played.

Here's how it goes. Jones runs hard from the first snap, and the Aggies hold the ball long enough to frustrate Minicucci on the sideline. Delaware strikes back with two quick drives, Wilson making a pair of big catches. New Mexico State keeps it close behind Peterson and Gethers, and the crowd gets very loud in the fourth quarter with a chance to win it. Minicucci makes one more good throw at the end, and Delaware escapes by three.

Esperanza hands Hen a jar of salsa anyway. "For the flight," she says.

"I'll save it for the rematch," Hen says.

My call: Delaware Blue Hens 27, New Mexico State Aggies 24.

display.story_text:
At one moment on Saturday, Kennesaw State will ask every veteran and active-duty service member in the stands to rise and be recognized by Owl Nation. That's the Salute to Service game against FIU, the Owls' last home date, and it is the backdrop for a Florida International vs Kennesaw State pick I like more than the number suggests: Kennesaw State Owls −3.5, Under 44.5, Kennesaw State Owls 24, Florida International Panthers 19 at 3:00 PM ET.

Kennesaw State closes its home schedule Saturday with a Salute to Service game, and the Florida International Panthers vs Kennesaw State Owls matchup at Walens Family Field will stop at one point so every veteran and active-duty service member in the stands can stand and be recognized. Ximena Holcombe-Reyes wants the Owls to send the seniors out on a four-game run; Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate drove up from Miami with a cooler, a flag and a plan to spoil it.

"Senior Tribute, Salute to Service, final home game," Ximena says, scrolling through the game-day notes on her phone. "Operation Hat Trick is giving recognition boxes to nominated veterans. Vet Tix donors are in a drawing for two field passes. This is a big day for our community, Lourdes. I'm just letting you know before it happens."

"Miami honors its veterans too," Lourdes says. "We will stand up with everybody Saturday, and then we will sit down and yell at your quarterback. Both things are allowed."

Ximena loves this program because it is still being built in front of her. Kennesaw State is new to this level, and the early part of 2026 was a lesson. The Owls lost six straight after the opener, including a 27-26 game against Jacksonville State, a 24-21 game at Missouri State and a 17-14 game at Arkansas State. Close, close, close. Then something clicked. They went to Murfreesboro and put 44 on Middle Tennessee. They beat Delaware 42-40 at home on Homecoming. Last Saturday they went to Huntsville, Texas, and beat Sam Houston 26-7.

"Three straight," Ximena says. "Landon Varnes has thrown the most in both of the last two, and he looks like he owns the place. Boogie Woods ran for 101 at Sam Houston. And Ugonna Nwoha has five and a half sacks, which means your quarterback is going to have company."

That quarterback is JJ Kohl, and Lourdes will defend him until the sun goes down. Kohl has thrown for 2,348 yards this year. He threw for 367 against Buffalo and 313 last week at Delaware. The receiver he looks for first is Maguire Anderson, who has 53 catches for 732 yards and caught nine balls for 122 in Newark.

"Kohl throws it like he is angry at the air," Lourdes says. "Anderson catches it like it's a family heirloom. And Devonte Lyons runs for 706 yards and you never see him coming."

The thing Lourdes does not love talking about is the road. FIU is 4-6, and all four wins came at home. Away from Miami, the Panthers lost at South Florida, at Florida Atlantic, at Jacksonville State, at Liberty and at Delaware. Some of those were close, like 27-24 in Jacksonville, Alabama. One was not, the 49-10 night at Liberty that she refers to only as "the Lynchburg thing."

"This time is different," she says. "DeeJay Holmes Jr. has seven sacks. Seven! Your quarterback has never seen him. DeAndre Boykins is going to be everywhere in that secondary."

Ximena has a defender to brag about too. Tywon Christopher leads the Owls with 74 tackles, and he has been the steady voice of a defense that held Sam Houston to a single touchdown. And she has history on her side. Kennesaw State has beaten FIU both times these programs have met, 27-26 in 2024 and 45-26 last year.

"One point and then nineteen," Ximena says. "We're trending."

"You're counting," Lourdes says. "Counting isn't trending."

There is a particular kind of quiet that settles over a stadium during a military recognition, and both of them will take their hats off for it. Then the noise comes back, louder, the way it always does, because the people being honored would want it that way.

Here is how the afternoon goes. Holmes gets to Varnes early and the FIU sideline erupts, and Kohl hits Anderson on a long throw to make it a game. But the Owls answer with Woods running downhill behind a front that has been getting better every week. Nwoha gets a sack on a third down in the second half that sends the student section into a frenzy. FIU keeps pushing into the fourth quarter, but Christopher makes the stop that matters, and the Kennesaw State seniors get to wave goodbye with a fourth straight win.

Lourdes packs up her cooler. "Your fans are polite," she says. "I will give you that."

"Come back next year," Ximena says. "We'll be bigger."

My call: Kennesaw State Owls 24, Florida International Panthers 19.

display.fanatic_story:
Lane Kiffin coached exactly one season at Tennessee, 2009, and on Saturday the LSU Tigers vs Tennessee Volunteers game brings him back to Neyland Stadium as the man running LSU. It is also Senior Day in Knoxville, the Vol Navy will be tied up along the Tennessee River from noon, and Earl "Rocky Top" Haskew and Cece Thibodeaux have been arguing about it since the schedule came out.

Earl opens with a banjo roll, as always, then sets the instrument across his knees like a man about to tell a long story.

"He's been back before," Earl says. "Came back with Alabama as a coordinator. Came back with Ole Miss. Every time, this place lets him know it hasn't forgotten. But here's the thing, Cece. Saturday isn't about him. Saturday is about our seniors and a team that controls its own path to the playoff."

Cece, who grew up between crawfish boils and film sessions in Baton Rouge, does not let him finish the sentence. "Saturday is about LSU being hungry. We had Texas beat. We led 21-10 in the second half and lost 22-21 on a throw in the final seconds. Do you know what that does to a team, Earl? It makes it mean."

Tennessee is 8-2, and the way the Vols win is not complicated. They run DeSean Bishop until the other team gets tired of tackling him. Bishop has 230 carries for 1,163 yards and 13 touchdowns, and he carried 34 times last week at Texas A&M in a 22-7 win that felt like a long, slow squeeze. George MacIntyre has thrown the most in each of the last six games, and his job is simple: hit Mike Matthews when the safeties creep up, and never give the ball away. MacIntyre threw only 17 times in College Station and completed 13.

"Rocky Top football," Earl says. "Run it, hit it, run it again. Tyree Weathersby has seven sacks. Arion Carter has 66 tackles. Our defense gives up 14.3 a game. Fourteen point three, Cece. You'll need a map to find the end zone."

Cece has her own map. LSU scores 35.5 a game, and Sam Leavitt is the reason. He has thrown for 2,797 yards and 19 touchdowns, including 388 yards at Auburn and 380 against Alabama. Jackson Harris has 55 catches for 864 yards and nine touchdowns. Dilin Jones has 838 rushing yards and ran for 125 against Texas. And on defense, Princewill Umanmielen has nine and a half sacks off the end.

"Umanmielen is going to introduce himself to MacIntyre early," Cece says. "And often. He's very polite. He just doesn't leave."

The worry for Cece is the turnovers. Leavitt threw three interceptions against Texas and three more against Louisiana Tech, and he has 12 for the year. In a stadium this loud on third down, a quarterback who forces throws can turn a close game into a long ride home.

"He'll be fine," she says. "He threw for 380 against Alabama. Loud doesn't scare him."

Earl strums a minor chord and gives her the history. Tennessee has won 21 of the 34 games in the series, against 10 LSU wins and 3 ties, going all the way back to a 0-0 tie in Knoxville in 1925. The Vols crushed LSU 40-13 in Baton Rouge the last time these two met, in 2022. But here's the part Earl hums quietly: the Vols have not beaten LSU in Neyland Stadium since 2001.

"Twenty-five years," Cece says. "Tell me again how the stadium remembers."

"The stadium remembers," Earl says. "It's just been patient."

Senior Day at Neyland is one of the great scenes in the sport, and Earl gets a little choked up talking about it, a whole class of players who stuck around to put Tennessee back in the playoff talk. Cece respects it. She will clap for those seniors. Then she will try to ruin their afternoon.

Here's how it plays out. LSU strikes first, Leavitt finding Harris on a deep ball that quiets the checkerboard end zones for a minute. Tennessee answers the only way it knows, with Bishop, again and again, until the Vols are inside the red zone and the crowd is thundering. Umanmielen gets a big sack that forces a field goal. The game swings back and forth through the third quarter, both defenses bending, both offenses landing punches. Late in the fourth, Weathersby gets home on third down, and the Vols take over with a chance to put it away. Bishop does the rest, and a field goal makes it a two-point game that LSU cannot quite get back.

Earl plays the first bars of Rocky Top. Cece puts her hands over her ears and smiles anyway.

"He'll be back," she says.

"We'll be here," Earl says.

My call: Tennessee Volunteers 26, LSU Tigers 24.

Creek Show has its last night on Saturday, ten light installations glowing along Waller Creek from 4th Street down to Lady Bird Lake, and Texas would love to have this one wrapped up before the first of them switches on. Arkansas vs Texas, my side and my over/under: Arkansas Razorbacks +20.5, Under 46.5, and a projected Texas Longhorns 33, Arkansas Razorbacks 13 at 3:30 PM ET in Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium.

Caro Whitfield runs the Longhorns like a portfolio, and she opens the ledger. "Five home wins in six. Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks. Jelani McDonald has 78 tackles. Our defense gives up 17.8 a game, and Arch Manning just walked into Baton Rouge and won 22-21. That's a blue-chip asset, Bubba."

Bubba Fayette-Dorsey calls the Hogs before he answers, then gets serious. "We just beat South Carolina 34-6. KJ Jackson threw two touchdowns. Chris Marshall has 761 receiving yards. We lost to Tennessee by seven and at Auburn by three. And in 2021 we put 40 on y'all in Fayetteville. Respect the hog."

I'll be honest about the risk on the points. Arkansas has lost by more than three touchdowns four times this year: Utah, Georgia, Texas A&M and Missouri. Twenty and a half is not a gift. But Texas has not been a blowout machine against good teams. The Longhorns beat Ohio State by one, Tennessee by three, Ole Miss by seven and LSU by one, and lost to Oklahoma and Florida by three each. Their three wins by more than 20 came against Texas State, UTSA and Mississippi State. Manning threw three interceptions last week. My 33-13 is a 20-point win, half a point shy of the number.

The market agrees with a little less. DraftKings opened Texas −21 with a 48.5 total, as shown in ESPN pickcenter, and the total has since dropped to 46.5.

The Under is where I feel best. Texas allows 17.8 points a game, and Simmons against the Arkansas front protecting Jackson is the matchup of the afternoon. Arkansas scored 7 at Texas A&M and 10 at Utah. Raleek Brown has 572 rushing yards and Texas will run the clock with a lead. My 46 lands just under the 46.5.

A few hours earlier and a short walk up the creek, the Arkansas Razorbacks vs Texas Longhorns game fills Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, and Caro Whitfield and Bubba Fayette-Dorsey are already arguing about which team gets to glow.

"Creek Show moved downstream this year," Caro says, sounding like a woman who reads the annual report. "First time on the new southern stretch, the Confluence, 4th Street to Lady Bird Lake. Ten installations. Tickets this year. Austin keeps growing, Bubba. So does this program."

Bubba wipes his glasses and lets out a short hog call, just enough to make the people near him jump. "Fayetteville has lights too," he says. "We just put ours on the field. And our boys are coming in hot."

He is not wrong about that. Arkansas is 4-6, but the Razorbacks just smashed South Carolina 34-6 behind KJ Jackson, who threw for 188 yards and two touchdowns. Chris Marshall caught one of them, and Marshall is the guy Bubba talks about at the dinner table: 52 catches, 761 yards, a receiver who makes contested balls look easy. Jackson has thrown for 2,041 yards this year, and he has thrown the most for Arkansas in every game this season.

"KJ is a grown man," Bubba says. "He took a beating at Utah and Texas A&M, and he got back up. Tennessee beat us by seven. Auburn beat us by three. We are not afraid of your big stadium."

Caro lets him finish, then gets to the part she likes. Texas is 8-2. The Longhorns beat Ohio State 24-23 in September, won at Tennessee 20-17 a week later, and last Saturday went into Baton Rouge and stole one, 22-21. Arch Manning has thrown for 2,198 yards and 19 touchdowns. Ryan Wingo leads the receivers with 591 yards. Raleek Brown has 572 rushing yards and six scores.

"And then there's Colin Simmons," Caro says, and she says the name the way some people say "blue-chip stock." Simmons has ten and a half sacks off the end. Jelani McDonald has 78 tackles in the secondary. Texas allows 17.8 points a game.

"Simmons is going to be in your backfield so often your center should charge him rent," she says.

"Our center charges everybody rent," Bubba says. "It's an Ozark thing."

Bubba's honest worry is the road. Arkansas is 1-3 away from home this season, and the trips to Utah and College Station were the kind of days a fan tries to forget. But he also has history he can hold up. In 2021, the Razorbacks beat Texas 40-21 in Fayetteville, and Bubba has the ticket stub framed in his classroom. Texas won the two meetings since, 20-10 in 2024 and 52-37 last year.

"That 52-37 game was a fireworks show," Caro says. "This one will be a light show. Different art form."

The Texas worry, quietly, is turnovers. Manning threw three interceptions at LSU and still won, and the Longhorns lost to Oklahoma and Florida by three points each this season. They have been close-game artists more than blowout specialists against good opponents. Caro does not love that. She would prefer a clean, profitable afternoon, a word she uses about football more than she should.

Here's how it unfolds. Texas opens with Brown running hard and Manning finding Wingo on a crossing route, and the stadium settles in for a long, happy day. Simmons gets a sack in the first quarter that sends the student section into a frenzy. Arkansas answers with Jackson hitting Marshall down the sideline, and Bubba lets loose a full hog call that turns several heads in burnt orange. The Hogs get a field goal or two more, but the Texas defense keeps them out of the end zone after that, and McDonald comes up with a big stop on fourth down. Texas wins comfortably, but Arkansas never quits, and Bubba drives home proud of that.

Down on Waller Creek, the lights come on for one last night. Caro goes to see them. Bubba goes too, because even a hog caller appreciates good art.

"Next year in Fayetteville," he says.

"Bring the lights," Caro says.

My call: Texas Longhorns 33, Arkansas Razorbacks 13.

display.fanatic_story:
Baylor and Texas Tech have played 83 times, and the Bears lead the whole thing by two games, 42-40-1. On Saturday the Texas Tech Red Raiders vs Baylor Bears game closes the home schedule at McLane Stadium with Senior Day, and Maggie Whitlock and Bodie Ratliff are treating it like the closing argument in a case nobody will ever finish.

Maggie has her house rules. She walks the stands at McLane like it's a showroom she just finished: the river out past the end zone, the gold everywhere, the seniors about to walk out for the last time.

"This is a remodel," she tells Bodie. "We had a coaching change this fall. Joe Klanderman stepped in as interim head coach, and he went and won at UCF and beat Iowa State in back-to-back weeks. That's how you renovate on the fly. You keep the bones and fix the kitchen."

Bodie, who rides bareback in the summer and charts Air Raid concepts the rest of the year, tips his hat. "Y'all lost 28-7 at BYU last week, Maggie. That kitchen's still got some sawdust in it."

Texas Tech is the team with the shine this fall. The Red Raiders are 9-1 and they won their first seven games. Their only loss came at Cincinnati in late October. Since then, Thomas Castellanos has thrown the most in each game, and the results have been loud: 362 yards and five touchdowns in a 53-48 win over West Virginia, then 263 yards and four touchdowns in a 52-27 win at Oklahoma State. J'Koby Williams has 1,078 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and he ran for 124 in Stillwater. Kenny Johnson leads the receivers with 707 yards.

"Castellanos throws it like he's roping a calf," Bodie says. "Quick, mean and right on target."

Maggie answers with the room she is proudest of, the defense. Baylor gives up 18.1 points a game. The Bears held TCU to 17 and Colorado to 13 and smothered UCF 41-9. Travion Barnes has 73 tackles at linebacker, and Garrick Ponder has four sacks off the end. And on offense, DJ Lagway has thrown 16 touchdowns with only five interceptions, while Gavin Freeman has caught 75 balls for 889 yards.

"Freeman is the crown molding," Maggie says. "Nobody notices him until you realize the whole room looks better because he's there."

The other storyline in this one has a Waco address. Joey McGuire, Tech's fifth-year head coach, used to be an assistant at Baylor. He knows the building. He knows the crowd. Bodie claims that's a home-field advantage for the Red Raiders. Maggie claims that's a man who should know better than to come back.

The history gives both of them material. Baylor has won five of the last seven meetings. Baylor also holds a 20-12 lead in games played in Waco. But Tech won the last time it came to town, 39-14 in 2023, and Bodie still keeps the box score folded in his truck's glove box. Baylor answered the next year with a 59-35 blowout in Lubbock that Maggie calls "a full gut job."

"Fifty-nine," she says. "On your homecoming. In your town."

"That was two years ago," Bodie says. "We've had a renovation too."

There is also a Salute to Service element on Saturday, with the Bears honoring active-duty military, veterans and first responders along with the seniors. Both of them stand for that part. Then Maggie sits down and gets back to work on Bodie.

Here's how it goes. Texas Tech gets the first punch, Castellanos finding Johnson on a quick slant that turns into a long gain and a touchdown, and the visiting section in the corner gets loud. Baylor settles in. Lagway lives on short throws to Freeman, the Bears grind out a couple of long drives, and the defense makes Castellanos throw it away twice in the second quarter. The game goes back and forth all afternoon. Holmes gets a big sack late, forcing a Baylor field goal instead of a touchdown, and that's the difference. Tech escapes, barely.

Maggie stands and applauds her seniors as they leave the field.

"Two points," Bodie says.

"Two points in a house this good is still a good house," Maggie says. "We'll fix the trim next year."

My call: Texas Tech Red Raiders 28, Baylor Bears 26.

Florida State has never worn turquoise in a real football game until Saturday. The Seminole Heritage uniforms come out for Homecoming against NC State at Doak Campbell Stadium, and the NC State vs Florida State spread gets my vote for the home team: Florida State Seminoles −9.5, Over 54.5, with Florida State Seminoles 33, NC State Wolfpack 23 at 3:30 PM ET.

Gianna Ravello works the room like it's the last week of session. "Rick Stockstill has been interim head coach for two games, and we've won both, 31-24 at Boston College and 16-10 at Pitt. One more and we're bowl eligible. Ousmane Kromah has 609 rushing yards. Rylan Kennedy has six sacks. The votes are counted, Ruff."

Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram lights the grill out of habit. "We've won six of the eight meetings since 2016, Gianna, including 21-11 last year. CJ Bailey has 2,289 throwing yards and only five interceptions. Jayden Scott ran for 127 against Syracuse. The Pack loves a road upset."

The road is where my side starts. NC State is 0-3 away from home this year, losing by 26 at Virginia, by four at Vanderbilt and by three at Stanford. The Wolfpack also got crushed 41-3 by Duke at home two weeks ago and then lost to Syracuse 34-31. The defense allows 28.2 points a game. Florida State's offense scores 29.2, and Ashton Daniels has thrown for 2,309 yards. My 33-23 is a 10-point win, half a point past the 9.5.

DraftKings opened Florida State −10 and the line has ticked down a half point to −9.5. The over/under opened and stays at 54.5.

The Over has the strongest numbers in this story. Seven of NC State's ten games have gone over 54.5, including 73-0 over Richmond, 41-31 over App State and 31-28 over Louisville. Six of Florida State's ten went over too. Daniels has 12 interceptions, and short fields add points for both sides. Micahi Danzy has 511 receiving yards and Keenan Jackson has six touchdown catches for NC State. My 56 clears the 54.5.

Most of the room is with the Seminoles on the side and the Over on the total, with a twist. The Formula has Florida State 32, NC State 22, lays the 9.5 but goes Under 54.5. Letdown Watch has Florida State 33, NC State 22, lays the 9.5 and goes Over. Next Man Up has Florida State 35, NC State 26, takes NC State +9.5 and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call on this one. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Nine points of margin is Florida State winning and the Pack still getting there late. That's college football in November."

The Formula: "And Under is me remembering a team that scored three against Duke. Somebody here has to keep receipts."

Stockstill was one of Bobby Bowden's first quarterbacks. Saturday he gets a turquoise Homecoming and a chance to make this a bowl team again.

display.fanatic_story:
Turquoise is coming to Doak Campbell Stadium. For the first time in program history, Florida State will wear turquoise uniforms in a real game, and the NC State Wolfpack vs Florida State Seminoles matchup is the Seminole Heritage game and Homecoming all at once, which has Gianna Ravello talking like she's whipping votes and Ruff Pegram talking like he brought his own tailgate tent into the capitol.

"Zae Thomas said it best," Gianna says. "He's a member of the Seminole Tribe, and he called turquoise a color with deep meaning. Our heritage games started in 2023, and we have never lost one. Three for three. Add Homecoming and FSU175. Ruff, this is the most important Saturday in Tallahassee since, well, since last week."

Ruff, who has never met a parking lot he could not turn into a barbecue, waves a pair of tongs. "We've beaten y'all six times in the last eight meetings, Gianna. Last year, 21-11. I don't care what color the jerseys are. I care what color the scoreboard is."

The Seminoles have had a fall that felt like three seasons stacked on top of each other. Florida State started 1-2, beat Central Arkansas and Virginia, then lost three straight, including an overtime heartbreak at Miami. On Nov. 1, the school made a leadership change and named Rick Stockstill interim head coach. Stockstill was one of Bobby Bowden's first quarterbacks, and the team has won both games since, 31-24 at Boston College and 16-10 at Pitt. The Seminoles are 5-5. One more win makes them bowl eligible.

"Coach Stockstill has these guys playing like they remember who they are," Gianna says. "Tough, simple and loud."

The engine is Ashton Daniels, who has thrown for 2,309 yards and 14 touchdowns. He threw for 377 at Alabama and 350 against Clemson. Ousmane Kromah leads the runners with 609 yards, and Micahi Danzy is the deep threat, with 511 receiving yards. On defense, Rylan Kennedy has six sacks and Chris Jones has 71 tackles.

Ruff answers with his own list, loud enough for three tailgates over. CJ Bailey has thrown for 2,289 yards with 14 touchdowns and just five interceptions. Jayden Scott ran for 127 yards against Syracuse last week. Keenan Jackson has six touchdown catches. Popo Aguirre has 84 tackles at linebacker, and Elijah Satchell has five sacks.

"Bailey doesn't throw it to the other team," Ruff says. "That's the whole game plan. Daniels has thrown twelve. We just have to be standing in the right place."

It's a fair shot, and Gianna knows it. Daniels has thrown 12 interceptions, including three against Alabama and three against Clemson. A Florida State team that hands the ball away is a team that has lost games it could have won.

But NC State has its own weight to carry. The Wolfpack are 4-6, and they have not won a road game this season: Virginia, Vanderbilt and Stanford all sent them home with losses. Two weeks ago Duke beat them 41-3 in Raleigh. Last week Syracuse won 34-31.

"The road has been rough," Ruff admits. "But you know what's rougher? Tallahassee in November thinking it already won."

The all-time series belongs to Florida State, 27-17, and the Seminoles are 16-6 at home against the Wolfpack. Ruff, of course, prefers the recent stuff, including the 47-28 win in 2018 that he describes in loving detail at every tailgate.

Here's how it goes. The turquoise comes out of the tunnel and Doak goes wild. Florida State scores early when Daniels hits Danzy deep. NC State answers with Scott running hard and Bailey moving the chains, and the Wolfpack section starts to believe. Kennedy gets a big sack before halftime that kills a Pack drive. In the second half, Kromah takes over, and the Seminoles pull away with two long scoring drives. Bailey gets one more late, but the Homecoming crowd gets what it came for: a bowl-eligible team in brand-new colors.

Ruff packs up his tongs. "Nice jerseys," he says. "Grill's still warm next year."

"Bring the grill back next year," Gianna says. "We'll still be in turquoise."

My call: Florida State Seminoles 33, NC State Wolfpack 23.

The Seminole Heritage uniforms come out for Homecoming against NC State at Doak Campbell Stadium, and the NC State vs Florida State spread gets my vote for the home team: Florida State Seminoles −9.5, Over 54.5, with Florida State Seminoles 33, NC State Wolfpack 23 at 3:30 PM ET.

Gianna Ravello works the room like it's the last week of session. "Rick Stockstill has been interim head coach for two games, and we've won both, 31-24 at Boston College and 16-10 at Pitt. One more and we're bowl eligible. Ousmane Kromah has 609 rushing yards. Rylan Kennedy has six sacks. The votes are counted, Ruff."

Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram lights the grill out of habit. "We've won six of the eight meetings since 2016, Gianna, including 21-11 last year. CJ Bailey has 2,289 throwing yards and only five interceptions. Jayden Scott ran for 127 against Syracuse. The Pack loves a road upset."

The road is where my side starts. NC State is 0-3 away from home this year, losing by 26 at Virginia, by four at Vanderbilt and by three at Stanford. The Wolfpack also got crushed 41-3 by Duke at home two weeks ago and then lost to Syracuse 34-31. The defense allows 28.2 points a game. Florida State's offense scores 29.2, and Ashton Daniels has thrown for 2,309 yards. My 33-23 is a 10-point win, half a point past the 9.5.

DraftKings opened Florida State −10 and the line has ticked down a half point to −9.5. The over/under opened and stays at 54.5.

The Over has the strongest numbers in this story. Seven of NC State's ten games have gone over 54.5, including 73-0 over Richmond, 41-31 over App State and 31-28 over Louisville. Six of Florida State's ten went over too. Daniels has 12 interceptions, and short fields add points for both sides. Micahi Danzy has 511 receiving yards and Keenan Jackson has six touchdown catches for NC State. My 56 clears the 54.5.

Most of the room is with the Seminoles on the side and the Over on the total, with a twist. The Formula has Florida State 32, NC State 22, lays the 9.5 but goes Under 54.5. Letdown Watch has Florida State 33, NC State 22, lays the 9.5 and goes Over. Next Man Up has Florida State 35, NC State 26, takes NC State +9.5 and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call on this one. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Nine points of margin is Florida State winning and the Pack still getting there late. That's college football in November."

The Formula: "And Under is me remembering a team that scored three against Duke. Somebody here has to keep receipts."

Stockstill was one of Bobby Bowden's first quarterbacks. Saturday he gets a turquoise Homecoming and a chance to make this a bowl team again.

Florida State Seminoles 33, NC State Wolfpack 23. Florida State Seminoles cover the 9.5. Over 54.5.

display.story_text:
Seventeen bells hang above the Kerrytown market in Ann Arbor, and on Saturday morning anyone can climb up and play them for half an hour before heading to Michigan Stadium. The UCLA vs Michigan spread sends me toward the home team in its final home game: Michigan Wolverines +3.5, Over 38.5, with UCLA Bruins 21, Michigan Wolverines 19 at 3:30 PM ET.

Kensington "Kenzie" Rhee has the season storyboarded. "Ten wins, no losses, first in the Big Ten. We gave up 14.1 points a game. Wayne Knight has 845 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. Ty Dieffenbach threw for 232 against Illinois. Act three, Gus. We're in act three."

Augustin "Gus" Hartwell taps the margin of his notes. "Kenzie, your offense scored 17 at Oregon, 17 against Wisconsin and 22 against Illinois. Our defense allows 17.7 a game. John Henry Daley has six sacks and Troy Bowles has 79 tackles. Close games are our whole personality."

That last part is the case for the points. Michigan has played seven home games, and five were decided by seven points or fewer: 13-12 over Western Michigan, 17-10 over Oklahoma, a 20-19 loss to Iowa, 21-18 over Penn State and a 13-6 overtime loss to Indiana. UCLA's 17-15 win at Oregon shows this team can win ugly on the road too, and ugly games tend to stay inside a field goal and a hook. My 21-19 puts the Bruins up two, inside the 3.5.

There's no hiding Michigan's offense. The Wolverines score 18.3 a game, Tommy Carr went 4 for 12 for 45 yards at Oregon, and Bryce Underwood has six interceptions. That's why my number sits so low. UCLA's defense has allowed 20 points or fewer in seven straight games.

The Over is the tighter call. DraftKings opened the total at 42.5, as shown in ESPN pickcenter, and it has dropped four points to 38.5. Only four of UCLA's ten games have gone over 38.5, and only four of Michigan's ten. My projection lands on 40, a point and a half above the 38.5, built on Knight's ground game and Savion Hiter's 107 rushing yards at Oregon.

The desks split three ways on the side. The Formula has UCLA 23, Michigan 21, takes Michigan +3.5 and likes the Over 38.5. Letdown Watch has UCLA 21, Michigan 20, likes Michigan +3.5 and goes Over. Next Man Up has UCLA 20, Michigan 15, lays the 3.5 with UCLA and likes the Under. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call on this one. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Unbeaten team, road trip, rivalry game for Michigan next week. Everybody's looking past somebody."

Next Man Up: "UCLA hasn't allowed more than 20 in seven straight games. I don't see 19 Michigan points in there."

Kerrytown's chime keeps more than two hundred songs written out by number. Michigan only needs one Saturday, the fight song after a close one.

UCLA Bruins 21, Michigan Wolverines 19. Michigan Wolverines cover the 3.5. Over 38.5.
